pu-01.statement: How many centimeters are in 6 meters?
hints: 1 meter = 100 centimeters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 100.

pu-02.statement: How many meters are in 300 centimeters?
hints: 100 centimeters = 1 meter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 100.

pu-03.statement: How many minutes are in 6 hours?
hints: 1 hour = 60 minutes: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 60.

pu-04.statement: How many hours are in 180 minutes?
hints: 60 minutes = 1 hour: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 60.

pu-05.statement: How many bani are in 4 lei?
hints: 1 leu = 100 bani: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 100.

pu-06.statement: How many lei are in 500 bani?
hints: 100 bani = 1 leu: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 100.

pu-07.statement: How many decimeters are in 3 meters?
hints: 1 meter = 10 decimeters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 10.

pu-08.statement: How many meters are in 70 decimeters?
hints: 10 decimeters = 1 meter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 10.

pu-09.statement: How many centimeters are in 4 decimeters?
hints: 1 decimeter = 10 centimeters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 10.

pu-10.statement: How many decimeters are in 50 centimeters?
hints: 10 centimeters = 1 decimeter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 10.

pu-11.statement: How many millimeters are in 7 centimeters?
hints: 1 centimeter = 10 millimeters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 10.

pu-12.statement: How many centimeters are in 50 millimeters?
hints: 10 millimeters = 1 centimeter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 10.

pu-13.statement: How many grams are in 6 kilograms?
hints: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 1000.

pu-14.statement: How many kilograms are in 5000 grams?
hints: 1000 grams = 1 kilogram: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 1000.

pu-15.statement: How many milliliters are in 8 liters?
hints: 1 liter = 1000 milliliters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 1000.

pu-16.statement: How many liters are in 2000 milliliters?
hints: 1000 milliliters = 1 liter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 1000.

pu-17.statement: How many deciliters are in 6 liters?
hints: 1 liter = 10 deciliters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 10.

pu-18.statement: How many liters are in 20 deciliters?
hints: 10 deciliters = 1 liter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 10.

pu-19.statement: How many centiliters are in 3 liters?
hints: 1 liter = 100 centiliters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 100.

pu-20.statement: How many liters are in 900 centiliters?
hints: 100 centiliters = 1 liter: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 100.

pu-21.statement: How many seconds are in 5 minutes?
hints: 1 minute = 60 seconds: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 60.

pu-22.statement: How many minutes are in 240 seconds?
hints: 60 seconds = 1 minute: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 60.

pu-23.statement: How many hours are in 2 days?
hints: 1 day = 24 hours: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 24.

pu-24.statement: How many days are in 96 hours?
hints: 24 hours = 1 day: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 24.

pu-25.statement: How many days are in 6 weeks?
hints: 1 week = 7 days: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 7.

pu-26.statement: How many weeks are in 35 days?
hints: 7 days = 1 week: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 7.

pu-27.statement: How many months are in 4 years?
hints: 1 year = 12 months: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 12.

pu-28.statement: How many years are in 24 months?
hints: 12 months = 1 year: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 12.

pu-29.statement: How many meters are in 4 kilometers?
hints: 1 kilometer = 1000 meters: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 1000.

pu-30.statement: How many kilometers are in 6000 meters?
hints: 1000 meters = 1 kilometer: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 1000.

pu-31.statement: How many kilograms are in 9 metric tons?
hints: 1 metric ton = 1000 kilograms: from the larger unit to the smaller one, you multiply by 1000.

pu-32.statement: How many metric tons are in 4000 kilograms?
hints: 1000 kilograms = 1 metric ton: from the smaller unit to the larger one, you divide by 1000.

pu-33.statement: How many centimeters are in 3 meters and 80 centimeters?
hints: First convert 3 meters to centimeters, then add 80 centimeters.

pu-34.statement: How many bani are in 4 lei and 25 bani?
hints: First convert 4 lei to bani, then add 25 bani.

pu-35.statement: How many minutes are in 3 hours and 23 minutes?
hints: First convert 3 hours to minutes, then add 23 minutes.

pu-36.statement: How many meters are in 2 kilometers and 565 meters?
hints: First convert 2 kilometers to meters, then add 565 meters.

pu-37.statement: How many grams are in 1 kilogram and 520 grams?
hints: First convert 1 kilogram to grams, then add 520 grams.

ms-01.statement: The bench is 6 hand spans long, and the table is 9 hand spans long, measured with the same hand. Which one is longer?
hints: With the same unit, more hand spans means longer.
solution: 9 hand spans are more than 6 hand spans ⇒ the table is longer.

ms-02.statement: A pencil is 3 paper clips long. How long are 2 pencils of the same kind, placed end to end? (in paper clips)
hints: Add the lengths.

ms-03.statement: Ana and her dad measure the same table in hand spans. Ana gets 10 hand spans, her dad gets 6 hand spans. Why?
hints: With a bigger unit you need fewer of them.
solution: Dad's hand is bigger, so it fits fewer times ⇒ 6 hand spans instead of 10.

ms-04.statement: A notebook is 4 erasers long, and a book is 7 erasers long. By how many erasers is the book longer?
hints: The difference of the lengths.

ms-05.statement: A step is about 50 cm. About how many steps long is a classroom that is 8 m long?
hints: 1 m is 100 cm, that is 2 steps of 50 cm.
solution: 2 steps of 50 cm fit in one meter; in 8 m: 8 × 2 = 16 steps.

ms-06.statement: What do you measure the length of a pencil with?
hints: Length is measured in centimeters.
solution: The ruler has the centimeters marked ⇒ with a ruler.

ms-07.statement: What unit do you use for the mass of a watermelon?
hints: How heavy is it?
solution: Mass is measured in kilograms (with a scale).

ms-08.statement: Which unit is suitable for the length of the road between two cities?
hints: The road is very long.
solution: Long distances are measured in kilometers.

ms-09.statement: How do you find out how much milk fits in a cup?
options: with a measuring jug, in milliliters
hints: Capacity is measured in liters and milliliters.
solution: You pour the milk into a measuring jug and read the milliliters.
Answer: with a measuring jug, in milliliters.

ms-10.statement: Which mass is suitable for a cat?
hints: Think about how heavy a bag of sugar is (1 kg).
solution: A cat weighs about as much as 4 bags of sugar ⇒ 4 kg. (A piece of candy weighs about 4 g, and a big truck about 4 t.)

ms-11.statement: How long is the orange segment?
hints: The segment starts at 0; read where it ends.
solution: The segment starts at 0 and ends at 7 ⇒ 7 cm.

ms-12.statement:
How long is the orange segment?
Careful: the segment does not start at 0.
hints: Length = where it ends − where it starts.
solution: The segment starts at 2 and ends at 9: 9 − 2 = 7 cm.

ms-13.statement: A segment is 8 cm long. Another one is 3 cm shorter. How long is the second segment?
hints: “Shorter by” means subtraction.

ms-14.statement: You want to draw a segment of 5 cm with a ruler. Between which marks do you draw it?
hints: Start at 0.
solution: From 0 to 5 is exactly 5 cm. (From 1 to 5 would be only 4 cm.)

ms-15.statement:
How many millimeters long is the orange segment?
Between two neighboring numbers on the ruler there is 1 cm = 10 mm.
hints: Count the whole centimeters, then the remaining millimeters.

ms-16.statement: How many centimeters are in 1 m?
hints: 1 m = 10 dm, and 1 dm = 10 cm.

ms-21.statement: How many whole kilometers are in 7500 m?
solution: 7 × 1000 = 7000 and 7500 − 7000 = 500 m are left ⇒ 7 whole kilometers (and 500 m).

ms-22.statement: How many grams are in 1 kg?
hints: “Kilo” means one thousand.

ms-24.statement: A bag of flour weighs 500 g. How many bags make 2 kg together?

ms-26.statement: A sack weighs 25 kg. How many sacks together weigh one metric ton?

ms-27.statement: How many milliliters are in 1 l?
hints: “Milli” means one thousandth.

ms-28.statement: A bottle holds 2 l of water. How many glasses of 250 ml can be filled from it?

ms-30.statement: An aquarium holds 60 l and is filled with a bucket of 5 l. How many times must the bucket be filled?
hints: How many 5s fit into 60?

ms-32.statement: Add 2 m 40 cm and 1 m 80 cm. How many centimeters is that in total?
hints: Convert everything to centimeters.
solution: 240 cm + 180 cm = 420 cm (that is 4 m 20 cm).

ms-33.statement: A piece of cloth 5 m long is cut into pieces of 50 cm each. How many pieces are there?

ms-34.statement: A truck carries 3 t 500 kg of goods and unloads 1 t 800 kg. How many kilograms of goods does it still carry?
hints: Convert everything to kilograms.

ms-35.statement: A cup holds 250 ml. How many liters are in 8 full cups?

ms-36.statement: 6 kg of apples cost 18 lei. How much do 2 kg of apples cost?
hints: First find how much 1 kg costs.

ms-37.statement: You have one 10 lei banknote and one 5 lei banknote. How many lei do you have in total?
hints: Add the values.

ms-38.statement: Which amount of money is the largest?
hints: Compare the numbers.

ms-39.statement: How many bani are in 1 leu?
hints: The ban is one hundredth of a leu.
3 lei = 300 bani.

ms-41.statement: How many 50-bani coins make 4 lei together?
hints: 2 coins of 50 bani make 1 leu.
solution: One leu means 2 coins of 50 bani; for 4 lei: 4 × 2 = 8 coins.

ms-42.statement: A notebook costs 6 lei. You pay with a 10 lei banknote. How much change do you get?
hints: Change = what you paid − what it costs.

ms-43.statement: You buy a book for 34 lei and a pen for 7 lei. How many lei do you pay?
hints: Add the prices.

ms-44.statement: You have 50 lei and buy a ball for 28 lei. How many lei do you have left?
hints: Subtract the price from what you have.

ms-45.statement: Three notebooks cost 4 lei each, and a pencil case costs 15 lei. How much do they all cost?
hints: The notebooks first: 3 × 4.

ms-46.statement: You have 100 lei and buy 3 books for 27 lei each. How many lei do you have left?
hints: First find how much the 3 books cost.

ms-47.statement:
What time does the clock show?
The small (yellow) hand shows the hour, the big (blue) hand shows the minutes.
hints: The big hand is at 12: the hour exactly.
solution: The small hand points to 9, and the big hand is at 12 ⇒ 9 o'clock.

ms-48.statement:
What time does the clock show?
The small (yellow) hand shows the hour, the big (blue) hand shows the minutes.
hints: The big hand at 6 means “half past”.
solution: The small hand has passed 4, and the big hand is at 6 ⇒ half past 4, that is 4:30.

ms-49.statement:
What time does the clock show?
The small (yellow) hand shows the hour, the big (blue) hand shows the minutes.
hints: The big hand at 3 means 15 minutes.
solution: The small hand has just passed 7, and the big hand is at 3 ⇒ 7:15 (a quarter past seven).

ms-50.statement:
What time does the clock show?
The small (yellow) hand shows the hour, the big (blue) hand shows the minutes.
hints: The small hand is close to 11, but has not reached it yet.
solution: The big hand at 9 means 45 minutes; the small hand is between 10 and 11 ⇒ 10:45, that is a quarter to 11.

ms-51.statement: The digital clock shows 18:20. How many minutes are left until 19:00?
hints: An hour has 60 minutes.

ms-52.statement: What time is it 25 minutes after 8:50?
hints: Until 9 o'clock there are 10 minutes left.
solution: 8:50 + 10 minutes = 9:00; another 15 minutes ⇒ 9:15. (8:75 does not exist: an hour has 60 minutes.)

ms-53.statement: How many days are in two weeks?
hints: A week has 7 days.
Say the days of the week in order.

ms-55.statement: How many months are in a year?
hints: January, February, …
solution: From January to December there are 12 months.

hints: Summer: June, July, August.
solution: June, July and August are the summer months ⇒ summer.

ms-57.statement: How many days does April have?
hints: Count the months on your knuckles: the months on a knuckle have 31 days, and those in the dips between them have one day less (except February).

ms-58.statement: How many days does a leap year have?
hints: In a leap year, February has 29 days.
solution: An ordinary year has 365 days; a leap year has one more: 365 + 1 = 366.

ms-59.statement: A movie starts at hour 16 and lasts 2 hours. At what time does it end?
hints: Add the 2 hours.

ms-60.statement: How many minutes are there from 9:15 to 10:00?
hints: How many minutes are left until the next hour?

ms-61.statement: The train leaves at 14:30 and arrives at 17:10. How many minutes does the trip take?
hints: From 14:30 to 17:00, then another 10 minutes.
solution: From 14:30 to 17:00: 2 and a half hours = 150 minutes; plus 10 minutes ⇒ 160 minutes.

ms-62.statement: A trip lasts 3 hours and 20 minutes and ends at 18:00. At what time did it start?
hints: Go back from 18:00.

ms-63.statement: Mihai sleeps from 21:30 to 7:00. How many minutes does he sleep?
hints: Count the whole hours first.
solution: From 21:30 to 7:30 is 10 hours, but he wakes up 30 minutes earlier ⇒ 9 hours and 30 minutes.

ms-64.statement: How many years are in a decade?
hints: “Deca” means ten.

ms-65.statement: How many years are in a century?
hints: A century has 10 decades.

ms-66.statement: How many centuries are in a millennium?
hints: A millennium has 1000 years.

ms-67.statement: How many years are in a century and a half?
hints: Half a century = 50 years.

ms-68.statement: In which century is the year 2026?
hints: The twentieth century runs from the year 1901 to the year 2000.
solution: The years 2001–2100 form the twenty-first century ⇒ 2026 is in the twenty-first century.

ms-69.statement: In which century is the year 1859?
hints: The years 1801–1900 form one century.
solution: The years 1801–1900 form the nineteenth century ⇒ 1859 is in the nineteenth century.

fg-01.statement: Which shape is to the left of the yellow star?
hints: The yellow star is in the top row; look in the box to its left.
solution: In the top row, to the left of the yellow star is the triangle.

fg-02.statement: Which shape is below the heart?
hints: The heart is in the middle; look in the box below it.
solution: Below the heart, in the bottom row, is the green square.

fg-03.statement: Which shape is in the bottom right corner?
hints: Bottom right corner = bottom row, the box on the right.
solution: In the bottom row, the last box on the right has the blue star.

fg-04.statement: How many shapes are in the box above the red square?
hints: The red square is in the middle row, on the left.
solution: Above the red square there is only one box: the one with the green triangle ⇒ 1 shape.

fg-05.statement: Ana is facing the board, and the classroom door is on her left. If Ana turns her back to the board, the door is:
hints: When you turn around, left and right swap places.
solution: With her back turned, what was on the left ends up on the right ⇒ the door is on her right.

fg-06.statement: There are three books on a shelf. The red book is between the green book and the blue book, and the green book is the first from the left. In which place from the left is the blue book?
hints: Put the books in order: green, then…
solution: The order from the left: green, red, blue ⇒ the blue book is the 3rd.

fg-07.statement:
In which column is the star?
The columns are numbered at the bottom, the rows on the left (from bottom to top).
hints: Read the number under the star's column.
solution: The star is above the number 2 ⇒ column 2 (and row 2).

fg-08.statement: We start from the star and move 3 squares to the right. In which column do we end up?
hints: The star is in column 2.

fg-09.statement: A robot starts from A and does: → → ↑ → ↑ ↑ →. How many squares further to the right than A does it end up?
hints: Count only the → arrows.
solution: There are 4 → arrows (the other 3 are ↑) ⇒ 4 squares further to the right.

fg-10.statement: Point A is in column 1 and row 1. Point B is in column 4 and row 4. What is the smallest number of steps (only to the right and up, one square at a time) from A to B?
hints: Count the steps to the right and the steps up.
solution: To the right: 4 − 1 = 3 steps; up: 4 − 1 = 3 steps ⇒ 3 + 3 = 6 steps.

fg-11.statement: The star is in column 2 and row 2 (rows are counted from bottom to top). We move 2 squares to the right and 2 up. In which row do we end up?
hints: Only moving up changes the row.
solution: The row: 2 + 2 = 4 (the column becomes 2 + 2 = 4, that is exactly at B).

fg-12.statement: A robot moves from the box in column 1, row 1 to column 5, row 3, only to the right and up. How many times as many steps does it take to the right as up?
hints: How many steps to the right? How many up?
solution: To the right: 5 − 1 = 4 steps; up: 3 − 1 = 2 steps; 4 ÷ 2 = 2 ⇒ 2 times as many.

hints: It has two endpoints.
solution: The line has two endpoints, A and B ⇒ the segment AB.

hints: It has one endpoint and goes on forever in the other direction.
solution: It starts at A and goes on forever in one direction ⇒ a ray.

hints: It has no endpoints.
solution: It goes on forever in both directions ⇒ a line.

fg-16.statement: How many segments make up the broken line ABCDE?
hints: Count the straight pieces between the points.

fg-17.statement: How many different segments have their endpoints at three points A, B, C that are not on the same line?
hints: Join each point to each other point.
solution: AB, AC, BC ⇒ 3 segments (they form a triangle).

fg-18.statement: How many lines pass through two different points?
hints: Try to draw two different lines through the same two points.
solution: Through two different points passes exactly one line.

fg-19.statement: How are the two lines related?
hints: Do they ever meet?
solution: The lines keep the same distance and never meet ⇒ parallel.

fg-20.statement: How are the two lines related?
hints: What kind of angle do they form?
solution: The lines form right angles ⇒ perpendicular.

fg-21.statement: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
hints: The opposite sides.
solution: The opposite sides are parallel: the two lengths and the two widths ⇒ 2 pairs.

fg-22.statement: Two adjacent sides of a square are:
hints: What angle do the adjacent sides of a square form?
solution: Adjacent sides form a right angle ⇒ they are perpendicular.

fg-23.statement: How many right angles are formed around the point where two perpendicular lines meet?
hints: Look at the picture with the perpendicular lines.
solution: Around the meeting point, 4 angles are formed, all right angles.

fg-24.statement: How are the two lines related?
hints: They meet, but what angle do they form?
solution: The lines meet at a point, but the angles are not right angles ⇒ they intersect, without being perpendicular.
Answer: they intersect, without being perpendicular.

fg-25.statement: What kind of angle is drawn?
hints: Compare it with the corner of a sheet of paper (a right angle).
solution: The angle is smaller than a right angle ⇒ acute.

fg-26.statement: What kind of angle is drawn?
hints: It is exactly like the corner of a sheet of paper.
solution: The angle is like the corner of a sheet of paper (marked with a small square) ⇒ right.

fg-27.statement: What kind of angle is drawn?
hints: It is wider open than the corner of a sheet of paper.
solution: The angle is larger than a right angle ⇒ obtuse.

fg-28.statement: How many right angles do a rectangle and a square have altogether?
hints: A rectangle and a square have only right-angled corners.
solution: A rectangle has 4 right angles, and a square has 4 too ⇒ 4 + 4 = 8 right angles.

fg-29.statement: At 3 o'clock exactly, the hands of a clock form an angle that is:
hints: The small hand at 3, the big hand at 12.
solution: The hands point to 12 and 3, that is a quarter turn ⇒ a right angle.

fg-30.statement: At 4 o'clock exactly, the hands of a clock form an angle that is:
hints: At 3 o'clock it is right; at 4 o'clock the small hand has moved further.
solution: The hands point to 12 and 4, more than a quarter turn ⇒ an obtuse angle.

fg-31.statement: How many sides does the drawn polygon have?
hints: Count the segments of the outline.
solution: The outline has 6 segments ⇒ 6 sides (a hexagon).

fg-32.statement: How many vertices does a polygon with 5 sides have?
hints: Each side ends at a vertex.
solution: A polygon has as many vertices as sides ⇒ 5 vertices (a pentagon).

fg-33.statement: How many diagonals does a rectangle have?
hints: A diagonal joins two vertices that are not adjacent.
solution: The rectangle ABCD has the diagonals AC and BD ⇒ 2 diagonals.

fg-34.statement: How many diagonals does a triangle have?
hints: Are there two vertices of a triangle that are not adjacent?
solution: In a triangle, any two vertices are joined by a side ⇒ no diagonal: 0.

fg-35.statement: Which is the polygon with the smallest number of sides?
hints: A polygon has at least 3 sides.
solution: The smallest number of sides is 3 ⇒ the triangle. (The circle is not a polygon.)

fg-36.statement: A polygon has 8 sides. How many vertices and sides does it have in total?
hints: Vertices = sides.

fg-37.statement: How many triangles are in the picture?
hints: A triangle has 3 corners.
solution: The shapes with 3 corners are 3 ⇒ 3 triangles.

fg-38.statement: How many corners does a triangle have?
hints: “Tri” means three.

fg-39.statement: A triangle is made from 3 sticks of 7 cm each. How long is its outline?
hints: Add the three sides.

fg-40.statement: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: Perimeter = the sum of the sides.

fg-41.statement: A triangle with all sides equal is called:
hints: “Equi” means equal.
solution: The triangle with all 3 sides equal is equilateral.

fg-42.statement: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. How long is one side?
hints: The 3 sides are equal.

fg-43.statement: How many rectangles (that are not squares) are in the picture?
hints: A rectangle has 4 right-angle corners and two sides longer than the other two.
solution: The shapes with 4 right-angle corners and sides of different lengths are 3 ⇒ 3 rectangles.

fg-44.statement: How many right-angle corners does a rectangle have?
hints: All its corners are the same.

fg-45.statement: The opposite sides of a rectangle are:
hints: Compare the top side with the bottom one.
solution: The opposite sides of a rectangle are equal (and parallel).

fg-46.statement: A rectangle has a length of 9 cm and a width of 4 cm. What is the sum of the two long sides of the rectangle?
hints: A rectangle has two long sides, equal to each other.

fg-47.statement: The sides of a rectangle are 12 cm, 5 cm, 12 cm and 5 cm. What is the width?
hints: The width is the shorter side.
solution: The shorter sides are 5 cm ⇒ the width is 5 cm (the length is 12 cm).

fg-48.statement: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width, and the width is 6 cm. What is the length?
hints: “3 times as long” means multiplication.

fg-49.statement: How many squares are in the picture?
hints: A square has 4 sides of the same length and 4 right-angle corners.
solution: The shapes with 4 equal sides and right-angle corners are 4 ⇒ 4 squares.

fg-50.statement: How many equal sides does a square have?
hints: All the sides of a square are the same.
solution: A square has 4 sides, all equal.

fg-51.statement: Is a square also a rectangle?
options: yes, a rectangle with all sides equal
no, a square has no right-angle corners
yes, but only if it is small
hints: What does a shape need in order to be a rectangle?
solution: A square has 4 right-angle corners and equal opposite sides, so it is a rectangle — one with all sides equal.
Answer: yes, a rectangle with all sides equal.

fg-52.statement: A square has a side of 8 cm. What is the sum of two sides?
hints: All the sides are 8 cm.

fg-53.statement: A rectangle has a length of 7 cm and a width of 7 cm. What shape is it?
hints: The length and the width are equal.
solution: A rectangle with all sides equal is a square.

fg-54.statement: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. What is the sum of two sides?
hints: First find the side: 36 ÷ 4.
solution: The side: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm; two sides: 9 + 9 = 18 cm.

fg-55.statement: What shape is drawn? (all 4 sides are equal)
hints: It has 4 equal sides, but the corners are not right angles.
solution: Four equal sides and corners that are not right angles ⇒ a rhombus.

hints: The opposite sides are parallel and equal, the corners are not right angles.
solution: Opposite sides parallel and equal, no right-angle corners ⇒ a parallelogram.

fg-57.statement: How many equal sides does a rhombus have?
hints: A rhombus looks like a “tilted” square.
solution: A rhombus has all 4 sides equal.

fg-58.statement: A rhombus with all corners right angles is a:
options: rectangle that is not a square
hints: 4 equal sides + 4 right-angle corners.
solution: Equal sides and right-angle corners ⇒ a square.

fg-59.statement: A parallelogram with all corners right angles is a:
hints: The opposite sides stay equal, and the corners become right angles.
solution: A parallelogram with right-angle corners ⇒ a rectangle.

fg-60.statement: A parallelogram has sides of 9 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: The opposite sides are equal: 9, 5, 9, 5.

fg-61.statement: How many circles are in the picture?
hints: A circle is round, without corners.

fg-62.statement: How many corners does a circle have?
hints: A circle is round.
solution: A circle has no corners at all: 0.

fg-63.statement: The center of a circle is at the same distance from:
options: a single point of the circle
all the points of the circle
hints: Think of the spokes of a wheel.
solution: All the points of the circle are at the same distance from the center (this distance is the radius).
Answer: all the points of the circle.

fg-64.statement: The radius of a circle is 4 cm. What is its diameter?
hints: The diameter passes through the center and is made of two radii.

fg-65.statement: The diameter of a circle is 14 cm. What is the radius?
hints: The radius is half the diameter.

fg-66.statement: A circle together with its inside is called:
hints: Like a full plate, not just its rim.
solution: The circle is the outline; its inside, together with the outline, is the disk.

fg-67.statement: The figure is completed symmetrically about the dotted axis (as in a mirror). How many colored squares will the whole figure have?
hints: The right half will have just as many squares as the left half.
solution: To the left of the axis there are 7 squares; in the mirror 7 more appear: 7 + 7 = 14.

fg-68.statement: Which letter has a vertical line of symmetry (the left half is the mirror image of the right half)?
hints: Fold the letter down the middle, from top to bottom: do the halves match?
solution: The letter A has identical left and right halves ⇒ it has a vertical line of symmetry.

fg-69.statement: Which letter has NO line of symmetry?
hints: H and O even have two lines.
solution: F does not match itself by any fold ⇒ it has no line of symmetry.

fg-70.statement: If we fold a symmetrical figure along its line of symmetry, the two halves:
hints: Think of the wings of a butterfly.
solution: The line of symmetry divides the figure into two halves that match exactly.

fg-71.statement: A symmetrical figure has 18 colored squares in total, and the line of symmetry does not cut through any square. How many colored squares are to the left of the line of symmetry?
hints: The two halves have the same number of squares.

fg-72.statement: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
hints: Two through the midpoints of the sides and two along the diagonals.
solution: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 2 through the midpoints of opposite sides and 2 diagonals.

fg-73.statement: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
hints: The diagonals of a rectangle are NOT lines of symmetry.
solution: Only the lines through the midpoints of opposite sides ⇒ 2 lines.

fg-74.statement: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
hints: One from each vertex.
solution: From each vertex a line goes to the midpoint of the opposite side ⇒ 3 lines.

fg-75.statement: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
hints: Any line that passes through the center…
solution: Any line that passes through the center is a line of symmetry ⇒ countless.
Answer: countless (any line through the center).

fg-76.statement: Which shape has NO line of symmetry?
options: the parallelogram (that is not a rhombus or a rectangle)
hints: Try to fold each shape.
solution: An ordinary parallelogram does not match itself by any fold ⇒ no line of symmetry.
Answer: the parallelogram (that is not a rhombus or a rectangle).

fg-77.statement: What is the perimeter of the drawn polygon? (the side lengths are written in cm)
hints: Perimeter = the sum of all the sides.

fg-78.statement: A pentagon has all sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: 5 equal sides.

fg-79.statement: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm. What is the perimeter?
hints: Add the sides.

fg-80.statement: A hexagon with all sides equal has a perimeter of 48 cm. How long is one side?
hints: 6 equal sides.

fg-81.statement: A garden has the shape of a triangle with sides of 20 m, 30 m and 40 m. How many meters of fence are needed to go around it?
hints: The fence = the perimeter.

fg-82.statement: A square has a side of 9 cm. What is the perimeter?
hints: P = 4 × side.

fg-83.statement: The perimeter of a square is 48 cm. What is the side?
hints: Side = P ÷ 4.

fg-84.statement: A square has a side of 15 cm. What is the perimeter?
hints: 4 sides of 15 cm.

fg-85.statement: A square plot has a perimeter of 100 m. What is the side?
hints: Divide the perimeter by 4.

fg-86.statement: If the side of a square grows from 5 cm to 10 cm, the perimeter:
hints: Calculate both perimeters.
solution: 4 × 5 = 20 cm and 4 × 10 = 40 cm ⇒ the perimeter doubles.

fg-87.statement: A rectangle has a length of 12 cm and a width of 5 cm. What is the perimeter?

fg-88.statement: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm and a width of 5 cm. What is the length?

fg-89.statement: A rectangular plot has a perimeter of 56 m and a length of 20 m. What is the width?
hints: Half of the perimeter = L + l.

fg-90.statement: A rectangle has a width of 4 cm, and its length is 3 times the width. What is the perimeter?
hints: First find the length.

fg-91.statement: What is the perimeter of the drawn rectangle? (the lengths are written in cm)
hints: The opposite sides are equal: 8, 3, 8, 3.

fg-92.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the colored figure?
hints: Count the sides of small squares along the outline, all the way around.
solution: On the outline there are 12 sides of 1 cm each ⇒ 12 cm.

fg-93.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the colored figure?
hints: Go along the outline and count the sides of small squares.
solution: The outline has 14 sides of 1 cm each ⇒ 14 cm.

fg-94.statement: Two squares with a side of 3 cm are joined along one side. What is the perimeter of the figure obtained?
hints: The figure is a rectangle 6 cm × 3 cm.
solution: The rectangle is 6 cm by 3 cm: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18 cm (the joined side is not counted).

fg-95.statement: Three squares with a side of 2 cm are placed in a row, joined together. What is the perimeter of the figure?
hints: The figure is a rectangle 6 cm × 2 cm.

fg-96.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the colored figure?
hints: Count the sides on the “steps” too.
solution: The outline has 14 sides of 1 cm each ⇒ 14 cm.

fg-97.statement: How many small squares cover the colored figure? (this is its area, in small squares)
hints: Count the colored squares, row by row.

fg-98.statement: A figure is covered exactly by 24 squares with a side of 1 cm. What is its area?
hints: Each square of 1 cm has an area of 1 cm².
solution: 24 squares of 1 cm² each ⇒ the area is 24 cm².

fg-99.statement: Figure A is covered by 15 small squares, and figure B by 18 of the same small squares. Which has the larger area?
hints: More small squares = a larger area.
solution: 18 is greater than 15 ⇒ figure B has the larger area.

fg-100.statement: In what unit is area measured?
hints: Area is measured with squares.
solution: Area is measured in squares with a side of 1 cm, that is, in square centimeters (cm²).

fg-101.statement: Each small square has an area of 1 cm². What is the area of the colored figure?
hints: Count the small squares.

fg-102.statement: A rectangle has a length of 7 cm and a width of 4 cm. What is its area?
hints: 4 rows of 7 small squares each.

fg-103.statement: A square has a side of 6 cm. What is its area?
hints: The area of a square = side × side.

fg-104.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the area of the colored rectangle?
hints: 3 rows of 5 small squares each.

fg-105.statement: A rectangle has an area of 40 cm² and a length of 8 cm. What is the width?
hints: Width = area ÷ length.

fg-106.statement: A square has an area of 49 cm². What is its side?
hints: What number multiplied by itself gives 49?

fg-107.statement: A rectangular room is 5 m long and 4 m wide. How many square meters of flooring are needed?
hints: Area = L × l.

fg-108.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the area of the colored figure?
hints: Split the figure into two rectangles and add the areas.
solution: The left column: 3 small squares; the bottom right piece: 2 small squares; 3 + 2 = 5 cm².

fg-109.statement: An L-shaped figure is made of a rectangle of 6 cm × 2 cm and a square with a side of 2 cm. What is the area of the figure?
hints: Add the two areas.

fg-110.statement: From a rectangle of 8 cm × 5 cm, a square with a side of 2 cm is cut out of one corner. What is the area of the remaining figure?
hints: The whole area minus the cut-out area.

fg-111.statement: We cut a figure into two pieces and arrange them differently, without overlapping. The area of the new figure:
hints: The pieces cover just as many small squares as before.
solution: By moving the pieces we neither add nor lose small squares ⇒ the area stays the same.

fg-112.statement: Each small square has a side of 1 cm. What is the area of the colored figure?
hints: Count the small squares on each row.

fg-113.statement: A rectangle of 6 cm × 2 cm and a square with a side of 4 cm. What do they have in common?
options: the same area and the same perimeter
hints: Calculate the area and the perimeter of each.
solution: The areas: 6 × 2 = 12 cm² and 4 × 4 = 16 cm² — different. The perimeters: 2 × (6 + 2) = 16 cm and 4 × 4 = 16 cm — equal ⇒ the same perimeter, different areas.
Answer: the same perimeter, different areas.

fg-114.statement: A rectangle of 8 cm × 1 cm and one of 4 cm × 2 cm. Which has the larger area?
hints: Calculate the areas.
solution: 8 × 1 = 8 cm² and 4 × 2 = 8 cm² ⇒ the same area (the perimeters, however, differ: 18 cm and 12 cm).
Answer: they have the same area.

fg-115.statement: A square has a side of 4 cm. What number appears both for the perimeter (in cm) and for the area (in cm²)?
hints: Calculate both.
solution: The perimeter: 4 × 4 = 16 cm; the area: 4 × 4 = 16 cm² ⇒ 16 (but they are different quantities: a length and an area).

fg-116.statement: If the side of a square doubles, its area:
hints: Compare 3 × 3 with 6 × 6.
solution: 3 × 3 = 9 and 6 × 6 = 36; 36 ÷ 9 = 4 ⇒ the area becomes 4 times as large.

fg-117.statement: The fence around a garden is calculated with:
hints: The fence goes along the outline.
solution: The fence goes around the garden ⇒ its length is the perimeter. (The grass to be sown would be calculated with the area.)

hints: It looks like a die.
solution: All the faces are equal squares ⇒ a cube.

hints: It looks like a ball.
solution: It is round in every direction ⇒ a sphere.

hints: It looks like a tin can.
solution: Two equal circles at the top and bottom ⇒ a cylinder.

hints: It looks like an ice cream cone.
solution: A circle at the bottom and a sharp point at the top ⇒ a cone.

fg-122.statement: Which of these is a flat shape, not a solid?
hints: Flat shapes can be drawn on paper; solids take up space.
solution: The square is a flat shape; the cube, the sphere and the cylinder are solids.

fg-123.statement: What solid is drawn? (the faces are rectangles)
hints: It looks like a shoe box.
solution: The faces are rectangles, not all equal ⇒ a cuboid (rectangular box).

fg-124.statement: How many faces does a cube have?
hints: Think of a die: how many numbers does it have?
solution: A cube has 6 faces (like the 6 numbers on a die).

fg-125.statement: How many vertices does a cube have?
hints: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom.
solution: 4 vertices at the top and 4 at the bottom ⇒ 8 vertices.

fg-126.statement: How many edges does a cube have?
hints: 4 at the top, 4 at the bottom and 4 vertical.

fg-127.statement: The faces of a cube are:
hints: All the faces of a cube are the same.
solution: All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.

fg-128.statement: A cube has an edge of 5 cm. What is the sum of the lengths of all its edges?
hints: 12 equal edges.

fg-129.statement: How many faces does a cuboid (rectangular box) have?
hints: Just as many as a cube.
solution: A cuboid has 6 faces, all rectangles (equal in pairs).

fg-130.statement: How many bases (flat faces) does a cylinder have?
hints: One at the top and one at the bottom.
solution: A cylinder has 2 bases, equal circles.

fg-131.statement: How many bases does a cone have?
hints: A cone has a point and a…
solution: A cone has a single base (a circle) and a point.

fg-132.statement: How many flat faces does a sphere have?
hints: Can you put a ball on a table without it rolling?
solution: A sphere is round everywhere ⇒ no flat face.

fg-133.statement: How many side faces (triangles) does a pyramid with a square base have?
hints: One for each side of the base.
solution: The base has 4 sides ⇒ 4 triangular side faces.

hints: Solids with a curved surface can roll.
solution: A cube has only flat faces ⇒ it does not roll.

fg-135.statement: Which of the drawn solids has a point and a circular base?
hints: Look for the solid with a circle at the bottom and a point at the top.
solution: The cone (B) has a circular base and a point.

fg-136.statement: How many squares make up the net of a cube?
hints: How many faces does a cube have?
solution: A cube has 6 square faces ⇒ the net has 6 squares.

fg-137.statement: Which of the nets can be folded into a cube?
hints: Try folding it in your mind: the faces must not overlap.
solution: The cross (A) folds into a cube. B (6 squares in a row) wraps around without lids, and C (2 × 3) has squares that overlap.

fg-138.statement: The net of a cylinder is made of two circles and:
hints: Peel the label off a tin can.
solution: The unrolled side surface is a rectangle.

fg-139.statement: How many rectangles make up the net of a cuboid?
hints: How many faces does a cuboid have?
solution: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces ⇒ 6 rectangles.

fg-140.statement: Can six equal squares placed one after another, in a row, be folded into a cube?
options: no: no squares are left for the lids
no, because there are too many
hints: Wrap the strip in your mind: what covers the top and the bottom?
solution: The strip wraps around the cube, but the top and the bottom stay open ⇒ it is not possible.
Answer: no: no squares are left for the lids.

fg-141.statement: How many small cubes make up the drawn solid?
hints: One layer has 3 × 2 cubes; there are 2 layers.

fg-142.statement: How many small cubes make up the drawn solid?
hints: One layer has 4 × 3 cubes.

fg-143.statement: A big cube has an edge made of 3 small cubes. How many small cubes is it made of?
hints: 3 layers of 3 × 3 cubes each.

fg-144.statement: A cuboid is made of layers of 6 cubes each. How many layers does it have, if it has 30 cubes in total?
hints: Divide the total by the cubes in one layer.

fg-145.statement: A cuboid has 5 cubes along its length, 2 along its width and 2 along its height. How many cubes is it made of?
hints: Length × width × height.

vm-001.statement: A stick is 5 pencils long. How many pencils, placed end to end, measure two identical sticks?
hints: Two sticks means two times 5 pencils each.

vm-002.statement: Ana measures the desk with her hand span. Dan measures the same desk with a pencil shorter than a hand span. Who gets a greater number?
hints: With a smaller unit you need more pieces.
solution: The pencil is shorter than the hand span, so it fits more times into the length of the desk. Dan gets a greater number.

vm-003.statement: Why do we measure lengths in meters and centimeters, not in hand spans?
options: because hand spans are too small
because hand spans can't be counted
because the meter is the same for everyone
because hand spans are longer than the meter
hints: A child's hand span and an adult's hand span are not the same.
solution: Hand spans differ from person to person, so they give different results. The meter and the centimeter are the same for everyone.
Answer: because the meter is the same for everyone.

vm-004.statement: What do you use to find out how much a watermelon weighs?
hints: You want to find its mass.
solution: Mass is measured with a scale. A ruler measures lengths, a clock measures time, and a thermometer measures temperature.

hints: Think about hours and minutes.
solution: A clock measures time, in hours, minutes and seconds.

vm-006.statement: Which length is right for the height of a door?
hints: A door is a little taller than a person.
solution: A door is about 2 m. 2 cm and 2 mm are too little, and 2 km is a walking distance.

vm-007.statement: A segment is 4 cm long. You extend it by 4 cm more. How long is it now?
hints: Add the two lengths.

vm-008.statement: A segment starts at mark 4 on the ruler and ends at mark 10. How long is it?
hints: The segment doesn't start from 0: subtract the marks.
solution: 10 − 4 = 6. The length is the difference between the marks, not the number at the end.

vm-009.statement: A segment of 12 cm is divided into two equal parts. How long is each part?
hints: Divide the length by 2.
100 cm make 1 m.

vm-011.statement: How many meters are in half a kilometer?
hints: 1 km has 1000 m.

vm-012.statement:
Convert:
1 km and 5 m = □ m
hints: 1 km has 1000 m. Watch the zeros.
solution: 1000 + 5 = 1005. Not 105 and not 1050: it is 1000 meters and 5 more.

vm-013.statement: How many grams are in half a kilogram?
hints: 1 kg has 1000 g.

vm-014.statement:
Convert:
2 kg and 50 g = □ g
hints: 2 kg means 2000 g.

vm-015.statement: Which weighs more: 1 kg of feathers or 1 kg of iron?
hints: Read the masses carefully.
solution: Both are 1 kg, so they weigh the same. The feathers just take up more space.

vm-016.statement: How many kilograms are in half a metric ton?
hints: 1 t has 1000 kg.

vm-017.statement: How many milliliters are in half a liter?
hints: 1 l has 1000 ml.

vm-018.statement:
Convert:
1 l and 5 ml = □ ml
hints: 1 l has 1000 ml. Watch the zeros.

vm-019.statement: How many 500 ml bottles can be filled from a 5 l jug?
hints: Two 500 ml bottles make 1 l.
solution: From one liter 2 bottles are filled, so from 5 l, 5 × 2 = 10 bottles are filled.

vm-020.statement: From a ribbon of 1 m you cut 35 cm. How many centimeters are left?
hints: First convert the meter into centimeters.

vm-021.statement: A watermelon weighs 4 kg, and an apple weighs 150 g. How many grams do they weigh together?
hints: Convert the kilograms into grams, then add.

vm-022.statement: You pour 750 ml of water over 250 ml of syrup. How many liters of drink do you get?
hints: Add the milliliters, then convert to liters.

vm-023.statement: How many 1 leu banknotes do you get in exchange for a 5 lei banknote?
hints: The value must stay the same.
solution: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5, so you get 5 banknotes of 1 leu.

vm-024.statement: How many 10 lei banknotes make 100 lei together?
hints: Count 10 by 10 up to 100.

vm-025.statement: How many 10 bani coins make 1 leu together?
hints: 1 leu has 100 bani.

vm-026.statement: A juice costs 5 lei. You pay with a 5 lei banknote. How much change do you get?
hints: You gave exactly what it costs.

vm-027.statement: You have 20 lei. A book costs 23 lei. How many more lei do you need?
hints: By how much is the price greater than your money?

vm-028.statement: You have 50 lei. You want a ball that costs 32 lei and a game that costs 21 lei. Do you have enough money?
hints: Add the prices and compare with 50.
solution: 32 + 21 = 53, and 53 is greater than 50. You need 53 − 50 = 3 more lei.
Answer: no, you need 3 more lei.

vm-029.statement: At exactly 12 o'clock, where do the two hands of the clock point?
hints: On the hour, the long hand points toward 12.
solution: At exactly 12 o'clock, the short hand shows the hour 12, and the long hand is also at 12: the hands overlap.

vm-030.statement: The long hand of the clock points toward 6. How many minutes have passed since the hour?
hints: From one number to the next there are 5 minutes.

vm-031.statement: The digital clock shows 15:00. What time does a clock with hands show then?
hints: After hour 12, subtract 12.
The week ends and starts again.
solution: The week ends with Sunday, then Monday comes again. Before Monday is Sunday.

vm-033.statement: How many days does February have in a year that is not a leap year?
hints: February is the shortest month.
solution: In a common year, February has 28 days. In leap years it has 29.

hints: April, June, September and November have 30 days each.
solution: December has 31 days. November and April have 30, and February has 28 or 29.

vm-035.statement: A match starts at 10 o'clock and ends at 12 o'clock. How many hours does it last?
hints: Subtract the start time from the end time.

vm-036.statement: The lesson starts at 8:00 and lasts 50 minutes. How many minutes are there from its end until 9:00?
hints: From 8:00 to 9:00 there are 60 minutes.

vm-037.statement: A train leaves at 23:40 and arrives at 0:25, the next day. How many minutes does the trip take?
hints: First calculate up to midnight, then after.
solution: Until midnight there are 20 minutes, and after that 25 more: 20 + 25 = 45.

vm-038.statement: How many years are in a millennium?
hints: A millennium has 10 centuries.

vm-039.statement: How many decades are in a century?
hints: A century has 100 years, and a decade has 10 years.

vm-040.statement: In which century is the year 2000?
hints: A century ends with the year that has two zeros at the end.
solution: The twentieth century runs from 1901 to 2000. The year 2000 is its last year; the twenty-first century begins in 2001.

vm-041.statement: How many minutes are in half an hour?
hints: An hour has 60 minutes.

vm-042.statement: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
hints: An hour has 60 minutes.

vm-043.statement: How many hours are in a week?
hints: A day has 24 hours.

vg-001.statement: On a shelf there are, from left to right: the teddy bear, the ball and the toy car. Which toy is in the middle?
hints: In the middle is the toy that has one on each side.
solution: The teddy bear is on the left, the toy car on the right, and the ball is between them, in the middle.

vg-002.statement: Mihai and Ana stand facing each other. Mihai raises his right hand. On which side does Ana see the raised hand?
hints: When you face someone, their right is on your left side.
solution: The two look at each other, so left and right are reversed: Mihai's right is on Ana's left.

vg-003.statement: A robot takes 3 steps to the right, then 3 steps to the left. How many squares from the starting place is it?
hints: The steps to the left cancel the ones to the right.
solution: 3 − 3 = 0: the robot is back where it started.

vg-004.statement: A robot starts from A and does: ↑ ↑ → ↓ ↓. How many squares further to the right than A does it end up?
hints: Count only the → arrows.
solution: There is only one arrow to the right, so the robot ends up 1 square further to the right. The steps up and down don't move it to the right.

vg-005.statement: On a grid, the star is in column 3 and row 5 (rows are counted from bottom to top). We go 2 squares down. In which row do we end up?
hints: When you go down, the row number decreases.

vg-006.statement: How many endpoints does a segment have?
hints: A segment is bounded at both ends.

vg-007.statement: How many endpoints does a line have?
hints: A line does not end in either direction.
solution: A line extends forever in both directions, so it has no endpoint: 0.

vg-008.statement: Which of them has only one endpoint?
hints: It starts from a point and never ends.
solution: A ray has one endpoint (the origin) and extends forever in the other direction.

vg-009.statement: The straight rails of a railway are an example of lines that are:
options: at a right angle to each other
hints: The rails always stay at the same distance from each other.
solution: The rails never meet and stay at the same distance: they are parallel.

vg-010.statement: At how many points do two parallel lines meet?
hints: Parallel lines always stay at the same distance.
solution: Two parallel lines never meet: 0 points.

vg-011.statement: How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
hints: The opposite sides are parallel.
solution: The square has two pairs of opposite sides, so 2 pairs of parallel sides.

vg-012.statement: How many sides does an angle have?
hints: An angle is made of two rays with the same origin.
solution: An angle has 2 sides and one vertex.

vg-013.statement: At 6 o'clock exactly, the hands of a clock form an angle that is:
hints: The long hand points toward 12, and the short hand toward 6.
solution: The hands are in line with each other, on the same line: the angle is straight.

vg-014.statement: An angle smaller than a right angle is called:
hints: It looks like a sharp point.
solution: An angle smaller than a right angle is acute. An angle greater than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle is obtuse.

vg-015.statement: How many vertices does a hexagon have?
hints: A hexagon has 6 sides.
solution: A polygon has as many vertices as sides: the hexagon has 6.

vg-016.statement: Which figure is NOT a polygon?
hints: A polygon has straight sides.
solution: The circle is a curved line, with no sides and no vertices, so it is not a polygon.

vg-017.statement: A polygon has 7 vertices. How many sides does it have?
hints: Each side joins two neighboring vertices.
solution: A polygon has as many sides as vertices: 7.

vg-018.statement: You draw two separate triangles. How many sides did you draw in total?
hints: A triangle has 3 sides.

vg-019.statement: You have 6 identical sticks. How many separate triangles can you make, if each side is one stick?
hints: For one triangle you need 3 sticks.
solution: Each triangle uses 3 sticks: 3 + 3 = 6, so you can make 2 triangles.

vg-020.statement: A triangle has a perimeter of 20 cm, and two of its sides are 6 cm and 9 cm. How long is the third side?
hints: Subtract the two known sides from the perimeter.

vg-021.statement: You draw two separate rectangles. How many corners do they have in total?
hints: A rectangle has 4 corners.

vg-022.statement: Which object is shaped like a rectangle?
hints: Look for the object with four right-angle corners.
solution: The door has four sides and four right-angle corners: it is a rectangle. The other objects are round.

vg-023.statement: A rectangle has two sides of 8 cm each and two sides of 3 cm each. What is the sum of all the sides?
hints: Add the four sides.

vg-024.statement: You cut a square of paper in two, from one corner to the opposite corner. What shapes do you get?
hints: Each piece has three corners.
solution: The cut from one corner to the opposite corner divides the square into two identical triangles.

options: no: only the one with all sides equal
yes, if it is drawn big
hints: The square has all sides equal.
solution: A rectangle is a square only if it has all sides equal. Every square is a rectangle, but not the other way around.
Answer: no: only the one with all sides equal.

vg-026.statement: A square is made from a wire of 20 cm, using all the wire. How long is its side?
hints: The 4 sides are equal.

vg-027.statement: A rhombus has a side of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: A rhombus has all 4 sides equal.

options: yes: it has all sides equal
hints: A rhombus is the figure with four equal sides.
solution: The square has all sides equal, so it is also a rhombus: a rhombus with all right-angle corners.
Answer: yes: it has all sides equal.

vg-029.statement: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
hints: The opposite sides are parallel.
solution: In a parallelogram, the opposite sides are parallel two by two: 2 pairs.

vg-030.statement: Which object is shaped like a circle?
hints: Look for the round object, with no corners.
solution: The ring is round, like a circle. The other objects have corners.

vg-031.statement: The diameter of a circle is 10 cm. How many centimeters from the center is a point on the circle?
hints: The distance from the center to the circle is the radius.
solution: The radius is half the diameter: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. All the points of the circle are 5 cm from the center.

vg-032.statement: How many times as long as its radius is the diameter of a circle?
hints: The diameter goes through the center, from one edge to the other.
solution: The diameter is made of two radii, so it is 2 times as long as the radius.

vg-033.statement: A symmetric figure has 6 colored squares to the left of the line of symmetry. How many colored squares does it have to the right of the line?
hints: The two parts are like a mirror image.
solution: The right part is the mirror image of the left part, so it also has 6 colored squares.

vg-034.statement: A point is 3 squares to the left of the line of symmetry. How many squares to the right of the line is its symmetric point?
hints: A point and its symmetric point are at the same distance from the line.
solution: The symmetric point is on the other side of the line, at the same distance: 3 squares.

vg-035.statement: A butterfly with open wings is symmetric about:
options: a line through the tip of a wing
a line through the middle of the body
hints: The left wing is the mirror image of the right wing.
solution: If we fold the drawing along the body, the wings overlap. The line of symmetry goes through the middle of the body.
Answer: a line through the middle of the body.

vg-036.statement: How many lines of symmetry does the letter A have?
hints: Try folding it vertically and horizontally.
solution: The letter A has only one line of symmetry, the vertical one: the left half is the mirror image of the right half.

vg-037.statement: How many lines of symmetry does the letter H have?
hints: Try folding it vertically and horizontally.
solution: The letter H has 2 lines of symmetry: one vertical and one horizontal.

vg-038.statement: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus that is not a square have?
hints: Fold the rhombus from one corner to the opposite corner.
solution: A rhombus has 2 lines of symmetry: the lines that join opposite corners.

vg-039.statement: A triangle has all sides 5 cm long. What is its perimeter?
hints: Add the three sides.

vg-040.statement: A quadrilateral has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: The perimeter is the sum of all the sides.

vg-041.statement: A pentagon has a perimeter of 40 cm. Four of the sides are 7 cm each. How long is the fifth side?
hints: First find how long the four sides are together.

vg-042.statement: A square has a side of 1 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: A square has 4 equal sides.

vg-043.statement: Mihai says that the perimeter of the square with a side of 7 cm is 14 cm. What did he do wrong?
hints: How many sides does a square have?
solution: Correct: 4 × 7 = 28. Mihai calculated 7 + 7 = 14, which is only two sides.
Answer: he added only two sides.

vg-044.statement: A square fence has a perimeter of 60 m. How many meters are three of its sides together?
hints: First find one side.

vg-045.statement: A rectangle has a length of 10 cm and a width of 1 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: There are two lengths and two widths.

vg-046.statement: The sum of the length and the width of a rectangle is 15 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: The perimeter has two lengths and two widths.
solution: The perimeter is twice the sum of the length and the width: 2 × 15 = 30.

vg-047.statement: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm, and its length is equal to its width. How long is a side?
hints: If the length is equal to the width, the rectangle is a square.

vg-048.statement: Four squares with a side of 1 cm are glued together to form a bigger square. What is the perimeter of the big square?
hints: The big square has a side made of two small squares.
solution: The side of the big square is 1 + 1 = 2 (cm), and the perimeter is 4 × 2 = 8.

vg-049.statement: Two rectangles of 4 cm × 2 cm are glued along their long sides. What is the perimeter of the figure obtained?
hints: What shape do you get? The glued sides are no longer on the edge.
solution: You get a square with a side of 4 cm (2 + 2 = 4). Its perimeter is 4 × 4 = 16.

vg-050.statement: We glue two identical squares along one side. The perimeter of the figure obtained is:
options: equal to the sum of the perimeters of the two squares
equal to the perimeter of a single square
less than the sum of the perimeters of the two squares
greater than the sum of the perimeters of the two squares
hints: The glued sides end up inside the figure.
solution: The two glued sides are no longer part of the outline, so the perimeter is less than the sum of the perimeters.
Answer: less than the sum of the perimeters of the two squares.

vg-051.statement: A figure is covered by 10 whole squares and 4 half squares. What is its area, in squares?
hints: Two halves make one whole square.

vg-052.statement: Two figures of different shapes are each covered by 8 identical squares. What do we know about their areas?
options: the wider figure has the greater area
the longer figure has the greater area
hints: Area shows how many squares cover the figure.
solution: Both are covered by 8 squares, so they have the same area, even though they have different shapes.

vg-053.statement: Figure A is covered by 20 identical squares, and figure B by 14 identical squares. By how many squares is the area of figure A greater?
hints: Subtract the areas.

vg-054.statement: A rectangle is covered by 3 rows of 5 squares each. How many squares cover it?
hints: Count by rows: 3 times 5.

vg-055.statement: A rectangle is covered by 24 squares, arranged in 4 equal rows. How many squares are in a row?
hints: Divide the squares by the number of rows.

vg-056.statement: A figure is made of a rectangle covered by 12 squares and a square covered by 4 squares, with no overlap. How many squares cover the whole figure?
hints: Add the areas of the two parts.

vg-057.statement: From a rectangle covered by 20 squares we cut out 3 squares. How many squares cover the remaining figure?
hints: Subtract the cut-out part.

vg-058.statement: A figure covered by 10 squares is cut into two pieces. One of the pieces has 4 squares. How many squares does the other have?
hints: The two pieces together have the area of the whole figure.
solution: 10 − 4 = 6. When you cut, the total area does not change.

vg-059.statement: In which situation do you need area, not perimeter?
options: you find out how much fence goes around the yard
you find out how far you run around a field
you find out how much tile covers the floor
you find out how much ribbon goes around a painting
hints: Area shows how much is covered, perimeter shows how much goes around.
solution: Tile covers the floor, so you need the area. The fence, the ribbon and running around the field are about perimeter.
Answer: you find out how much tile covers the floor.

vg-060.statement: A square is covered exactly by 9 squares with a side of 1 cm. What is its perimeter?
hints: The 9 squares sit in 3 rows of 3.
solution: The side of the square is 3 cm, and the perimeter is 4 × 3 = 12.

vg-061.statement: Two figures are each covered by 4 identical squares: one is a square, the other is a row of 4 squares. What do they have in common?
options: both the area and the perimeter
neither the area nor the perimeter
hints: Count the square sides along the outline.
solution: The area is the same: 4 squares. The outline of the square has 8 square sides, and that of the row has 10.
Figures with the same area can have different perimeters.

hints: It is round on all sides.
solution: The ball is round on all sides: it is shaped like a sphere.

vg-063.statement: What shape is a tin can?
hints: It has two round lids.
solution: The tin can has two round lids and can roll: it is a cylinder.

vg-064.statement: How many faces of a cube meet at a vertex?
hints: Look at the corner of a box.
solution: At each vertex of the cube 3 faces (and 3 edges) meet.

vg-065.statement: How many edges does a cuboid (rectangular prism) have?
hints: It has as many edges as the cube has.
solution: A cuboid has 12 edges: 4 on the bottom, 4 on top and 4 vertical.

vg-066.statement: How many vertices does a cone have?
hints: Think of a party hat.
solution: The cone has only one vertex and a base shaped like a circle.

vg-067.statement: How many vertices does a pyramid with a square base have?
hints: Count the corners of the base and the top vertex.
solution: The base has 4 vertices, and there is one more on top: 4 + 1 = 5.

vg-068.statement: What solid do you get if you fold 6 equal squares, placed the right way?
hints: The solid has 6 square faces.
solution: The solid with 6 equal square faces is the cube.

vg-069.statement: The net of a pyramid with a square base is made of the square of the base and how many triangles?
hints: Each side of the base has a triangular face above it.
solution: The base has 4 sides, so the pyramid has 4 triangular faces.

vg-070.statement: The net of a cube is made of squares with a side of 2 cm, each covered by 4 small squares with a side of 1 cm. How many small squares cover the whole net?
hints: The net of the cube has 6 squares.

vg-071.statement: A big cube has an edge made of 2 small cubes. How many small cubes is it made of?
hints: It has 2 layers of 2 × 2 cubes each.
solution: One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes, and two layers have 2 × 4 = 8.

vg-072.statement: A tower has 7 floors and a single cube on each floor. How many cubes is it made of?
hints: One cube per floor.

vg-073.statement: A solid is made of 3 layers of 4 cubes each. We take out one cube. How many cubes are left?
hints: First find how many cubes the whole solid has.

hints: Draw two bars: a shorter one and one that is 13 longer.
Subtract the difference from the sum, then divide by 2.

hints: If you add the difference to the sum, you get twice the greater number.
solution: Check: the smaller number is 106 − 56 = 50, and 106 + 50 = 156.

hints: If you subtract the difference from the sum, two equal parts remain, each equal to the smaller number.
solution: 115 − 5 = 110: this is two times the smaller number.
