solution: The common edge of the two planes is AB.
BC ⊥ AB (in the base) and BC′ ⊥ AB (AB ⊥ face BCC′B′) ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠C′BC = 45°.

cb-180.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the measure of the angle between the planes (D′AB) and (ABC)?
hints: A plane through three points may contain a whole section of the cube: look for the fourth vertex.
solution: The plane (D′AB) also contains the point C′ (ABC′D′ is a rectangle) ⇒ it is the same plane as (ABC′D′).
The edge shared with the base is AB; AD ⊥ AB and AD′ ⊥ AB ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠D′AD = 45°.

cb-181.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the measure of the angle between the planes (ACC′) and (BDD′)?
hints: Intersect the two planes with the plane of the base.
solution: The two diagonal planes intersect along the line OO′ (O, O′ the centers of the bases), perpendicular to the base.
In the base, AC ⊥ BD ⇒ the angle between the planes is 90°: the planes are perpendicular.

cb-182.statement: What is the measure of the dihedral angle between a lateral face and the base of a right prism?
hints: A right prism has its lateral edges perpendicular to the base.
solution: The lateral edges of a right prism are perpendicular to the base.
A lateral face contains a lateral edge ⇒ the face is perpendicular to the base: 90°.

cb-183.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the tangent of the angle between the planes (A′BD) and (ABD)?
hints: The plane angle of the dihedral: from the midpoint O of BD, AO in the base and A′O in the plane (A′BD).
solution: The common edge is BD; O is the center of the base. AO ⊥ BD, and A′O ⊥ BD (triangle A′BD is equilateral, A′O is a median).
The angle between the planes is ∠A′OA; tan ∠A′OA = AA′ ÷ AO = a ÷ (a√2/2) = 2/√2 = √2.

cb-184.statement: In the rectangular prism ABCDA′B′C′D′, AB = 5 cm, BC = 4 cm and AA′ = 4√3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes (ABC′) and (ABC).
hints: AB is the common edge; BC ⊥ AB and BC′ ⊥ AB.
solution: The angle between the planes is ∠C′BC (both of its sides are perpendicular to AB at B).

cb-185.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the line BD is perpendicular to the plane:
hints: A line is perpendicular to a plane if it is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in the plane.
solution: BD ⊥ AC (the diagonals of the square ABCD) and BD ⊥ AA′ (the edge AA′ is perpendicular to the base).
AC and AA′ are two intersecting lines in the plane (ACC′) ⇒ BD ⊥ (ACC′).

cb-186.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to the plane:
hints: Show that AC′ is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in the plane, for example BD and A′B.
solution: BD ⊥ (ACC′) ⇒ BD ⊥ AC′; likewise, A′B ⊥ (AB′C′) ⇒ A′B ⊥ AC′.
BD and A′B intersect in the plane (A′BD) ⇒ AC′ ⊥ (A′BD).

cb-187.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the edge AB is perpendicular to the plane:
hints: The edge AB is perpendicular to both of the other edges that start from B.
solution: AB ⊥ BC (in the square ABCD) and AB ⊥ BB′ (in the square ABB′A′).
BC and BB′ intersect in the plane (BCC′) ⇒ AB ⊥ (BCC′).

cb-188.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 5 cm. Find the distance from the point A′ to the plane of the base (ABC).
hints: A′A is perpendicular to the base.
solution: A′A ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the distance from A′ to the base is A′A = 5 cm.

cb-189.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 7 cm. Find the distance from the point A′ to the plane of the base (ABC).
hints: A′A is perpendicular to the base.
solution: A′A ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the distance from A′ to the base is A′A = 7 cm.

cb-190.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance from the point A to the plane (BCC′).
hints: AB is perpendicular to the face BCC′B′.
solution: AB ⊥ BC and AB ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ the distance is AB = 6 cm.

cb-191.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance from the point C to the plane (BDD′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: CO ⊥ BD (O is the center of the base) and CO ⊥ DD′.
solution: CO ⊥ BD (the diagonals of the square) and CO ⊥ DD′ ⇒ CO ⊥ (BDD′).

cb-192.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 8 cm. Find the distance from the point C to the plane (BDD′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: CO ⊥ BD (O is the center of the base) and CO ⊥ DD′.
solution: CO ⊥ BD (the diagonals of the square) and CO ⊥ DD′ ⇒ CO ⊥ (BDD′).

cb-193.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance from the point A to the plane (A′BD). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: Calculate the volume of the pyramid AA′BD in two ways: with the base ABD and with the base A′BD.
solution: Triangle A′BD is equilateral, with side 6√2 cm ⇒ area(A′BD) = 72 · √3 ÷ 4 = 18√3 cm².
d = 3 · V ÷ area(A′BD) = 108 ÷ (18√3) = 2√3 cm (that is, the diagonal of the cube divided by 3).

cb-194.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 9 cm. Find the distance from the point A to the plane (A′BD). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: Calculate the volume of the pyramid AA′BD in two ways: with the base ABD and with the base A′BD.
solution: Triangle A′BD is equilateral, with side 9√2 cm ⇒ area(A′BD) = 162 · √3 ÷ 4 = 40.5√3 cm².
d = 3 · V ÷ area(A′BD) = 364.5 ÷ (40.5√3) = 3√3 cm (that is, the diagonal of the cube divided by 3).

cb-195.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 3 cm. The diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD), and the distance from A to this plane is √3 cm. Find the distance from C′ to the plane (A′BD). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The plane (A′BD) cuts the diagonal AC′ at a point; what is left of the diagonal up to C′?
solution: AC′ = 3√3 cm and it is perpendicular to the plane, so the distances from A and from C′ to the plane are measured along AC′.
The distance from C′ = AC′ − √3 = 3√3 − √3 = 2√3 cm (the plane divides the diagonal in the ratio 1 to 2).

cb-196.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance from the point A to the plane (A′D′C). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The plane (A′D′C) also contains the point B: it is the diagonal plane A′BCD′.
solution: A′D′ ∥ BC ⇒ the plane (A′D′C) also contains B: it is the rectangle A′BCD′.
BC ⊥ face ABB′A′ ⇒ the perpendicular from A to A′B is perpendicular to the plane.
In the square ABB′A′, the distance from A to A′B is half of the diagonal AB′: 6√2 ÷ 2 = 3√2 cm.

cb-197.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 8 cm. Find the distance from the point A to the plane (A′D′C). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The plane (A′D′C) also contains the point B: it is the diagonal plane A′BCD′.
solution: A′D′ ∥ BC ⇒ the plane (A′D′C) also contains B: it is the rectangle A′BCD′.
BC ⊥ face ABB′A′ ⇒ the perpendicular from A to A′B is perpendicular to the plane.
In the square ABB′A′, the distance from A to A′B is half of the diagonal AB′: 8√2 ÷ 2 = 4√2 cm.

cb-198.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 4 cm, and O is the center of the face ABB′A′. Find the distance from O to the plane (BDD′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified (if there is no number in front of the radical, enter 1 as the coefficient).
hints: O is the midpoint of AB′; the distance from A to the plane (BDD′) is AO₁, where O₁ is the center of the base.
solution: The distance from A to (BDD′) is half of AC: 4√2 ÷ 2 = 2√2 cm; from B′ it is 0 (B′ is in the plane).
O is the midpoint of AB′ ⇒ the distance from O is half as much: 2√2 ÷ 2 = √2 cm.

cb-199.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 8 cm, and O is the center of the face ABB′A′. Find the distance from O to the plane (BDD′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: O is the midpoint of AB′; the distance from A to the plane (BDD′) is AO₁, where O₁ is the center of the base.
solution: The distance from A to (BDD′) is half of AC: 8√2 ÷ 2 = 4√2 cm; from B′ it is 0 (B′ is in the plane).
O is the midpoint of AB′ ⇒ the distance from O is half as much: 4√2 ÷ 2 = 2√2 cm.

cb-200.statement: The base ABCD of a rectangular prism has AB = 15 cm and BC = 20 cm. Find the distance from A to the line BD.
hints: In the right triangle ABD, the distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse: AB · AD ÷ BD.

cb-201.statement: The base ABCD of a rectangular prism has AB = 6 cm and BC = 8 cm. Find the distance from A to the line BD.
hints: In the right triangle ABD, the distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse: AB · AD ÷ BD.

cb-202.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 4 cm. Find the distance from A′ to the line BD. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: Let O be the center of the base: AO ⊥ BD and A′A ⊥ base ⇒ A′O ⊥ BD (theorem of three perpendiculars).
solution: AO = AC ÷ 2 = 2√2 cm, and AO ⊥ BD.
A′A ⊥ (ABC) and AO ⊥ BD ⇒ A′O ⊥ BD (theorem of three perpendiculars).

cb-203.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance from A′ to the line BD. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: Let O be the center of the base: AO ⊥ BD and A′A ⊥ base ⇒ A′O ⊥ BD (theorem of three perpendiculars).
solution: AO = AC ÷ 2 = 3√2 cm, and AO ⊥ BD.
A′A ⊥ (ABC) and AO ⊥ BD ⇒ A′O ⊥ BD (theorem of three perpendiculars).

cb-204.statement: In the rectangular prism ABCDA′B′C′D′, AB = 15 cm, AD = 20 cm and AA′ = 16 cm. Find the distance from A′ to the line BD.
hints: Construct AM ⊥ BD in the base; then A′M ⊥ BD by the theorem of three perpendiculars.

cb-205.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 5 cm. Find the distance from C′ to the line AB. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: AB ⊥ face BCC′B′, so AB ⊥ BC′.
solution: AB ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ AB ⊥ BC′ ⇒ the distance from C′ to AB is BC′.

cb-206.statement: How many faces does a rectangular prism have, and what shape are they?
hints: Opposite faces are congruent; the cube is a special case.
solution: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces (opposite faces are congruent). Only in a cube are they all squares.

cb-207.statement: A rectangular prism has a base that is a square with side 5 cm and a height of 5 cm. What solid is it?
hints: Compare the three dimensions.
solution: All three dimensions are equal (5 cm) ⇒ the solid is a cube.

cb-208.statement: In the rectangular prism ABCDA′B′C′D′, which edge is equal and parallel to the edge AA′, other than BB′, CC′ and DD′?
hints: The lateral edges are the 4 vertical edges.
solution: The edges equal and parallel to AA′ are only BB′, CC′ and DD′ (the lateral edges) ⇒ no other edge.

cb-209.statement: The frame of a rectangular prism with dimensions of 4 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm is made of wire. What length of wire is used?
hints: 4 edges of each dimension.

cb-210.statement: The frame of a rectangular prism with dimensions of 7 cm, 2 cm and 5 cm is made of wire. What length of wire is used?
hints: 4 edges of each dimension.

cb-211.statement: A rectangular prism has dimensions of 2 cm, 3 cm and 7 cm. What is the sum of the lengths of the edges?
hints: Each dimension appears 4 times.
solution: Careful: 24 = 2 · 12 counts each dimension only 2 times; 42 = 2 · 3 · 7 is the volume.

cb-212.statement: A rectangular prism has a base that is a square with side 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: The perimeter of the square base is 4 · side.

cb-213.statement: A rectangular prism has a base that is a square with side 9 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: The perimeter of the square base is 4 · side.

cb-214.statement: A rectangular prism has dimensions of 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. The base is the 2 cm by 3 cm face. What is the lateral surface area?
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height (here the height is 4 cm).
solution: Lateral surface area = 10 · 4 = 40 cm². (52 cm² is the total surface area, 24 cm³ the volume.)

cb-215.statement: Calculate the total surface area of a rectangular prism with a length of 6 cm, a width of 5 cm and a height of 4 cm.
hints: Lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.

cb-216.statement: Calculate the total surface area of a rectangular prism with a length of 12 cm, a width of 3 cm and a height of 2 cm.
hints: Lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.

cb-217.statement: The total surface area of a rectangular prism is 94 cm², and the lateral surface area is 70 cm². Find the area of the base.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.

cb-218.statement: A rectangular prism has a 4 cm by 3 cm base and a total surface area of 108 cm². Find the height.
hints: Subtract the two bases, then divide by the perimeter of the base.
solution: The two bases: 2 · 4 · 3 = 24 cm²; lateral surface area = 108 − 24 = 84 cm².
Perimeter of the base: 2 · (4 + 3) = 14 cm; height = 84 ÷ 14 = 6 cm.

cb-219.statement: In the rectangular prism ABCDA′B′C′D′, AB = 10 cm, BC = 9 cm and AA′ = 12 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the face BCC′B′.
hints: The face BCC′B′ has the sides BC and CC′.

cb-220.statement: In the rectangular prism ABCDA′B′C′D′, AB = 10 cm, BC = 8 cm and AA′ = 15 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the face BCC′B′.
hints: The face BCC′B′ has the sides BC and CC′.

cb-221.statement: A rectangular prism has dimensions of 3 cm, 4 cm and 12 cm. Which of the lengths is NOT the diagonal of a face?
hints: Face diagonals: √(3² + 4²), √(3² + 12²), √(4² + 12²).
solution: 13 cm = √(9 + 16 + 144) is the diagonal of the rectangular prism, not of a face.

cb-222.statement: Three cubes with an edge of 2 cm are glued one after another, in a straight line, along whole faces. Calculate the area of the outer surface of the resulting solid.
hints: The solid is a 6 cm × 2 cm × 2 cm rectangular prism.
solution: The rectangular prism has dimensions 6, 2, 2: total surface area = 2 · (12 + 4 + 12) = 56 cm².
Another way: 3 · 6 = 18 small faces, of which 4 are glued ⇒ 14 faces · 4 cm² = 56 cm².

cb-223.statement: A swimming pool has the shape of a rectangular prism, 25 m long, 10 m wide and 2 m deep. How many cubic meters of water does it hold?
hints: V = length · width · depth.

cb-224.statement: How many cubic decimeters are in 3 m³?
solution: 3 · 1000 = 3000 dm³. Between neighboring cubic units, the factor is 1000, not 10.

cb-225.statement: What shape are all the faces of a cube?
hints: A cube has all its edges equal and all the angles of its faces are right angles.
solution: A cube has 6 faces, all congruent squares (they have the same side: the edge of the cube).

cb-226.statement: Which of the objects has the shape of a cube?
hints: In a cube, the length, the width and the height are equal.
solution: The die has all three dimensions equal and square faces ⇒ a cube. The shoe box is a rectangular prism, the ball is a sphere, the ice cream cone is a cone.

cb-227.statement: A rectangular prism has all its edges equal. What solid is it?
hints: Compare with the definition of a cube.
solution: A rectangular prism with all its edges equal has congruent square faces ⇒ it is a cube.

cb-228.statement: The base of a cube is a square with side 7 cm. How long is a vertical edge of the cube?
hints: In a cube, all the edges are equal.
solution: All 12 edges of the cube are equal ⇒ the vertical edge is also 7 cm.

cb-229.statement: Which statement about the cube is false?
hints: Count the faces: bottom, top and the 4 lateral ones.
solution: The cube has 6 faces, not 8; the other statements are true (8 vertices, 12 equal edges, 6 square faces).

cb-230.statement: A cube is a right prism whose base is:
options: a square, with the height equal to the side of the base
hints: In a cube, all three dimensions are equal.
solution: A right prism with a square base is a regular square prism; it becomes a cube only when the height is equal to the side of the base.
Answer: a square, with the height equal to the side of the base.

cb-231.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, which face is parallel to the base ABCD?
hints: The top face is parallel to the base.
solution: The top face A′B′C′D′ is parallel to the base ABCD; the other faces in the list are lateral faces, perpendicular to the base.

cb-232.statement: What angle do two edges of a cube that start from the same vertex form?
hints: The faces of the cube are squares.
solution: Two edges that start from the same vertex are sides of a square face ⇒ they form a right angle: 90°.

pi-001.statement: How many edges does a quadrilateral pyramid have?
hints: Count the edges of the base and the lateral edges.
solution: The base has 4 edges, and 4 lateral edges start from the apex: 4 + 4 = 8.

pi-002.statement: How many vertices does a quadrilateral pyramid have?
hints: The vertices of the base and the apex of the pyramid.
solution: The base has 4 vertices, plus the apex of the pyramid: 4 + 1 = 5.

pi-003.statement: How many faces does a quadrilateral pyramid have (base included)?
hints: The base and the lateral faces.
solution: The base and 4 triangular lateral faces: 1 + 4 = 5 faces.

pi-004.statement: How many edges does a triangular pyramid have?
hints: 3 edges in the base and 3 lateral edges.

pi-005.statement: How many faces does a triangular pyramid have?
hints: The base and the 3 lateral faces.
solution: The base and 3 lateral faces: 1 + 3 = 4 faces. That is why a triangular pyramid is also called a tetrahedron (“four faces”).

pi-006.statement: How many edges does a hexagonal pyramid have?
hints: The base has 6 sides, and the same number of lateral edges start from the apex.

pi-007.statement: A pyramid has a base that is a polygon with 7 sides. How many edges does the pyramid have?
hints: A pyramid whose base is a polygon with n sides has 2n edges.

pi-008.statement: For a quadrilateral pyramid, calculate the number of vertices − the number of edges + the number of faces.
hints: A quadrilateral pyramid has 5 vertices, 8 edges and 5 faces.
solution: 5 − 8 + 5 = 2 (Euler's formula, as for any convex polyhedron).

pi-009.statement: What shape are the lateral faces of any pyramid?
hints: Each lateral face joins a side of the base to the apex.
solution: Each lateral face has as its vertices two neighboring vertices of the base and the apex of the pyramid ⇒ it is a triangle.

options: the height is equal to the side of the base
the base is a regular polygon and the foot of the height is the center of the base
hints: There are two conditions: one about the base, one about the height.
solution: A regular pyramid has a base that is a regular polygon, and the foot of the height is the center of the base (the center of the circle circumscribed about the base).
Answer: the base is a regular polygon and the foot of the height is the center of the base.

pi-011.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, where does the foot of the height from V fall?
options: at the midpoint of edge VC
at the midpoint of side AB
at the intersection point of the diagonals of the base
hints: The center of a square is the intersection of its diagonals.
solution: The base is the square ABCD, and its center is O, the intersection of the diagonals AC and BD ⇒ VO is the height.
Answer: at the intersection point of the diagonals of the base.

pi-012.statement: In the regular triangular pyramid VABC, the foot of the height from V is:
options: the midpoint of the altitude from A
the centroid of triangle ABC (the intersection of the medians)
hints: The base is an equilateral triangle: its center is also its centroid.
solution: The base ABC is an equilateral triangle; its center (the center of the circumscribed circle) coincides with the centroid, which lies on each median two thirds of the way from the vertex.
Answer: the centroid of triangle ABC (the intersection of the medians).

pi-013.statement: What shape are the lateral faces of a regular pyramid?
hints: The lateral edges of a regular pyramid are equal.
solution: The lateral edges are equal (VA = VB = …), and the sides of the base are equal ⇒ the lateral faces are congruent isosceles triangles. They are equilateral only if the lateral edge is equal to the side of the base.

pi-014.statement: Which statement about a regular square pyramid is true?
options: the base can be any rectangle
all the lateral edges are equal
all the edges are equal, always
hints: Think about the right triangles VOA, VOB…
solution: VO is perpendicular to the base, and OA = OB = OC = OD ⇒ triangles VOA, VOB, VOC, VOD are congruent ⇒ VA = VB = VC = VD.
Answer: all the lateral edges are equal.

options: a triangular pyramid with all 6 edges equal
a quadrilateral pyramid with all edges equal
hints: In a regular tetrahedron, all the faces are equilateral triangles.
solution: A regular tetrahedron has all 6 edges equal, so all 4 faces are congruent equilateral triangles.
Answer: a triangular pyramid with all 6 edges equal.

pi-016.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has AB = 6 cm and VA = 10 cm. Is it a regular tetrahedron?
options: yes, every regular triangular pyramid is a regular tetrahedron
no, the lateral edges are not equal to the sides of the base
hints: In a regular tetrahedron, all 6 edges are equal.
solution: It is a tetrahedron (it has 4 faces), but not a regular one: VA = 10 cm ≠ AB = 6 cm. The lateral faces are isosceles, not equilateral.
Answer: no, the lateral edges are not equal to the sides of the base.

pi-017.statement: How many edges does a regular tetrahedron have, and how long are they?
options: 6 edges: the 3 base edges equal to each other, the 3 lateral edges longer
hints: The tetrahedron has 4 vertices; each pair of vertices forms an edge.
solution: From 4 vertices you can form 6 pairs ⇒ 6 edges, all equal in a regular tetrahedron.

pi-018.statement: A regular tetrahedron has an edge of 4 cm. Find the sum of the lengths of all the edges.
hints: The tetrahedron has 6 equal edges (not 4).

pi-019.statement: A regular tetrahedron has an edge of 7 cm. Find the sum of the lengths of all the edges.
hints: The tetrahedron has 6 equal edges (not 4).

pi-020.statement: A regular tetrahedron has an edge of 2.5 cm. Find the sum of the lengths of all the edges.
hints: The tetrahedron has 6 equal edges (not 4).

pi-021.statement: The sum of the lengths of the edges of a regular tetrahedron is 36 cm. What is the length of one edge?
hints: Divide by the number of edges: 6.
solution: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 cm. Careful: 9 cm would come from dividing by 4 (the number of faces), 12 cm from dividing by 3.

pi-022.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, M is the midpoint of BC. What is the segment VM called?
options: the slant height of the pyramid
hints: VM is the altitude of the lateral face VBC.
solution: VM is the altitude of the isosceles triangle VBC (M the midpoint of the base BC) ⇒ VM is the slant height of the pyramid. OM is the apothem of the base, VO the height of the pyramid, VB a lateral edge.
Answer: the slant height of the pyramid.

pi-023.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, O is the center of the base and M is the midpoint of BC. What is the segment OM called?
options: the slant height of the pyramid
the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base
hints: OM is the distance from the center of the square to a side.
solution: OM ⊥ BC and O is the center of the square ⇒ OM is the apothem of the base (half the side). OA is the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base.
Answer: the apothem of the base.

pi-024.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm. Find the apothem of the base (the distance from the center O of the base to side BC).
hints: For a square, the apothem is half the side.

pi-025.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 10 cm. Find the apothem of the base (the distance from the center O of the base to side BC).
hints: For a square, the apothem is half the side.

pi-026.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 14 cm. Find the apothem of the base (the distance from the center O of the base to side BC).
hints: For a square, the apothem is half the side.

pi-027.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OA is half of the diagonal of the square: AC = AB · √2.
solution: AC = 6√2 cm, and O is the midpoint of AC.

pi-028.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 8 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OA is half of the diagonal of the square: AC = AB · √2.
solution: AC = 8√2 cm, and O is the midpoint of AC.

pi-029.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 10 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OA is half of the diagonal of the square: AC = AB · √2.
solution: AC = 10√2 cm, and O is the midpoint of AC.

pi-030.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6 cm, O is the center of the base and M is the midpoint of BC. Find the apothem of the base OM. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified (if there is no number in front of the radical, enter 1 as the coefficient).
hints: OM is one third of the height of the equilateral triangle: height = side · √3 ÷ 2.
solution: The height of triangle ABC: AM = 6 · √3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm.
OM = AM ÷ 3 = √3 cm (the centroid divides the median in the ratio 2 to 1).

pi-031.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OA = two thirds of the height of the equilateral triangle.
solution: The height of triangle ABC is 6 · √3 ÷ 2; OA is two thirds of it, that is, twice the apothem of the base.

pi-032.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 12 cm, O is the center of the base and M is the midpoint of BC. Find the apothem of the base OM. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OM is one third of the height of the equilateral triangle: height = side · √3 ÷ 2.
solution: The height of triangle ABC: AM = 12 · √3 ÷ 2 = 6√3 cm.
OM = AM ÷ 3 = 2√3 cm (the centroid divides the median in the ratio 2 to 1).

pi-033.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 12 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: OA = two thirds of the height of the equilateral triangle.
solution: The height of triangle ABC is 12 · √3 ÷ 2; OA is two thirds of it, that is, twice the apothem of the base.

pi-034.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6√3 cm, O is the center of the base and M is the midpoint of BC. Find the apothem of the base OM.
hints: OM is one third of the height of the equilateral triangle: height = side · √3 ÷ 2.
solution: The height of triangle ABC: AM = 6√3 · √3 ÷ 2 = 9 cm.
OM = AM ÷ 3 = 3 cm (the centroid divides the median in the ratio 2 to 1).

pi-035.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6√3 cm, and O is the center of the base. Find the length OA (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base).
hints: OA = two thirds of the height of the equilateral triangle.
solution: The height of triangle ABC is 6√3 · √3 ÷ 2; OA is two thirds of it, that is, twice the apothem of the base.

pi-036.statement: In the regular triangular pyramid VABC, the apothem of the base is 2 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base?
hints: In an equilateral triangle, the radius of the circumscribed circle is twice the apothem.
solution: The centroid divides the median in the ratio 2 to 1 ⇒ radius = 2 · apothem = 4 cm. The height of the triangle is 3 · 2 = 6 cm.

pi-037.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height VO of 4 cm. Find the slant height of the pyramid VM (M the midpoint of BC).
hints: Triangle VOM is right-angled at O, and OM is half of the base side.

pi-038.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 8 cm and a height VO of 3 cm. Find the slant height of the pyramid VM (M the midpoint of BC).
hints: Triangle VOM is right-angled at O, and OM is half of the base side.

pi-039.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 10 cm and a height VO of 12 cm. Find the slant height of the pyramid VM (M the midpoint of BC).
hints: Triangle VOM is right-angled at O, and OM is half of the base side.

pi-040.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 16 cm and a height VO of 6 cm. Find the slant height of the pyramid VM (M the midpoint of BC).
hints: Triangle VOM is right-angled at O, and OM is half of the base side.

pi-041.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a slant height VM of 10 cm. Find the height VO of the pyramid.
hints: In triangle VOM, right-angled at O, VM is the hypotenuse.

pi-042.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 24 cm and a slant height VM of 13 cm. Find the height VO of the pyramid.
hints: In triangle VOM, right-angled at O, VM is the hypotenuse.

pi-043.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a height of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Find the base side.
hints: First find the apothem of the base OM, then the side = 2 · OM.

pi-044.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, VO is the height and M the midpoint of BC. Which triangle is right-angled at O?
hints: VO is perpendicular to the plane of the base, so it is perpendicular to every line in the base that passes through O.
solution: VO ⊥ (ABC) and OM lies in the plane of the base ⇒ VO ⊥ OM ⇒ triangle VOM is right-angled at O. (Triangle VMB is right-angled at M.)

hints: Apothem of the base OM = side · √3 ÷ 6.

pi-145.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6√3 cm and a height of √3 cm. Find the measure of the dihedral angle between the face VBC and the plane of the base.
hints: Apothem of the base OM = side · √3 ÷ 6.

pi-146.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has a base side of 6√3 cm and a height of 3√3 cm. Find the measure of the dihedral angle between the face VBC and the plane of the base.
hints: Apothem of the base OM = side · √3 ÷ 6.

pi-147.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3√3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes of the opposite faces (VAD) and (VBC).
hints: The common line of the two planes passes through V and is parallel to AD; the slant heights VR and VM (R, M the midpoints of AD and BC) are perpendicular to it.
solution: AD ∥ BC ⇒ the planes intersect along the line d through V, parallel to AD; VR ⊥ d and VM ⊥ d ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠RVM.
VR = VM = 6 cm, RM = 6 cm. Triangle RVM is equilateral ⇒ 60°.

pi-148.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes of the opposite faces (VAD) and (VBC).
hints: The common line of the two planes passes through V and is parallel to AD; the slant heights VR and VM (R, M the midpoints of AD and BC) are perpendicular to it.
solution: AD ∥ BC ⇒ the planes intersect along the line d through V, parallel to AD; VR ⊥ d and VM ⊥ d ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠RVM.
VR = VM = 3√2 cm, RM = 6 cm. VR² + VM² = 18 + 18 = 36 = RM² ⇒ ∠RVM = 90°: the planes are perpendicular.

pi-149.statement: What is the cosine of the dihedral angle between two faces of a regular tetrahedron?
hints: On the edge BC, from the midpoint M: AM and DM are perpendicular to BC; in triangle AMD, MO = AM ÷ 3.
solution: The plane angle of the dihedral is ∠DMA, with M the midpoint of BC.
O (the foot of the height from D) lies on AM, with MO = AM ÷ 3 = DM ÷ 3 ⇒ cos ∠DMO = MO ÷ DM = 1/3.

pi-150.statement: In a regular tetrahedron, what is the tangent of the angle between a lateral edge and the plane of the base?
hints: With edge l: OA = l√3 ÷ 3, height DO = l√6 ÷ 3.

pi-151.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Find the distance from the center O of the base to the plane of the face VBC.
hints: Let M be the midpoint of BC and T the foot of the perpendicular from O to VM: BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT, so OT ⊥ (VBC).
solution: OM = 3 cm, VM = 5 cm (from triangle VOM).
BC ⊥ OM and BC ⊥ VO ⇒ BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT; since OT ⊥ VM, OT ⊥ (VBC).
d = OT = VO · OM ÷ VM = 4 · 3 ÷ 5 = 2.4 cm.

pi-152.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 16 cm and a height of 6 cm. Find the distance from the center O of the base to the plane of the face VBC.
hints: Let M be the midpoint of BC and T the foot of the perpendicular from O to VM: BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT, so OT ⊥ (VBC).
solution: OM = 8 cm, VM = 10 cm (from triangle VOM).
BC ⊥ OM and BC ⊥ VO ⇒ BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT; since OT ⊥ VM, OT ⊥ (VBC).
d = OT = VO · OM ÷ VM = 6 · 8 ÷ 10 = 4.8 cm.

pi-153.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a height of 8 cm. Find the distance from the center O of the base to the plane of the face VBC.
hints: Let M be the midpoint of BC and T the foot of the perpendicular from O to VM: BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT, so OT ⊥ (VBC).
solution: OM = 6 cm, VM = 10 cm (from triangle VOM).
BC ⊥ OM and BC ⊥ VO ⇒ BC ⊥ (VOM) ⇒ BC ⊥ OT; since OT ⊥ VM, OT ⊥ (VBC).
d = OT = VO · OM ÷ VM = 8 · 6 ÷ 10 = 4.8 cm.

pi-154.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 10 cm and a height of 12 cm. Find the distance from the center O of the base to the plane of the face VBC. Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: OT = VO · OM ÷ VM, with VM from triangle VOM.

pi-155.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Find the distance from the vertex A to the plane (VBC).
hints: O is the midpoint of AC, and C lies in the plane (VBC): the distance from A is twice the distance from O.
solution: A, O, C are collinear, O is the midpoint of AC and C ∈ (VBC) ⇒ d(A, (VBC)) = 2 · 2.4 = 4.8 cm.

pi-156.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 8 cm and a height of 3 cm. Find the distance from the vertex A to the plane (VBC).
hints: O is the midpoint of AC, and C lies in the plane (VBC): the distance from A is twice the distance from O.
solution: A, O, C are collinear, O is the midpoint of AC and C ∈ (VBC) ⇒ d(A, (VBC)) = 2 · 2.4 = 4.8 cm.

pi-157.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a height of 3 cm. Find the distance from the center O of the base to the edge VA. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: In triangle VOA, right-angled at O, the distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse.

pi-158.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, the diagonal BD of the base is perpendicular to the plane:
hints: BD is perpendicular to AC (the diagonals of the square) and to VO (the height).
solution: BD ⊥ AC and BD ⊥ VO, and AC and VO intersect at O, in the plane (VAC) ⇒ BD ⊥ (VAC).

pi-159.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, what is the measure of the angle between the lines BD and VC?
hints: BD is perpendicular to the plane (VAC), which contains VC.
solution: BD ⊥ (VAC) and VC lies in the plane (VAC) ⇒ BD ⊥ VC: the angle is 90°.

pi-160.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the area of the diagonal section VAC. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: The section VAC is a triangle with base AC (the diagonal of the square) and height VO.

pi-161.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 10 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the area of the diagonal section VAC. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: The section VAC is a triangle with base AC (the diagonal of the square) and height VO.

pi-162.statement: A regular square pyramid with a base side of 8 cm is cut by a plane parallel to the base, through the midpoint of the height. Calculate the area of the section.
hints: The section is a square whose side is half of the base side (a midsegment in the lateral faces).
solution: Side of the section = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm (a midsegment in triangle VAB).

pi-163.statement: A regular square pyramid with a base side of 10 cm is cut by a plane parallel to the base, through the midpoint of the height. Calculate the area of the section.
hints: The section is a square whose side is half of the base side (a midsegment in the lateral faces).
solution: Side of the section = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm (a midsegment in triangle VAB).

pi-164.statement: A pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to the base, through the midpoint of the height. What fraction of the volume of the large pyramid is the volume of the small pyramid on top? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The small pyramid is similar to the large one, with ratio 1/2; the volumes are in the ratio (1/2)³.
solution: The similarity ratio is 1/2 ⇒ the ratio of the areas of the bases is 1/4, and the ratio of the volumes is (1/2)³ = 1/8.

pi-165.statement: A tent has the shape of a regular square pyramid without a base, with a base side of 4 m and a height of 1.5 m. How many m² of canvas does the tent have (without a floor)?
hints: Canvas = lateral surface area; first find the slant height from VO = 1.5 m and OM = 2 m.

pi-166.statement: The tent, shaped like a regular square pyramid, has a base side of 4 m and a height of 1.5 m. How many m³ of air fit in the tent?
hints: V = area of the base · height ÷ 3.

pi-167.statement: The roof of a gazebo has the shape of a regular square pyramid with a base side of 6 m and a slant height of 5 m. How many m² of roof tiles are needed?
hints: The tiles cover only the lateral faces.

pi-168.statement: Which of these pyramids is definitely regular?
options: a square base, with the height falling at the center of the square
an isosceles triangle base, with equal lateral edges
a rectangle base, with equal lateral edges
a rhombus base, with the height falling at the center of the rhombus
hints: The base of a regular pyramid must be a regular polygon.
solution: Of the bases in the options, only the square is a regular polygon; with the height at its center, the pyramid is regular.
Answer: a square base, with the height falling at the center of the square.

pi-169.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, the edge VA is 10 cm. What is the length of the edge VC?
hints: The lateral edges of a regular pyramid are equal.
solution: Triangles VOA and VOC are congruent (VO is common, OA = OC) ⇒ VC = VA = 10 cm.

pi-170.statement: How many lines of symmetry does the base of a regular square pyramid have?
hints: The base is a square.
solution: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: the two diagonals and the two perpendicular bisectors of the sides.

pi-171.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 12 · 10 ÷ 2 = 240 cm²; area of the base: 12² = 144 cm².

pi-172.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 24 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 24 · 13 ÷ 2 = 624 cm²; area of the base: 24² = 576 cm².

pr-001.statement: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
hints: 3 edges at the bottom, 3 at the top and 3 lateral edges.
solution: The bottom base has 3 edges, the top base 3, and between them there are 3 lateral edges: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

pr-002.statement: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
hints: The vertices of the two bases.

pr-003.statement: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
hints: The two bases and the lateral faces.

pr-004.statement: How many edges does a hexagonal prism have?
solution: 6 edges at the bottom, 6 at the top and 6 lateral edges: 18 edges.

pr-005.statement: How many faces does a hexagonal prism have?
hints: 2 bases and one lateral face for each side of the base.

pr-006.statement: A prism has a base that is a polygon with 5 sides. How many vertices does the prism have?
hints: Each base has 5 vertices.
solution: 5 vertices at the bottom + 5 vertices at the top = 10 vertices.

pr-007.statement: For a triangular prism, calculate the number of vertices − the number of edges + the number of faces.
hints: 6 vertices, 9 edges, 5 faces.

pr-008.statement: What shape are the two bases of a prism?
options: two congruent polygons, in parallel planes
hints: Think of a box: the bottom and the lid.
solution: The bases of a prism are two congruent polygons lying in parallel planes; the lateral edges are parallel and equal.
Answer: two congruent polygons, in parallel planes.

options: the lateral edges are perpendicular to the plane of the base
hints: “Right” refers to the lateral edges.
solution: A right prism has its lateral edges perpendicular to the bases; that is why its lateral faces are rectangles, and its height is equal to the lateral edge.
Answer: the lateral edges are perpendicular to the plane of the base.

pr-010.statement: What shape are the lateral faces of a right prism?
hints: The lateral edge is perpendicular to the side of the base.
solution: Each lateral face has two sides on the bases and two lateral edges perpendicular to them ⇒ it is a rectangle.

pr-011.statement: In the right prism ABCA′B′C′, the lateral edge AA′ is 9 cm long. What is the height of the prism?
hints: In a right prism, the lateral edge is perpendicular to the base.
solution: AA′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the height of the prism is the lateral edge itself: 9 cm.

pr-012.statement: A right prism whose base is an equilateral triangle is called:
hints: A regular prism = a right prism whose base is a regular polygon.
solution: An equilateral triangle is a regular polygon ⇒ a right prism whose base is an equilateral triangle is the regular triangular prism.

pr-013.statement: Which solid is a regular square prism?
options: the right prism whose base is a rhombus of any kind
the pyramid whose base is a square
the right prism whose base is a square
the right prism whose base is a rectangle of any kind
hints: The base must be a regular polygon with 4 sides.
solution: The only regular quadrilateral is the square ⇒ the regular square prism is the right prism whose base is a square (the cube is a special case).
Answer: the right prism whose base is a square.

pr-014.statement: In the regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′, AB = 6 cm. What is BC?
hints: The base is an equilateral triangle.
solution: The base ABC is an equilateral triangle ⇒ BC = AB = 6 cm.

pr-015.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCDEF has the face DEF above the base ABC (D above A, E above B). Which edge is parallel to AD?
hints: The lateral edges of a prism are parallel.
solution: AD, BE and CF are the lateral edges ⇒ they are parallel: AD ∥ CF.

pr-016.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the equilateral triangle = side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-017.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 4 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the equilateral triangle = side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-018.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 2√3 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the equilateral triangle = side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-019.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 10 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the equilateral triangle = side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-020.statement: A regular hexagonal prism has a base side of 2 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles whose side is equal to the base side.

pr-021.statement: A regular hexagonal prism has a base side of 4 cm. Calculate the area of the base. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles whose side is equal to the base side.

pr-022.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-023.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-024.statement: A regular square prism has a base side of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-025.statement: A regular hexagonal prism has a base side of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-026.statement: A regular hexagonal prism has a base side of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-027.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 5 cm and a lateral surface area of 180 cm². Find the height.
hints: Lateral surface area = perimeter of the base · height.

pr-028.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is the lateral surface area?
hints: There are 3 lateral faces, each a rectangle of 4 cm by 5 cm.
solution: Watch out: 20 cm² is the area of a single face; 80 cm² would be for 4 faces.

pr-029.statement: A regular square prism has a base side of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 5 · 8 = 160 cm²; area of the base: 5² = 25 cm².

pr-030.statement: A regular square prism has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 4 · 10 = 160 cm²; area of the base: 4² = 16 cm².

pr-031.statement: A regular square prism has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 6 · 3 = 72 cm²; area of the base: 6² = 36 cm².

pr-032.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is the total surface area?
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the TWO bases.
solution: Lateral surface area = 3 · 6 · 10 = 180 cm²; area of one base = 36 · √3 ÷ 4 = 9√3 cm².
Total surface area = 180 + 2 · 9√3 = (180 + 18√3) cm². Watch out: only one base (180 + 9√3), only the lateral surface area (180).

pr-033.statement: The total surface area of a regular square prism is 192 cm², and the base side is 4 cm. Find the height.
hints: Subtract the two bases, then divide by the perimeter of the base.
solution: The two bases: 2 · 16 = 32 cm²; lateral surface area = 192 − 32 = 160 cm².

pr-034.statement: Which formula gives the total surface area of a prism?
options: lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base
lateral surface area + area of the base
hints: A prism has two bases.
solution: A prism has two congruent bases ⇒ total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base. (Area of the base · height is the volume; perimeter of the base · height is the lateral surface area.)
Answer: lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.

pr-035.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular triangular prism with a base side of 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. Write the result as a√b cm³, with the radical simplified.
hints: Volume of the prism = area of the base · height.

pr-036.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular triangular prism with a base side of 4 cm and a height of 2√3 cm.
hints: Volume of the prism = area of the base · height.

pr-037.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular triangular prism with a base side of 2√3 cm and a height of 8 cm. Write the result as a√b cm³, with the radical simplified.
hints: Volume of the prism = area of the base · height.

pr-038.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular triangular prism with a base side of 6 cm and a height of 4√3 cm.
hints: Volume of the prism = area of the base · height.

pr-039.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular square prism with a base side of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm.
hints: V = area of the base · height.

pr-040.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular square prism with a base side of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm.
hints: V = area of the base · height.

pr-041.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular hexagonal prism with a base side of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm. Write the result as a√b cm³, with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the regular hexagon = 6 · side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-042.statement: Calculate the volume of the regular hexagonal prism with a base side of 4 cm and a height of √3 cm.
hints: Area of the regular hexagon = 6 · side² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-043.statement: A prism has a base area of 15 cm² and a volume of 120 cm³. Find the height.
hints: The height is the volume divided by the area of the base.

pr-044.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 2√3 cm. What is its volume?
hints: Area of the base = 4² · √3 ÷ 4 = 4√3 cm².
solution: Watch out: 8 cm³ comes from dividing by 3 (as for a pyramid), 24√3 comes from forgetting that √3 · √3 = 3.

pr-045.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the lateral face BCC′B′.
hints: The lateral face is a rectangle with sides BC and CC′.

pr-046.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the lateral face BCC′B′.
hints: The lateral face is a rectangle with sides BC and CC′.

pr-047.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the lateral face BCC′B′.
hints: The lateral face is a rectangle with sides BC and CC′.

pr-048.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Find the length of the diagonal BC′ of the lateral face BCC′B′.
hints: The lateral face is a rectangle with sides BC and CC′.

pr-049.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 7 cm. Find the length of the diagonal AC′ of the prism.
hints: AC′² = AC² + CC′², where AC is the diagonal of the square.

pr-050.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 7 cm. Find the length of the diagonal AC′ of the prism.
hints: AC′² = AC² + CC′², where AC is the diagonal of the square.

pr-051.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 2 cm and a height of 1 cm. Find the length of the diagonal AC′ of the prism.
hints: AC′² = AC² + CC′², where AC is the diagonal of the square.

pr-052.statement: The regular hexagonal prism ABCDEFA′B′C′D′E′F′ has a base side of 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. Find the length of the diagonal AD′.
hints: AD is the long diagonal of the hexagon: AD = 2 · side.

pr-053.statement: The regular hexagonal prism ABCDEFA′B′C′D′E′F′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 5 cm. Find the length of the diagonal AD′.
hints: AD is the long diagonal of the hexagon: AD = 2 · side.

pr-054.statement: A regular triangular prism has a base side of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the length of the diagonal of a lateral face?
hints: The Pythagorean theorem in the rectangle of the face.

pr-055.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 6√3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the line AB′ and the plane of the base.
hints: The projection of B′ onto the base is B: the angle we want is ∠B′AB.
solution: BB′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the projection of AB′ onto the base is AB ⇒ the angle we want is ∠B′AB.

pr-056.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 6 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the line AB′ and the plane of the base.
hints: The projection of B′ onto the base is B: the angle we want is ∠B′AB.
solution: BB′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the projection of AB′ onto the base is AB ⇒ the angle we want is ∠B′AB.

pr-057.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 2√3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the line AB′ and the plane of the base.
hints: The projection of B′ onto the base is B: the angle we want is ∠B′AB.
solution: BB′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the projection of AB′ onto the base is AB ⇒ the angle we want is ∠B′AB.

pr-058.statement: In the regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′, what is the projection of the point A onto the plane of the lateral face (BCC′)?
options: the center of the base ABC
hints: AM ⊥ BC (a median in the equilateral triangle) and AM ⊥ BB′.
solution: AM ⊥ BC and AM ⊥ BB′ (BB′ is perpendicular to the base), and BC and BB′ intersect in the plane (BCC′) ⇒ AM ⊥ (BCC′): the projection of A is M.
Answer: the midpoint M of BC.

pr-059.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 6√2 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the line AB′ and the plane of the lateral face (BCC′).
hints: The projection of A onto the plane (BCC′) is M, the midpoint of BC: the angle we want is ∠AB′M.
solution: AM ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ the angle we want is ∠AB′M, where AM = 3√3 cm.

pr-060.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 2√2 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the line AB′ and the plane of the lateral face (BCC′).
hints: The projection of A onto the plane (BCC′) is M, the midpoint of BC: the angle we want is ∠AB′M.
solution: AM ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ the angle we want is ∠AB′M, where AM = 2√3 cm.

pr-061.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3√3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes (ABC′) and (ABC).
hints: Let K be the midpoint of AB: CK ⊥ AB and C′K ⊥ AB, so the angle between the planes is ∠C′KC.
solution: CK = 6 · √3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm (the altitude of the equilateral triangle).

pr-062.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 9 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes (ABC′) and (ABC).
hints: Let K be the midpoint of AB: CK ⊥ AB and C′K ⊥ AB, so the angle between the planes is ∠C′KC.
solution: CK = 6 · √3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm (the altitude of the equilateral triangle).

pr-063.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the planes (ABC′) and (ABC).
hints: Let K be the midpoint of AB: CK ⊥ AB and C′K ⊥ AB, so the angle between the planes is ∠C′KC.
solution: CK = 6 · √3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm (the altitude of the equilateral triangle).

pr-064.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 4√2 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the diagonal AC′ and the plane of the base.
hints: The angle we want is ∠C′AC, where AC is the diagonal of the square.

pr-065.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 6√6 cm. Find the measure of the angle between the diagonal AC′ and the plane of the base.
hints: The angle we want is ∠C′AC, where AC is the diagonal of the square.

pr-066.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm. Find the distance from the vertex A to the plane of the lateral face (BCC′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: AM ⊥ (BCC′), where M is the midpoint of BC; AM is the altitude of the equilateral triangle.
solution: AM ⊥ BC and AM ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AM ⊥ (BCC′).

pr-067.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 4 cm. Find the distance from the vertex A to the plane of the lateral face (BCC′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: AM ⊥ (BCC′), where M is the midpoint of BC; AM is the altitude of the equilateral triangle.
solution: AM ⊥ BC and AM ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AM ⊥ (BCC′).

pr-068.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 8 cm. Find the distance from the vertex A to the plane of the lateral face (BCC′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: AM ⊥ (BCC′), where M is the midpoint of BC; AM is the altitude of the equilateral triangle.
solution: AM ⊥ BC and AM ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AM ⊥ (BCC′).

pr-069.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm. What is the distance between the edge AA′ and the plane of the face (BCC′)?
hints: AA′ is parallel to the plane (BCC′): all its points are at the same distance from it.
solution: AA′ ∥ BB′ ⊂ (BCC′) ⇒ AA′ ∥ (BCC′); the distance is the distance from A to the plane: AM = 6 · √3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm.

pr-070.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 9 cm. Find the distance from the vertex C to the plane (ABC′).
hints: Let K be the midpoint of AB: AB ⊥ (CC′K); the distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse in triangle C′CK.
solution: AB ⊥ CK and AB ⊥ CC′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (CC′K); the perpendicular from C to C′K is perpendicular to the plane (ABC′).

pr-071.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 2 cm. Find the distance from the vertex C to the plane (ABC′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified (if there is no number in front of the radical, enter 1 as the coefficient).
hints: Let K be the midpoint of AB: AB ⊥ (CC′K); the distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse in triangle C′CK.
solution: AB ⊥ CK and AB ⊥ CC′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (CC′K); the perpendicular from C to C′K is perpendicular to the plane (ABC′).

pr-072.statement: The regular hexagonal prism ABCDEFA′B′C′D′E′F′ has a base side of 2 cm. Find the distance between the planes of the opposite lateral faces (ABB′) and (DEE′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The distance between two opposite sides of a regular hexagon is twice the apothem: side · √3.
solution: The sides AB and DE are opposite in the hexagon; the distance between them is 2 · apothem = 2 · 2 · √3 ÷ 2 = 2√3 cm.
The lateral faces are perpendicular to the base ⇒ the distance between the planes is the same: 2√3 cm.

pr-073.statement: The regular hexagonal prism ABCDEFA′B′C′D′E′F′ has a base side of 4 cm. Find the distance between the planes of the opposite lateral faces (ABB′) and (DEE′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The distance between two opposite sides of a regular hexagon is twice the apothem: side · √3.
solution: The sides AB and DE are opposite in the hexagon; the distance between them is 2 · apothem = 2 · 4 · √3 ÷ 2 = 4√3 cm.
The lateral faces are perpendicular to the base ⇒ the distance between the planes is the same: 4√3 cm.

pr-074.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a height of 7 cm. What is the distance from the point A′ to the plane of the base (ABC)?
hints: A′A is perpendicular to the plane of the base.
solution: A′A ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the distance from A′ to the base is A′A = 7 cm (the height of the prism).

pr-075.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 7 cm. Calculate the area of the diagonal section ACC′A′. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: The section is a rectangle with sides AC and AA′.

pr-076.statement: The regular square prism ABCDA′B′C′D′ has a base side of 5 cm and a height of 3√2 cm. Calculate the area of the diagonal section ACC′A′.
hints: The section is a rectangle with sides AC and AA′.

pr-077.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 3 cm. Calculate the area of triangle ABC′.
hints: Triangle ABC′ is isosceles; its altitude is C′K, where K is the midpoint of AB.

pr-078.statement: The regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′ has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 2 cm. Calculate the area of triangle ABC′.
hints: Triangle ABC′ is isosceles; its altitude is C′K, where K is the midpoint of AB.

pr-079.statement: A regular triangular prism is cut by a plane parallel to the bases. What figure is the section?
options: an equilateral triangle smaller than the base
an equilateral triangle congruent to the base
hints: The lateral edges are parallel and equal.
solution: The plane parallel to the base cuts the lateral edges at points that form a triangle congruent to the base (in a prism, unlike in a pyramid, the section does not get smaller).
Answer: an equilateral triangle congruent to the base.

pr-080.statement: A chocolate box has the shape of a regular triangular prism with a base side of 4 cm and a length (the height of the prism) of 20 cm. Calculate the volume of the box. Write the result as a√b cm³, with the radical simplified.
hints: V = area of the base · height; area of the base = 4² · √3 ÷ 4.

pr-081.statement: The attic of a house has the shape of a right triangular prism: the base is an isosceles triangle with a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m, and the length of the attic is 10 m. How many m³ of air does the attic hold?
hints: Area of the triangle = base · height ÷ 2.
solution: Area of the base of the prism: 8 · 3 ÷ 2 = 12 m².

pr-082.statement: A pillar has the shape of a regular hexagonal prism with a base side of 10 cm and a height of 2 m. Only the lateral faces are painted. How many m² are painted?
hints: Work in meters: 10 cm = 0.1 m.

pr-083.statement: In a right prism, what angle does a lateral edge make with the plane of the base?
hints: A right prism has its lateral edges perpendicular to the base.
solution: The lateral edges of a right prism are perpendicular to the base ⇒ the angle is 90°.

pr-084.statement: A right prism whose base is a rectangle is called:
hints: It is the shape of a shoebox.
solution: A right prism whose base is a rectangle is the rectangular prism (the cube, when all the edges are equal).

pr-085.statement: Is a cube a right prism?
options: no, a cube is a pyramid
yes, its lateral edges are perpendicular to the base
only if the edge is longer than 1 cm
no, a prism must have a triangular base
hints: Check the definition of a right prism.
solution: A cube has two congruent, parallel square bases, and its lateral edges are perpendicular to them ⇒ it is a right prism (even a regular one).
Answer: yes, its lateral edges are perpendicular to the base.

pr-086.statement: In the right prism ABCDEF, the lateral edge AD is 12 cm long (D above A). What is the height of the prism?
hints: The lateral edge of a right prism is perpendicular to the base.
solution: AD ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the height of the prism is AD = 12 cm.

pr-087.statement: How many lateral faces does a right pentagonal prism have, and what shape are they?
hints: One lateral face for each side of the base.
solution: The base has 5 sides ⇒ 5 lateral faces; since the prism is right, they are rectangles.

pr-088.statement: How many lines of symmetry does the base of a regular triangular prism have?
hints: The base is an equilateral triangle.
solution: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry (the perpendicular bisectors of its sides).

pr-089.statement: What shape is the base of a regular hexagonal prism?
hints: A regular prism has a base that is a regular polygon.
solution: The base is a regular hexagon: 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles (120° each).

pr-090.statement: What shape are the lateral faces of a regular prism?
hints: The sides of the base are equal, and the lateral edges are equal and perpendicular to the base.
solution: Each lateral face is a rectangle with one side equal to the base side and the other equal to the height ⇒ they are all congruent rectangles (squares only if the height is equal to the base side).

pr-091.statement: In the regular triangular prism ABCA′B′C′, the edge AA′ is 8 cm long. What is the length of the edge CC′?
hints: The lateral edges of a prism are equal.
solution: The lateral edges are parallel and equal ⇒ CC′ = AA′ = 8 cm.

pr-092.statement: A regular hexagonal prism has a base side of 4 cm and a height of 6 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: 6 lateral faces, each a rectangle of 4 cm by 6 cm.

pr-093.statement: Calculate the total surface area of the regular square prism with a base side of 2 cm and a height of 5 cm.
hints: Lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 2 · 5 = 40 cm²; the two bases: 2 · 4 = 8 cm².

pr-094.statement: Calculate the total surface area of the regular square prism with a base side of 7 cm and a height of 2 cm.
hints: Lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: Lateral surface area: 4 · 7 · 2 = 56 cm²; the two bases: 2 · 49 = 98 cm².

sp-001.statement: What are the primary (undefined) notions of solid geometry?
options: the point, the segment and the angle
the line, the angle and the circle
the plane, the cube and the sphere
the point, the line and the plane
hints: They are the notions that are not defined, only described.
solution: The point, the line and the plane are the primary notions; all the others (segment, angle, polyhedron) are defined with their help.
Answer: the point, the line and the plane.

sp-002.statement: How is a plane usually denoted?
options: with two capital letters, for example AB
with a lowercase letter, for example a
with a Greek letter (α, β) or by three of its non-collinear points, for example (ABC)
hints: Lines are denoted by lowercase letters or by two points.
solution: A plane is denoted by a Greek letter (α, β, γ) or by three of its non-collinear points: (ABC). AB denotes a line (or a segment), a denotes a line.
Answer: with a Greek letter (α, β) or by three of its non-collinear points, for example (ABC).

sp-003.statement: How many points does a line have?
options: as many as you like, but a finite number
hints: A line is unbounded in both directions.
solution: A line has infinitely many points; any two of them determine the line.

options: the plane determined by the non-collinear points A, B, C
the line that passes through A, B, C
hints: Parentheses indicate a plane.
solution: (ABC) is the plane that passes through the non-collinear points A, B, C; the triangle is denoted ABC (or ΔABC).
Answer: the plane determined by the non-collinear points A, B, C.

sp-005.statement: Which statement about a plane is true?
options: a plane is unbounded; its drawing (a parallelogram) shows only a part of it
a plane contains only a finite number of lines
hints: Think of a sheet of paper that would stretch out forever.
solution: A plane is unbounded and has no thickness; we draw it as a parallelogram, but this shows only a portion of it.
Answer: a plane is unbounded; its drawing (a parallelogram) shows only a part of it.

sp-006.statement: How many lines pass through two distinct points?
hints: It is an axiom of geometry.
solution: Through two distinct points there passes one and only one line.

sp-007.statement: You are given 4 points in space, no three of them collinear. How many lines do they determine?
hints: Each pair of points determines a line, and two different pairs give different lines.

sp-008.statement: You are given 5 points in space, no three of them collinear. How many lines do they determine?
hints: Each pair of points determines a line, and two different pairs give different lines.

sp-009.statement: You are given 6 points in space, no three of them collinear. How many lines do they determine?
hints: Each pair of points determines a line, and two different pairs give different lines.

sp-010.statement: How many distinct lines do the vertices of a cube determine (taken two at a time)?
hints: No three vertices of the cube are collinear.
solution: The vertices of the cube: 8, no three of them collinear ⇒ 8 · 7 ÷ 2 = 28 lines (12 edges, 12 face diagonals, 4 space diagonals of the cube).

sp-011.statement: How many planes pass through three non-collinear points?
hints: It is an axiom of solid geometry.
solution: Through three non-collinear points there passes one and only one plane (the points determine the plane).

sp-012.statement: How many planes pass through three collinear points?
hints: Three collinear points lie on the same line.
solution: The points lie on a line, and infinitely many planes pass through a line (“like the pages of a book”) ⇒ three collinear points do not determine a plane.

sp-013.statement: You are given 4 non-coplanar points in space. How many planes do they determine?
hints: Each group of three points determines a plane, and the planes are different.
solution: The number of groups of three: 4 ⇒ 4 planes.

sp-014.statement: You are given 5 points in space, no four of them coplanar. How many planes do they determine?
hints: Each group of three points determines a plane, and the planes are different.
solution: The number of groups of three: 5 · 4 · 3 ÷ 6 = 10 ⇒ 10 planes.

sp-015.statement: How many planes do the vertices of a tetrahedron determine (taken three at a time)?
hints: The four vertices do not lie in the same plane.
solution: The vertices are non-coplanar ⇒ each group of three determines a different plane: the planes of the 4 faces.

sp-016.statement: How many planes are determined by a line and a point not on it?
hints: Choose two points on the line: together with the point not on the line, they are three non-collinear points.
solution: A line and a point not on it determine one and only one plane.

sp-017.statement: Through a line and a point lying on it there pass:
hints: The point adds nothing new compared to the line.
solution: The point lies on the line, and infinitely many planes pass through a line ⇒ no plane is determined.

sp-018.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the plane determined by the line AB and the point C′ also contains the point:
hints: Look for the rectangle that has the side AB and the vertex C′.
solution: AB ∥ D′C′ ⇒ A, B, C′, D′ are coplanar: the plane (ABC′) is the plane of the rectangle ABC′D′, so it contains D′.

sp-019.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, how many vertices of the cube lie in the plane determined by the line BD and the point B′?
solution: BD ∥ B′D′ ⇒ the plane (BDB′) also contains D′: 4 vertices: B, D, B′, D′ (the diagonal section BDD′B′).

sp-020.statement: How many planes do two intersecting lines determine?
hints: The common point and one point on each line are non-collinear.
solution: Two intersecting lines determine one and only one plane.

sp-021.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines AB and AA′ determine the plane:
hints: The lines intersect at A.
solution: AB and AA′ intersect at A ⇒ they determine the plane of the face ABB′A′, denoted (ABB′).

sp-022.statement: Three lines pass through the same point, but they do not all lie in the same plane. How many planes do they determine, taken two at a time?
hints: Think of the three edges that start from the vertex A of the cube.
solution: Each pair of intersecting lines determines a plane: 3 pairs ⇒ 3 planes (like the faces ABB′, ADD′ and ABC that start from A).

sp-023.statement: How many planes do two distinct parallel lines determine?
hints: Parallel means coplanar and with no common points.
solution: Two distinct parallel lines determine one and only one plane.

sp-024.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the parallel lines AA′ and CC′ determine the plane that also contains the line:
hints: AA′C′C is a rectangle.
solution: AA′ ∥ CC′ ⇒ they determine the plane ACC′A′, which also contains the diagonals AC and A′C′.

sp-025.statement: The edges AA′, BB′ and CC′ of the cube are parallel and do not all lie in the same plane. How many planes do they determine, taken two at a time?
hints: Each pair of distinct parallel lines determines a plane.
solution: The pairs AA′ and BB′, BB′ and CC′, AA′ and CC′ determine the planes (ABB′), (BCC′), (ACC′): 3 planes.

sp-026.statement: Which of the following does NOT determine a plane?
options: a line and a point not on it
hints: A plane is determined by three non-collinear points, two intersecting lines, two parallel lines, or a line + a point not on it.
solution: Skew lines do not lie in the same plane, so they do not determine any plane; each of the other options determines a plane.

sp-027.statement: If two distinct points of a line belong to a plane, then:
options: the line cuts the plane at the two points
the line is parallel to the plane
the line is contained in the plane
hints: It is an axiom of solid geometry.
solution: A line that has two distinct points in a plane is contained in that plane.
Answer: the line is contained in the plane.

sp-028.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the diagonal AC′ is contained in the plane:
hints: Look for the plane that contains both points A and C′.
solution: A and C′ both lie in the diagonal plane ABC′D′ ⇒ AC′ ⊂ (ABC′). The planes (ABC), (ABB′), (BCC′) contain only one of the points.

sp-029.statement: How many of the 12 edges of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ are contained in the plane of the base (ABC)?
hints: The edges of the base.
solution: AB, BC, CD, DA: 4 edges; the other 8 have at most one point in the base.

sp-030.statement: How many of the 12 edges of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ are contained in the diagonal plane (ACC′)?
hints: The diagonal section ACC′A′ has only two sides that are edges.
solution: The plane ACC′A′ contains the edges AA′ and CC′; AC and A′C′ are face diagonals, not edges ⇒ 2 edges.

sp-031.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines AC and CD′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: The lines have the common point C and do not coincide ⇒ they are intersecting.

sp-032.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines BD′ and AC′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: BD′ and AC′ are diagonals of the rectangle ABC′D′ ⇒ they intersect at the center of the cube: they are intersecting.

sp-033.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines AB′ and DC′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: ADC′B′ is a rectangle (AD ∥ B′C′ and AD = B′C′) ⇒ the opposite sides AB′ and DC′ are parallel.

sp-034.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines AD and B′C′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: AD ∥ BC and BC ∥ B′C′ ⇒ AD ∥ B′C′ (two lines parallel to a third line are parallel).

sp-035.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines BD and D′B′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: BDD′B′ is a rectangle (the diagonal section) ⇒ BD ∥ B′D′.

sp-036.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines AC′ and CA′ are:
hints: Look for a common point or a plane that contains both of them.
solution: AC′ and CA′ are the diagonals of the rectangle ACC′A′ ⇒ they intersect at the center of the cube.

sp-037.statement: Two lines have three common points. Then they are:
hints: Through two distinct points there passes only one line.
solution: Two common points are already enough: only one line passes through them, so the two lines coincide.

sp-038.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, O is the center of the base. The lines AO and OC are:
hints: O is the midpoint of the diagonal AC.
solution: A, O, C are collinear (O is the midpoint of AC) ⇒ the lines AO and OC are the same line AC.

sp-039.statement: How many common points do two coincident lines have?
hints: Coincident means that they are the same line.
solution: Coincident lines have all their points in common.

hints: What would happen if they had two common points?
solution: If two lines have two common points, they coincide; so two distinct lines have at most one common point.
Answer: at most one common point.

sp-041.statement: The lines AB and BA are:
hints: The order of the points does not change the line.
solution: AB and BA pass through the same two points ⇒ they are the same line.

options: they have exactly one common point
hints: “Intersecting” = they meet at one point.
solution: Intersecting lines have exactly one common point and, as a result, they lie in the same plane.
Answer: they have exactly one common point.

sp-043.statement: Which statement about intersecting lines is true?
options: two coplanar lines are always intersecting
two lines with no common points are intersecting
two intersecting lines are always perpendicular
hints: Two intersecting lines determine a plane.
solution: Two intersecting lines determine a plane, so they are coplanar. Two coplanar lines can also be parallel.
Answer: two intersecting lines are coplanar.

sp-044.statement: How many common points do two intersecting lines have?
hints: Otherwise they would be coincident.

options: they are coplanar and have no common point
hints: Careful: “no common points” is not enough in space.
solution: Parallel = in the same plane and with no common points. Lines with no common points can also be skew (like AB and CC′ in the cube).
Answer: they are coplanar and have no common point.

sp-046.statement: Which statement about lines in space is false?
options: two distinct lines parallel to a third line are parallel to each other
two lines with no common points are parallel
only one plane passes through two distinct parallel lines
hints: Think of the edges AB and CC′ of the cube.
solution: “Two lines with no common points are parallel” is false: AB and CC′ have no common points, but they are skew (not parallel).
Answer: two lines with no common points are parallel.

sp-047.statement: How many pairs of parallel edges does a cube have?
hints: The edges of the cube have 3 directions, with 4 edges in each direction.
solution: In each of the 3 directions there are 4 parallel edges, which form 4 · 3 ÷ 2 = 6 pairs.

sp-048.statement: How many common points can a line have with a plane?
hints: The line can be parallel to the plane, it can intersect it, or it can be contained in it.
solution: Parallel to the plane: no common point; intersecting: one point; contained: infinitely many points.
Answer: none, one or infinitely many.

sp-049.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the position of the line A′C′ relative to the plane (ABC)?
options: intersecting the plane (it cuts the plane at one point)
hints: First check whether it has two points in the plane, then whether it is parallel to a line in the plane.
solution: A′C′ ∥ AC, and AC lies in the plane of the base ⇒ A′C′ is parallel to the plane (ABC) (it has no points in it).

sp-050.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the position of the line AC′ relative to the plane (ABC)?
options: intersecting the plane (it cuts the plane at one point)
hints: First check whether it has two points in the plane, then whether it is parallel to a line in the plane.
