solution: A lies in the plane, C′ does not ⇒ the line AC′ cuts the plane of the base at A: it is intersecting.
Answer: intersecting the plane (it cuts the plane at one point).

sp-051.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the position of the line BD′ relative to the plane (BDD′)?
options: intersecting the plane (it cuts the plane at one point)
hints: First check whether it has two points in the plane, then whether it is parallel to a line in the plane.
solution: B and D′ both lie in the diagonal plane BDD′B′ ⇒ BD′ is contained in the plane.

sp-052.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the position of the line AB relative to the plane (CDD′)?
options: intersecting the plane (it cuts the plane at one point)
hints: First check whether it has two points in the plane, then whether it is parallel to a line in the plane.
solution: AB ∥ DC, and DC lies in the plane (CDD′) ⇒ AB is parallel to the plane of the back face.

sp-053.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the planes (ABC) and (A′B′C′) are:
options: they have only one common point
hints: Parallel planes = no common points; intersecting = they have a common line.
solution: The base and the top face have no common points ⇒ the planes are parallel.

sp-054.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the planes (ABC) and (ACC′) are:
options: they have only one common point
hints: Parallel planes = no common points; intersecting = they have a common line.
solution: They have the line AC in common ⇒ the planes are intersecting (their common line is AC).
Answer: intersecting (they meet along a line).

sp-055.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the planes (ABC′) and (DCB′) are:
options: they have only one common point
hints: Parallel planes = no common points; intersecting = they have a common line.
solution: (ABC′) is the plane ABC′D′, and (DCB′) is the plane DCB′A′; both contain the center of the cube and do not coincide ⇒ they are intersecting.
Answer: intersecting (they meet along a line).

sp-056.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the planes (ABD) and (BCD) are:
options: they have only one common point
hints: Parallel planes = no common points; intersecting = they have a common line.
solution: The three points of each plane all lie in the base ABCD ⇒ the planes coincide: they are coincident.

sp-057.statement: Two distinct planes that have a common point:
options: meet along a line that passes through that point
hints: Two planes cannot touch at a single point.
solution: If two distinct planes have a common point, they have in common a line that passes through that point (they are intersecting).
Answer: meet along a line that passes through that point.

sp-058.statement: Which of the pairs determines the plane of the base (ABC) of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′?
hints: Both lines must lie in the base and determine a plane.
solution: AC and BD intersect at the center of the base and both lie in (ABC) ⇒ they determine the plane of the base. The other pairs determine diagonal planes.
Answer: the lines AC and BD.

sp-059.statement: The parallel lines AB and D′C′ of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ determine a plane. What figure do A, B, C′, D′ form in this plane?
hints: AB = D′C′ and AB ∥ D′C′; BC′ is the diagonal of a face.
solution: AB ∥ D′C′ and AB = D′C′ ⇒ ABC′D′ is a parallelogram; AB ⊥ BC′ (AB ⊥ face BCC′B′) ⇒ a rectangle, with AB = a and BC′ = a√2 (so not a square).

sp-060.statement: Through a point not on a line, how many parallels to that line can be drawn?
hints: It is the parallel postulate, which also holds in space.
solution: Through a point not on a line there passes only one parallel to that line (the parallel postulate).

sp-061.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, which is the only line through C′ parallel to AB?
hints: Look for the edge through C′ with the same direction as AB.
solution: AB ∥ DC ∥ D′C′ ⇒ C′D′ is the parallel through C′ to AB; by the parallel postulate, it is the only one.

sp-062.statement: Through the point A, not on the line d, there pass two lines a and b, both parallel to d. What can be said about a and b?
options: they intersect at A and are different
they coincide (they are the same line)
hints: The parallel postulate does not allow two different parallels through the same point.
solution: Only one parallel to d passes through A ⇒ a and b are the same line.
Answer: they coincide (they are the same line).

sp-063.statement: How many lines through the vertex A′ of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ are parallel to the diagonal BD of the base?
hints: A′ is not on the line BD: apply the parallel postulate.
solution: A′ is not on BD ⇒ exactly one line parallel to BD passes through A′; it lies in the top plane and is parallel to B′D′ (it is not an edge of the cube).

sp-064.statement: The lines a and b are parallel, and the line c intersects the line a. Can c be parallel to b?
options: yes, if c lies in another plane
no: two parallels to b would pass through the common point of a and c
hints: If c ∥ b, two parallels to b would pass through the common point of a and c.
solution: If c were also parallel to b, two parallels to b, namely a and c, would pass through the common point of a and c, which contradicts the parallel postulate.
Answer: no: two parallels to b would pass through the common point of a and c.

sp-065.statement: The distinct lines a and b are both parallel to the line c. Then:
hints: Transitivity of parallelism also holds in space.
solution: Two distinct lines parallel to a third line are parallel to each other, even if they do not lie in the same plane as c.

sp-066.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, AA′ ∥ BB′ and BB′ ∥ CC′. What follows for AA′ and CC′?
options: AA′ ∥ CC′, so ACC′A′ is a plane quadrilateral
hints: Transitivity of parallelism.
solution: AA′ ∥ BB′ and BB′ ∥ CC′ ⇒ AA′ ∥ CC′ ⇒ the lines determine a plane: ACC′A′ is the rectangle of the diagonal section.
Answer: AA′ ∥ CC′, so ACC′A′ is a plane quadrilateral.

sp-067.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, which line is parallel to A′B′, using AB ∥ A′B′ and AB ∥ DC?
hints: Two lines parallel to the same line are parallel.
solution: A′B′ ∥ AB and DC ∥ AB ⇒ A′B′ ∥ DC (A′B′CD is a rectangle).

sp-068.statement: The criterion for a line parallel to a plane: a line d, not contained in the plane α, is parallel to α if:
options: d is parallel to a line contained in α
d is parallel to a plane that intersects α
d is perpendicular to a line in α
d has a point in α
hints: A single line in the plane is enough.
solution: If a line not contained in a plane is parallel to a line in the plane, then it is parallel to the plane.
Answer: d is parallel to a line contained in α.

sp-069.statement: Why is the diagonal B′D′ parallel to the plane (A′BD) of the cube?
options: B′D′ ∥ BD, and BD is contained in (A′BD)
B′D′ is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD)
B′D′ and BD have the same length, so any line is parallel to the plane
hints: Look for a line in the plane that is parallel to B′D′.
solution: BDD′B′ is a rectangle ⇒ B′D′ ∥ BD; BD ⊂ (A′BD), and B′D′ has no points in the plane ⇒ B′D′ ∥ (A′BD).
Answer: B′D′ ∥ BD, and BD is contained in (A′BD).

sp-070.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the line A′C′ is parallel to the plane:
hints: Look for a plane that contains a parallel to A′C′ and does not contain A′C′.
solution: A′C′ ∥ AC ⊂ (ABC) and A′C′ is not in the base ⇒ A′C′ ∥ (ABC). (In (ACC′) and (A′B′C′), A′C′ is contained; (BCC′) cuts it at C′.)

sp-071.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, why is the edge AA′ parallel to the plane (BCC′)?
options: AA′ ∥ BB′, and BB′ is contained in (BCC′)
AA′ is a vertical edge, so it is parallel to any plane
hints: Look for an edge of the face BCC′B′ that is parallel to AA′.
solution: AA′ ∥ BB′ ⊂ (BCC′) and A is not in this plane ⇒ AA′ ∥ (BCC′).
Answer: AA′ ∥ BB′, and BB′ is contained in (BCC′).

sp-072.statement: How many of the 12 edges of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ are parallel to the plane of the base (ABC) (not counting those contained in it)?
hints: The top edges are parallel to those in the base.
solution: A′B′, B′C′, C′D′, D′A′ are parallel to the edges of the base ⇒ parallel to the plane of the base: 4 edges.

sp-073.statement: The line d is parallel to the plane α, and M is a point in α. What can be said about the parallel through M to d?
options: it cuts the plane α at M and leaves it
it is contained in the plane α
hints: The plane determined by d and M cuts α along a line parallel to d.
solution: The plane (d, M) cuts α along a line through M parallel to d; by the parallel postulate, this is exactly the parallel through M to d ⇒ it is contained in α.
Answer: it is contained in the plane α.

sp-074.statement: The edge A′B′ of the cube is parallel to the plane of the base. Which line in the base, through C, is parallel to A′B′?
hints: The parallel through C to A′B′ lies in the plane of the base.
solution: A′B′ ∥ AB ∥ CD ⇒ the parallel through C to A′B′ is CD, contained in the plane of the base.

sp-075.statement: If a line d is parallel to a plane α, then in α there is (are):
options: infinitely many lines parallel to d
exactly one line parallel to d
hints: Through each point of α there passes a parallel to d, contained in α.
solution: Through each point M of the plane there passes a parallel to d contained in α ⇒ infinitely many lines in α are parallel to d.
Answer: infinitely many lines parallel to d.

sp-076.statement: The line d is parallel to the plane α. Then, compared to the lines in α, the line d:
options: is parallel to all of them
is perpendicular to all of them
can be parallel to some and skew to others, but it intersects none of them
hints: d has no common point with the plane.
solution: d has no points in α ⇒ it intersects no line in α; some are parallel to d (those in its direction), the others are skew to d. Example: A′B′ ∥ (ABC), A′B′ ∥ CD, but A′B′ and BC are skew.
Answer: can be parallel to some and skew to others, but it intersects none of them.

sp-077.statement: The edge A′D′ of the cube is parallel to the plane (ABC). Through the point B of the base, the parallel to A′D′ is:
solution: A′D′ ∥ BC (both parallel to AD) ⇒ the parallel through B is BC, contained in the base.

sp-078.statement: The line d is parallel to the plane α, and a plane β that contains d cuts the plane α along the line a. Then:
hints: a and d lie in the same plane β and have no common points.
solution: a and d both lie in β; d has no points in α, so none on a either ⇒ coplanar and with no common points ⇒ a ∥ d.

sp-079.statement: The edge A′B′ of the cube is parallel to the plane of the base. The plane (A′B′C) cuts the plane of the base along the line:
hints: The plane (A′B′C) also contains D (A′B′CD is a rectangle).
solution: A′B′ ∥ DC ⇒ the plane (A′B′C) is the plane A′B′CD; it cuts the base along DC, which is parallel to A′B′.

sp-080.statement: The diagonal B′D′ is parallel to the plane of the base ABCD. The diagonal plane (BDD′) cuts the base along the line:
hints: The plane (BDD′) also contains B′.
solution: The plane BDD′B′ cuts the base along BD, and BD ∥ B′D′, as in the theorem.

sp-081.statement: The line d ∥ α. Two different planes that contain d cut the plane α along the lines a and b. What can be said about a and b?
hints: Both are parallel to d.
solution: a ∥ d and b ∥ d ⇒ a ∥ b (transitivity); a and b lie in the same plane α.

sp-082.statement: The edge AA′ of the cube is parallel to the plane (BCC′). The plane (ACC′), which contains AA′, cuts the plane (BCC′) along the line:
hints: What line do the planes ACC′A′ and BCC′B′ have in common?
solution: The planes ACC′A′ and BCC′B′ have the edge CC′ in common, and CC′ ∥ AA′, as in the theorem.

sp-083.statement: The criterion for two parallel planes: the plane α is parallel to the plane β if:
options: α and β have a common line
α contains two intersecting lines parallel to β
α contains a line parallel to β
α contains two parallel lines parallel to β
hints: Careful: two lines parallel to each other are not enough.
solution: If a plane contains two intersecting lines parallel to another plane, the planes are parallel. With two lines parallel to each other, the conclusion is no longer certain.
Answer: α contains two intersecting lines parallel to β.

sp-084.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, why are the planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′) parallel?
options: the planes have the same area
BD ∥ B′D′ and A′B ∥ D′C, and BD and A′B are intersecting
hints: The criterion requires two intersecting lines in the first plane, parallel to the second.
solution: BD ∥ B′D′ ⊂ (CB′D′) and A′B ∥ D′C ⊂ (CB′D′); BD and A′B intersect at B ⇒ (A′BD) ∥ (CB′D′).
Answer: BD ∥ B′D′ and A′B ∥ D′C, and BD and A′B are intersecting.

sp-085.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the plane (ACD′) is parallel to the plane:
hints: AC ∥ A′C′ and AD′ ∥ BC′.
solution: AC ∥ A′C′ and AD′ ∥ BC′, and AC and AD′ are intersecting ⇒ (ACD′) ∥ (A′C′B).

sp-086.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, why are the faces (ABB′) and (DCC′) parallel?
options: AB ∥ DC and AA′ ∥ DD′, and AB and AA′ are intersecting
hints: Use the criterion with two intersecting lines.
solution: AB ∥ DC and AA′ ∥ DD′ (lines in the face DCC′D′), and AB and AA′ intersect at A ⇒ (ABB′) ∥ (DCC′).
Answer: AB ∥ DC and AA′ ∥ DD′, and AB and AA′ are intersecting.

sp-087.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, M is the midpoint of the edge BB′. The parallel lines AB and A′B′ in the plane (ABB′) are both parallel to the plane (DCM). Are the planes (ABB′) and (DCM) parallel?
options: no, they intersect: the criterion requires two intersecting lines, not parallel ones
hints: The plane (DCM) passes through M, which also lies in the plane (ABB′).
solution: AB ∥ DC ⊂ (DCM) and A′B′ ∥ DC ⇒ both are parallel to (DCM).

However, M belongs to both planes, so they are not parallel; they intersect (along the parallel through M to AB). The criterion requires two intersecting lines; with lines parallel to each other, the conclusion can be false.
Answer: no, they intersect: the criterion requires two intersecting lines, not parallel ones.

sp-088.statement: The planes α and β are parallel, and the line d is contained in α. Then:
hints: Parallel planes have no common points.
solution: d cannot have points in β (otherwise α and β would have a common point) ⇒ d ∥ β.

sp-089.statement: The base and the top face of the cube are parallel planes. Which line is certainly parallel to the plane of the base?
hints: Any line in the top face is parallel to the base.
solution: B′D′ is contained in the top face, which is parallel to the base ⇒ B′D′ ∥ (ABC). The other lines have a point in the base or intersect it.

sp-090.statement: The planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′) of the cube are parallel. The line A′D is parallel to the plane:
hints: A′D is contained in (A′BD).

sp-091.statement: Two parallel planes α and β. A line d intersects the plane α. Then d:
hints: If d were parallel to β, what would happen with α?
solution: If d were parallel to β or contained in β, then, since α ∥ β, it would be parallel to α or contained in α — but d intersects α. So d also intersects the plane β.
Answer: also intersects the plane β.

hints: The definition of parallel planes.
solution: Parallel (distinct) planes have no common point.

sp-093.statement: Two parallel planes α and β are cut by a third plane γ along the lines a and b. Then:
hints: a and b lie in γ and have no common points.
solution: a and b are contained in γ; they lie in the parallel planes α and β, so they have no common points ⇒ a ∥ b.

sp-094.statement: The diagonal plane (BDD′) cuts the base and the top face of the cube (parallel planes). The lines of intersection are:
hints: The plane BDD′B′ contains BD and B′D′.
solution: The intersections are BD (with the base) and B′D′ (with the top face) ⇒ BD ∥ B′D′.

sp-095.statement: The parallel faces (ABB′) and (DCC′) of the cube are cut by the plane (ACC′). The intersections are:
hints: Which edges does the plane ACC′A′ have in common with ABB′A′ and with DCC′D′, respectively?
solution: (ACC′) ∩ (ABB′) = AA′ and (ACC′) ∩ (DCC′) = CC′ ⇒ AA′ ∥ CC′, as in the theorem.

sp-096.statement: The plane (A′B′C) cuts the parallel faces (ABB′) and (DCC′) of the cube along the lines:
hints: The plane (A′B′C) is the plane A′B′CD.

sp-097.statement: A box has its lid parallel to its bottom. A flat sheet cuts the box at a slant. What can be said about the traces of the sheet on the bottom and on the lid?
hints: The theorem of parallel planes cut by a third plane.
solution: The bottom and the lid lie in parallel planes, cut by the plane of the sheet ⇒ the traces are parallel lines.

sp-098.statement: Through a point not in a plane, how many planes parallel to the given plane can be drawn?
hints: It is a uniqueness theorem.
solution: Through a point not in a plane there passes only one plane parallel to the given plane.

sp-099.statement: Which is the only plane through the vertex A′ of the cube that is parallel to the plane of the base?
hints: The top face is parallel to the base.
solution: The plane of the top face passes through A′ and is parallel to the base; by the uniqueness theorem, it is the only one.

sp-100.statement: Through a point not in a plane, how many lines parallel to the plane can be drawn?
options: infinitely many (they all lie in the parallel plane through that point)
hints: Compare with the uniqueness of the parallel plane.
solution: Any line through the point, contained in the parallel plane through it, is parallel to the given plane ⇒ infinitely many; they form that unique plane.
Answer: infinitely many (they all lie in the parallel plane through that point).

sp-101.statement: The planes α and β are both parallel to the plane γ and pass through the same point M (not in γ). Then:
options: α and β are distinct parallel planes
hints: Uniqueness of the parallel plane.
solution: Only one plane parallel to γ passes through M ⇒ α = β.

sp-102.statement: Through the vertex C of the cube, which plane is parallel to the plane (A′BD)?
hints: Use the parallelism (A′BD) ∥ (CB′D′).
solution: (CB′D′) passes through C and is parallel to (A′BD); by the uniqueness theorem, it is the only one.

sp-103.statement: The line d is perpendicular to the plane α. Then d is perpendicular to:
options: no line in α that does not intersect it
only the lines in α that pass through its foot
any line in the plane α
hints: It is the definition (and the converse of the criterion) of a line perpendicular to a plane.
solution: A line perpendicular to a plane is perpendicular to any line in the plane, even to those that do not pass through its foot (the angle is measured using parallels).
Answer: any line in the plane α.

sp-104.statement: The edge AA′ of the cube is perpendicular to the base. What is the measure of the angle between the lines AA′ and BD?
hints: BD lies in the plane of the base.
solution: AA′ ⊥ (ABC) and BD ⊂ (ABC) ⇒ AA′ ⊥ BD, even though the lines are skew: 90°.

sp-105.statement: AB is perpendicular to the plane (BCC′) of the cube. What is the measure of the angle between the lines AB and B′C?
hints: B′C is contained in the plane (BCC′).

sp-106.statement: AC′ is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD). Which of the lines is certainly perpendicular to AC′?
hints: Choose the line contained in (A′BD).
solution: A′D is contained in (A′BD) ⊥ AC′ ⇒ A′D ⊥ AC′.

sp-107.statement: The line d is perpendicular to the plane α, and the line a in α does not pass through the foot of d. The lines d and a are:
hints: d ⊥ α ⇒ d ⊥ any line in α.
solution: The only common point of d and α is the foot, and the foot does not lie on the line a ⇒ d does not intersect a.
Nor is d parallel to a ⇒ d and a are skew; d ⊥ α ⇒ d ⊥ a.

sp-108.statement: Through a given point, how many lines perpendicular to a given plane can be drawn?
hints: It is an existence and uniqueness theorem.
solution: Through a point (in the plane or outside it) there passes only one line perpendicular to the plane.

sp-109.statement: Through the vertex A of the cube, which is the only line perpendicular to the plane of the base?
hints: The vertical edge from A.
solution: AA′ ⊥ (ABC) and it passes through A; by the uniqueness theorem, it is the only one.

sp-110.statement: Through the vertex A of the cube, which line is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD)?
hints: The diagonal of the cube from A.
solution: AC′ ⊥ (A′BD) and it passes through A ⇒ it is the (only) perpendicular from A to this plane.

sp-111.statement: Two different lines, both perpendicular to the plane α, pass through the same point M. Is it possible?
options: yes, if M is not in α
no: only one perpendicular to α passes through M
yes, if M is in α
hints: Uniqueness of the perpendicular.
solution: Only one perpendicular to a plane passes through any point ⇒ the two lines would coincide.
Answer: no: only one perpendicular to α passes through M.

sp-112.statement: From the point P, not in the plane α, the perpendicular PO to α is drawn (O in α). For another point Q in α, what kind of triangle is POQ?
hints: PO is perpendicular to any line in α.
solution: PO ⊥ α ⇒ PO ⊥ OQ ⇒ triangle POQ is right-angled at O.

sp-113.statement: Through a given point, how many planes perpendicular to a given line can be drawn?
hints: It is a uniqueness theorem.
solution: Through a point there passes only one plane perpendicular to a given line.

sp-114.statement: Through the vertex B of the cube, which plane is perpendicular to the edge AB?
hints: AB is perpendicular to BC and to BB′.
solution: AB ⊥ BC and AB ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (BCC′), a plane that passes through B; by the uniqueness theorem, it is the only one.

sp-115.statement: Through the vertex A′ of the cube, which plane is perpendicular to the diagonal AC′?
hints: AC′ is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD).
solution: AC′ ⊥ (A′BD) and A′ lies in this plane ⇒ (A′BD) is the plane through A′ perpendicular to AC′ (the only one).

sp-116.statement: The planes α and β are both perpendicular to the line d and pass through the same point M. Then:
options: α and β intersect along d
hints: Uniqueness of the perpendicular plane.
solution: Only one plane perpendicular to d passes through M ⇒ α = β.

sp-117.statement: The point M lies on the line d. How many lines through M are perpendicular to the line d?
options: infinitely many, all in the plane through M perpendicular to d
hints: In space, the perpendiculars to d through M fill a plane.
solution: All the perpendiculars to d drawn through M form the unique plane through M perpendicular to d ⇒ infinitely many.
Answer: infinitely many, all in the plane through M perpendicular to d.

sp-118.statement: Two lines perpendicular to the same plane are:
hints: Think of the vertical edges of the cube.
solution: Two lines perpendicular to the same plane are parallel (for example AA′ and CC′, both perpendicular to the base).

sp-119.statement: AA′ and CC′ are perpendicular to the base of the cube. What figure is ACC′A′?
hints: Normals to the same plane are parallel.
solution: AA′ ∥ CC′ (both ⊥ the base) and AA′ = CC′, and AA′ ⊥ AC ⇒ ACC′A′ is a rectangle.

sp-120.statement: Two poles are fixed perpendicular to a flat piece of ground. How are the poles positioned relative to each other?
hints: Two perpendiculars to the same plane.
solution: Both poles are perpendicular to the plane of the ground ⇒ they are parallel.

sp-121.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the lines BB′ and DD′ are perpendicular to the base. Which plane contains both lines?
hints: BB′ ∥ DD′ ⇒ they determine a plane.
solution: BB′ ∥ DD′ (normals to the same plane) ⇒ they determine the diagonal plane BDD′B′.

sp-122.statement: Can two skew lines be perpendicular to the same plane?
options: yes, if the plane is vertical
no: they would be parallel, so coplanar
hints: Normals to the same plane are parallel.
solution: Two lines perpendicular to the same plane are parallel ⇒ coplanar; so they cannot be skew.
Answer: no: they would be parallel, so coplanar.

sp-123.statement: The line d is perpendicular to the plane α, and the line a is parallel to d. Then:
hints: The parallel to a perpendicular to a plane.
solution: If a line is perpendicular to a plane, any parallel to it is perpendicular to that plane.

sp-124.statement: AA′ ⊥ (ABC) and BB′ ∥ AA′. What is the angle between BB′ and the plane of the base?
hints: The parallel to a perpendicular to a plane.

sp-125.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, AB ⊥ (BCC′). Which other edge is, for the same reason, perpendicular to (BCC′)?
hints: Look for a parallel to AB.

sp-126.statement: The diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to the plane (A′BD). A line parallel to AC′ makes with the plane (A′BD) an angle of:
hints: The parallel to a perpendicular to a plane.
solution: Any parallel to AC′ is perpendicular to (A′BD): 90°.

sp-127.statement: MN is a midsegment in a triangle VAB, parallel to VA, and VA is perpendicular to the plane α. What angle does MN make with α?
solution: MN ∥ VA and VA ⊥ α ⇒ MN ⊥ α: 90°.

sp-128.statement: Two planes perpendicular to the same line are:
hints: Think of the base and the top face of the cube.
solution: Two planes perpendicular to the same line are parallel (for example the base and the top face, both perpendicular to AA′).

sp-129.statement: The planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′) are both perpendicular to the diagonal AC′. Then they are:
hints: Planes perpendicular to the same line.
solution: Two distinct planes perpendicular to the same line are parallel ⇒ (A′BD) ∥ (CB′D′).

sp-130.statement: The faces (ABB′) and (DCC′) of the cube are perpendicular to the edge AD. Then they are:
hints: AD ⊥ AB, AD ⊥ AA′ and AD ⊥ DC, AD ⊥ DD′.
solution: Both faces are perpendicular to AD ⇒ they are parallel.

sp-131.statement: The shelves of a bookcase are all perpendicular to a vertical post. How are the shelves positioned relative to each other?
hints: Planes perpendicular to the same line.
solution: The planes of the shelves are perpendicular to the same line ⇒ they are parallel.

sp-132.statement: The plane α ⊥ d and the plane β ⊥ d, and α and β have a common point. Then:
hints: They are parallel; parallel planes with a common point coincide.
solution: α ∥ β (both ⊥ d); if they have a common point, they cannot be distinct parallel planes ⇒ they coincide.

sp-133.statement: The planes α and β are parallel, and the line d is perpendicular to α. Then:
hints: The perpendicular to one of two parallel planes.
solution: A line perpendicular to one of two parallel planes is also perpendicular to the other.

sp-134.statement: The base and the top face of the cube are parallel, and AA′ ⊥ (ABC). What angle does AA′ make with the plane (A′B′C′)?
hints: The perpendicular to one of two parallel planes.

sp-135.statement: The planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′) are parallel, and AC′ ⊥ (A′BD). What angle does AC′ make with the plane (CB′D′)?
hints: The perpendicular to one of two parallel planes.

sp-136.statement: The edge AD of the cube is perpendicular to the face (ABB′). To which other face is it perpendicular, for the same reason?
hints: The face parallel to (ABB′).

sp-137.statement: A line intersects two parallel planes and is perpendicular to the first one. Its angle with the second plane is:
hints: The perpendicular to one of two parallel planes.
solution: Since it is perpendicular to the first plane, it is also perpendicular to the plane parallel to it: 90°.

sp-138.statement: The orthogonal projection of a point P onto a plane α is:
options: the point in α farthest from P
the midpoint of the segment between P and α
the foot of the perpendicular from P to α
hints: Draw the perpendicular from P to the plane.
solution: The projection of P onto α is the point where the perpendicular from P to α meets the plane (if P is in α, the projection is P itself).
Answer: the foot of the perpendicular from P to α.

sp-139.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the projection of the point C′ onto the plane of the base (ABC) is:
hints: C′C is perpendicular to the base.
solution: C′C ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the projection of C′ onto the base is C.

sp-140.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, the projection of the point D′ onto the plane of the face (ABB′) is:
hints: D′A′ is perpendicular to the face ABB′A′.
solution: D′A′ ⊥ AB and D′A′ ⊥ AA′ ⇒ D′A′ ⊥ (ABB′) ⇒ the projection of D′ is A′.

sp-141.statement: The projection of the center of the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ onto the plane of the base is:
options: the center of the base (the intersection of the diagonals AC and BD)
hints: The center of the cube is at half the height, above the center of the base.
solution: The center of the cube is the midpoint of AC′; its projection onto the base is the midpoint of AC, that is, the center of the base.
Answer: the center of the base (the intersection of the diagonals AC and BD).

sp-142.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, the projection of the apex V onto the plane of the base is:
options: the center O of the base
hints: The pyramid is regular.
solution: In a regular pyramid, the height falls at the center of the base ⇒ the projection of V is O.
Answer: the center O of the base.

sp-143.statement: A point P is 7 cm from the plane α, and O is its projection onto α. What is PO?
hints: The distance from a point to a plane is the length of the perpendicular.
solution: PO is the perpendicular from P to α ⇒ PO is exactly the distance: 7 cm.

sp-144.statement: A segment AB is parallel to the plane α. Its projection onto α is a segment:
options: parallel to AB and of the same length
hints: AB and its projection form a rectangle.
solution: AA₁ and BB₁ (the perpendiculars to α) are parallel and equal ⇒ ABB₁A₁ is a rectangle ⇒ the projection A₁B₁ is parallel to AB and has the same length.
Answer: parallel to AB and of the same length.

sp-145.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the length of the projection of the segment A′C′ onto the plane of the base. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: A′C′ is parallel to the base; its projection is AC.
solution: A′C′ ∥ (ABC) ⇒ its projection is AC, of the same length.

sp-146.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 5 cm. Find the length of the projection of the segment A′C′ onto the plane of the base. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: A′C′ is parallel to the base; its projection is AC.
solution: A′C′ ∥ (ABC) ⇒ its projection is AC, of the same length.

sp-147.statement: The projection onto a plane of a line parallel to the plane is:
options: a line perpendicular to the given one
a line that intersects the given line
a line parallel to the given line
hints: We project all the points of the line.
solution: The projection of a line parallel to the plane is a line in the plane, parallel to the given line.
Answer: a line parallel to the given line.

sp-148.statement: What projects onto a plane as a single point?
options: a line perpendicular to the plane
a line parallel to the plane
a line contained in the plane
a line that makes 45° with the plane
hints: All the points of the line project onto the same point.
solution: A line perpendicular to the plane projects onto its foot: a single point.
Answer: a line perpendicular to the plane.

sp-149.statement: Of all the segments that join a point P not in the plane α to the plane α, the shortest is:
options: the segment to the farthest point
the perpendicular from P to α
the oblique segment that makes 45° with the plane
hints: The perpendicular and an oblique segment form a right triangle.
solution: For any point Q in α, triangle POQ is right-angled at O (PO ⊥ α) ⇒ PQ (the hypotenuse) > PO. That is why the distance is measured along the perpendicular.
Answer: the perpendicular from P to α.

sp-150.statement: The point P is 5 cm from the plane α, and O is its projection. An oblique segment PQ (Q in α) is 13 cm long. Find the length of OQ.
hints: Triangle POQ is right-angled at O.
solution: OQ² = PQ² − PO² = 169 − 25 = 144 ⇒ OQ = 12 cm. (The oblique segment, 13 cm, is longer than the perpendicular, 5 cm.)

sp-151.statement: The point P is 6 cm from the plane α, and O is its projection. An oblique segment PQ (Q in α) is 10 cm long. Find the length of OQ.
hints: Triangle POQ is right-angled at O.
solution: OQ² = PQ² − PO² = 100 − 36 = 64 ⇒ OQ = 8 cm. (The oblique segment, 10 cm, is longer than the perpendicular, 6 cm.)

sp-152.statement: The point P is 8 cm from the plane α, and O is its projection. An oblique segment PQ (Q in α) is 17 cm long. Find the length of OQ.
hints: Triangle POQ is right-angled at O.
solution: OQ² = PQ² − PO² = 289 − 64 = 225 ⇒ OQ = 15 cm. (The oblique segment, 17 cm, is longer than the perpendicular, 8 cm.)

sp-153.statement: The point P is 4 cm from the plane α. Which of the lengths can NOT be the length of a segment PQ, with Q in α?
hints: The perpendicular (4 cm) is the shortest segment.
solution: Any segment PQ is at least 4 cm long (the length of the perpendicular) ⇒ 3 cm is not possible.

sp-154.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance between the line A′B′ and the plane of the base (ABC).
hints: A′B′ is parallel to the base: all its points are at the same distance.
solution: A′B′ ∥ (ABC) ⇒ the distance from the line to the plane is the distance from any of its points, for example A′: A′A = 6 cm.

sp-155.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance between the diagonal B′D′ and the plane (A′BD). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: B′D′ ∥ BD ⊂ (A′BD); the plane (A′BD) is perpendicular to AC′ and cuts the diagonal at one third of its length from A.
solution: B′D′ ∥ (A′BD) ⇒ the distance is the distance from B′ (or from the center O′ of the top face) to the plane.
(A′BD) ∥ (CB′D′), and B′D′ ⊂ (CB′D′); the distance between these parallel planes is one third of the diagonal AC′: 6√3 ÷ 3 = 2√3 cm.

sp-156.statement: The line d is parallel to the plane α. The distance between d and α is:
options: the distance from any point of d to α
the greatest distance from d to α
the length of the projection of d
hints: All the points of the line are at the same distance from the plane.
solution: d ∥ α ⇒ all the points of d are at the same distance from α; this is the distance between the line and the plane.
Answer: the distance from any point of d to α.

sp-157.statement: What is the distance between a line and a plane that it intersects?
options: 0, because they have a common point
the distance from an arbitrary point
hints: The line–plane distance is defined only for a line parallel to the plane.
solution: If the line intersects the plane, it has a common point with it, so the distance is 0. That is why, in class, the distance from a line to a plane is calculated only when the line is parallel to the plane.
Answer: 0, because they have a common point.

sp-158.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 4 cm. Find the distance between the edge AA′ and the plane of the face (BCC′).
hints: AA′ ∥ (BCC′); AB is perpendicular to the face BCC′B′.
solution: AA′ ∥ BB′ ⊂ (BCC′) ⇒ AA′ ∥ (BCC′); the distance is AB = 4 cm (AB ⊥ (BCC′)).

sp-159.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance between the parallel planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to both planes and is divided by them into three equal parts.
solution: The planes divide the diagonal into three equal parts ⇒ the distance between them is 6√3 ÷ 3 = 2√3 cm.

sp-160.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 9 cm. Find the distance between the parallel planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to both planes and is divided by them into three equal parts.
solution: The planes divide the diagonal into three equal parts ⇒ the distance between them is 9√3 ÷ 3 = 3√3 cm.

sp-161.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 12 cm. Find the distance between the parallel planes (A′BD) and (CB′D′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The diagonal AC′ is perpendicular to both planes and is divided by them into three equal parts.
solution: The planes divide the diagonal into three equal parts ⇒ the distance between them is 12√3 ÷ 3 = 4√3 cm.

sp-162.statement: The distance between two parallel planes is:
options: the distance from any point of one of them to the other
the distance between any two of their points
hints: All the points of a plane are at the same distance from the parallel plane.
solution: The distance between parallel planes is the distance from any point of one of them to the other plane (the length of a common perpendicular).
Answer: the distance from any point of one of them to the other.

sp-163.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 7 cm. What is the distance between the base (ABC) and the top face (A′B′C′)?
hints: A vertical edge is perpendicular to both.
solution: AA′ ⊥ both planes ⇒ the distance is AA′ = 7 cm.

sp-164.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 5 cm. Find the distance between the parallel lines AB and C′D′. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The lines are opposite sides of the rectangle ABC′D′; BC′ is perpendicular to AB.
solution: AB ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ AB ⊥ BC′, and BC′ ⊥ C′D′ ⇒ BC′ is the common perpendicular.

sp-165.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 8 cm. Find the distance between the parallel lines AB and C′D′. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The lines are opposite sides of the rectangle ABC′D′; BC′ is perpendicular to AB.
solution: AB ⊥ (BCC′) ⇒ AB ⊥ BC′, and BC′ ⊥ C′D′ ⇒ BC′ is the common perpendicular.

sp-166.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance between the parallel edges AA′ and CC′. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: AC is perpendicular to both edges.
solution: AC ⊥ AA′ and AC ⊥ CC′ ⇒ the distance is AC = 6√2 cm.

sp-167.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. Find the distance between the parallel diagonals BD and B′D′.
hints: BB′ is perpendicular to both.
solution: BB′ ⊥ BD and BB′ ⊥ B′D′ ⇒ the distance is BB′ = 6 cm.

sp-168.statement: The distance between two parallel lines is:
options: the length of a common perpendicular (the distance from any point of one of them to the other)
the distance between any two of their points
the length of any oblique segment
hints: Parallel lines lie in the same plane.
solution: The distance between two parallel lines is the distance from any point of one of them to the other line.
Answer: the length of a common perpendicular (the distance from any point of one of them to the other).

sp-169.statement: The first converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars: PA ⊥ α, the line d ⊂ α, M ∈ d and PM ⊥ d. Then:
hints: Compare with the direct theorem (PA ⊥ α, AM ⊥ d ⇒ PM ⊥ d).
solution: If PA ⊥ α and PM ⊥ d (d in α, M on d), then AM ⊥ d: the foot of the oblique segment and the foot of the perpendicular lie on the same perpendicular to d.

sp-170.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, O is the center of the base. Knowing that A′A ⊥ (ABC) and A′O ⊥ BD, what follows?
hints: The first converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars.
solution: A′A ⊥ (ABC), A′O ⊥ BD ⇒ AO ⊥ BD (the first converse). It fits: the diagonals of the square are perpendicular.

sp-171.statement: PA is perpendicular to the plane of triangle ABC, and PM ⊥ BC, with M on BC. What is AM in triangle ABC?
hints: The first converse: AM ⊥ BC.
solution: PA ⊥ (ABC) and PM ⊥ BC ⇒ AM ⊥ BC ⇒ AM is the altitude from A of triangle ABC.

sp-172.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, VO ⊥ (ABC) and VM ⊥ BC (M on BC). What follows about OM?
options: OM ⊥ BC, so M is the midpoint of BC
hints: The first converse; in a square, the perpendicular from the center to a side falls at its midpoint.
solution: VO ⊥ (ABC), VM ⊥ BC ⇒ OM ⊥ BC; the perpendicular from the center of the square to a side falls at its midpoint.
Answer: OM ⊥ BC, so M is the midpoint of BC.

sp-173.statement: The direct theorem of three perpendiculars states: PA ⊥ α, AM ⊥ d (d ⊂ α, M ∈ d) ⇒ PM ⊥ d. What is its first converse?
hints: In a converse, a hypothesis is swapped with the conclusion.
solution: The first converse: PA ⊥ α and PM ⊥ d ⇒ AM ⊥ d. (the second converse: PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d and PA ⊥ AM ⇒ PA ⊥ α.)
Answer: PA ⊥ α, PM ⊥ d ⇒ AM ⊥ d.

sp-174.statement: The second converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars: PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d (d ⊂ α, A ∈ α, M ∈ d) and PA ⊥ AM. Then:
hints: d is perpendicular to the plane (PAM).
solution: d ⊥ PM and d ⊥ AM ⇒ d ⊥ (PAM) ⇒ d ⊥ PA; since PA ⊥ AM and AM, d are intersecting in α ⇒ PA ⊥ α.

sp-175.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, O is the center of the base: C′O ⊥ BD, CO ⊥ BD and C′C ⊥ CO. What follows from the second converse?
hints: Identify PM, AM, PA from the converse.
solution: With P = C′, A = C, M = O, d = BD: C′O ⊥ BD, CO ⊥ BD and C′C ⊥ CO ⇒ C′C ⊥ (ABC).

sp-176.statement: How is the second converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars used?
options: to show that a line is perpendicular to a plane
to show that two lines are parallel
hints: Its conclusion is PA ⊥ α.
solution: The conclusion of the second converse is that a line (PA) is perpendicular to a plane: we use it to identify the normal to the plane.
Answer: to show that a line is perpendicular to a plane.

sp-177.statement: Triangle PAM is right-angled at A, and the line d in the plane α passes through M and is perpendicular both to PM and to AM. A is in α. What is the position of PA relative to α?
hints: The second converse.
solution: PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d, PA ⊥ AM ⇒ PA ⊥ α.

sp-178.statement: For the second converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars, how many perpendicularity hypotheses are needed?
options: three: PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d and PA ⊥ AM
two: PM ⊥ d and AM ⊥ d
hints: The conclusion PA ⊥ α requires PA to be perpendicular to two intersecting lines in α.
solution: PM ⊥ d and AM ⊥ d give d ⊥ PA; together with PA ⊥ AM, PA is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in α (d and AM) ⇒ PA ⊥ α. There are three hypotheses.
Answer: three: PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d and PA ⊥ AM.

sp-179.statement: What angle does a line parallel to a plane make with it?
hints: By convention, the angle between a plane and a line parallel to it or contained in it is 0°.
solution: The angle between a line and a plane to which it is parallel (or in which it is contained) is, by definition, 0°.

sp-180.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, which line makes 0° with the plane of the base?
hints: Look for a line parallel to the base.
solution: B′D′ is parallel to the base ⇒ its angle with the base is 0°.

sp-181.statement: What angle does the diagonal AC make with the plane of the base (ABC) of the cube?
hints: AC lies in the plane of the base.
solution: A line contained in a plane makes an angle of 0° with it.
Answer: 0° (it is contained in the plane).

sp-182.statement: The edge A′B′ of the cube makes with the plane (ABC) an angle of:

sp-183.statement: If the angle between a line and a plane is 0°, then the line:
options: is parallel to the plane or contained in it
hints: 0° means that the line does not “tilt” relative to the plane.
solution: The angle 0° occurs exactly when the line is parallel to the plane or contained in it.
Answer: is parallel to the plane or contained in it.

sp-184.statement: What angle does a line perpendicular to a plane make with it?
hints: Perpendicular to the plane means perpendicular to any line in the plane.
solution: The angle between a line perpendicular to a plane and the plane is 90°.

sp-185.statement: Which line makes 90° with the plane (A′BD) of the cube?
hints: The diagonal of the cube from A.

sp-186.statement: Which line makes 90° with the plane of the face (ADD′) of the cube?
hints: AB is perpendicular to AD and to AA′.
solution: AB ⊥ AD and AB ⊥ AA′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (ADD′) ⇒ 90°.

sp-187.statement: Can the angle between a line and a plane be greater than 90°?
options: yes, if the line is skew
hints: We take the angle with the projection, which is at most 90°.
solution: The angle between a line and a plane is between 0° (parallel or contained) and 90° (perpendicular).
Answer: no, it is between 0° and 90°.

sp-188.statement: A line makes 90° with a plane. What angle does it make with any line in the plane?
hints: Perpendicular to the plane ⇒ perpendicular to all the lines in the plane.
solution: A line perpendicular to a plane is perpendicular to any line in the plane: 90°.

sp-189.statement: A line makes an angle of 30° with a plane. What angle does the line make with a perpendicular to the plane (the normal)?
hints: The line, its projection and the normal form a right triangle.
solution: The angle with the plane and the angle with the normal are complementary: 90° − 30° = 60°.

sp-190.statement: A line makes an angle of 45° with a plane. What angle does the line make with a perpendicular to the plane (the normal)?
hints: The line, its projection and the normal form a right triangle.
solution: The angle with the plane and the angle with the normal are complementary: 90° − 45° = 45°.

sp-191.statement: A line makes an angle of 70° with a plane. What angle does the line make with a perpendicular to the plane (the normal)?
hints: The line, its projection and the normal form a right triangle.
solution: The angle with the plane and the angle with the normal are complementary: 90° − 70° = 20°.

sp-192.statement: The diagonal AC′ of the cube makes an angle u with the edge CC′ and an angle v with the plane of the base. What relationship is there between u and v?
hints: CC′ is the normal to the base.
solution: CC′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ the angles of AC′ with the normal CC′ and with the plane are complementary: u + v = 90°.

sp-193.statement: If a line makes 0° with a plane, what angle does it make with the normal to the plane?
hints: The angles are complementary.
solution: 90° − 0° = 90°: a line parallel to the plane is perpendicular to the normal to the plane.

sp-194.statement: A segment of 10 cm makes an angle of 60° with a plane. Find the length of the projection of the segment onto the plane.
hints: The length of the projection = the length of the segment · cos(the angle with the plane).

sp-195.statement: A segment of 8 cm makes an angle of 30° with a plane. Find the length of the projection of the segment onto the plane. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The length of the projection = the length of the segment · cos(the angle with the plane).

sp-196.statement: A segment of 6√2 cm makes an angle of 45° with a plane. Find the length of the projection of the segment onto the plane.
hints: The length of the projection = the length of the segment · cos(the angle with the plane).

sp-197.statement: A segment of 12 cm makes an angle of 60° with a plane. Find the length of the projection of the segment onto the plane.
hints: The length of the projection = the length of the segment · cos(the angle with the plane).

sp-198.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. What is the length of the projection of the diagonal AC′ onto the plane of the base? Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: The projection of C′ onto the base is C.
solution: The projection of AC′ onto the base is AC = 6√2 cm.

options: the angle between two skew lines
the figure formed by two intersecting lines
the figure formed by two half-planes with the same boundary line (the edge)
hints: Think of an open book.
solution: A dihedral angle is the figure formed by two half-planes (the faces) that have the same boundary, a line called the edge of the dihedral angle.
Answer: the figure formed by two half-planes with the same boundary line (the edge).

sp-200.statement: How is a dihedral angle measured?
options: by the distance between the faces
by the plane angle: from the same point of the edge, perpendiculars to the edge are drawn, one in each face
by the length of the edge
by the area of the faces
hints: The plane angle of the dihedral.
solution: A point is chosen on the edge; in each face, a perpendicular to the edge is drawn from that point; the angle between them is the plane angle of the dihedral (it does not depend on the chosen point).
Answer: by the plane angle: from the same point of the edge, perpendiculars to the edge are drawn, one in each face.

sp-201.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the edge of the dihedral angle formed by the faces (ABC) and (ABB′)?
hints: The edge of the dihedral angle is the common line of the faces.
solution: The faces ABCD and ABB′A′ have the edge AB in common ⇒ this is the edge of the dihedral angle.

sp-202.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the plane angle of the dihedral between the plane (ABC) and the plane (ABC′), with the edge AB?
hints: From B, perpendiculars to AB: BC in the base, BC′ in the plane (ABC′).
solution: BC ⊥ AB and BC′ ⊥ AB (AB ⊥ face BCC′B′) ⇒ the plane angle of the dihedral is ∠CBC′.

sp-203.statement: Does the plane angle of a dihedral depend on the point chosen on the edge?
options: no, it has the same measure anywhere on the edge
yes, it increases toward the ends
yes, it is largest in the middle
hints: The plane angles obtained at different points have parallel sides.
solution: The plane angles constructed at different points of the edge have their sides respectively parallel and pointing in the same direction ⇒ they are congruent.
Answer: no, it has the same measure anywhere on the edge.

sp-204.statement: A dihedral angle whose plane angle measures 90° is called:
hints: Classification by the plane angle.
solution: Plane angle of 90° ⇒ right dihedral angle; less than 90° acute, more than 90° obtuse.

sp-205.statement: Two adjacent dihedral angles have the same edge and a common face, and their other faces form a plane. One of them has a plane angle of 70°. What is the measure of the other one?
hints: Their plane angles are adjacent supplementary angles.

sp-206.statement: Two adjacent dihedral angles have the same edge and a common face, and their other faces form a plane. One of them has a plane angle of 45°. What is the measure of the other one?
hints: Their plane angles are adjacent supplementary angles.

sp-207.statement: The dihedral angle formed by a lateral face and the base of a regular pyramid (with the apex above the base) is:
hints: The plane angle is ∠VMO, an angle of a right triangle.
solution: ∠VMO is an acute angle of the right triangle VOM ⇒ the dihedral angle is acute.

sp-208.statement: The dihedral angle between two neighboring faces of a cube is:
hints: The neighboring faces of the cube are perpendicular.
solution: The neighboring faces of the cube form dihedral angles of 90° (right angles).

sp-209.statement: The criterion for two perpendicular planes: the plane α is perpendicular to the plane β if:
options: α contains a line that intersects β
α contains a line perpendicular to β
α contains a line parallel to β
α and β have a common line
hints: Think of a door that rotates around a vertical axis.
solution: If a plane contains a line perpendicular to another plane, then the planes are perpendicular.
Answer: α contains a line perpendicular to β.

sp-210.statement: Why is the diagonal plane (ACC′) perpendicular to the plane of the base?
options: it cuts the base along AC
it contains the edge CC′, which is perpendicular to the base
it has the shape of a rectangle
hints: Look in (ACC′) for a line perpendicular to the base.
solution: Answer: it contains the edge CC′, which is perpendicular to the base.

sp-211.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, O and O′ are the centers of the bases. Why are the diagonal planes (ACC′) and (BDD′) perpendicular?
options: BD ⊥ (ACC′), and BD is contained in (BDD′)
hints: BD ⊥ AC and BD ⊥ CC′.
solution: BD ⊥ AC and BD ⊥ CC′ ⇒ BD ⊥ (ACC′); BD ⊂ (BDD′) ⇒ (BDD′) ⊥ (ACC′).
Answer: BD ⊥ (ACC′), and BD is contained in (BDD′).

sp-212.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD with base center O, the plane (VAC) is perpendicular to the plane of the base because:
options: it contains the height VO, perpendicular to the base
solution: Answer: it contains the height VO, perpendicular to the base.

sp-213.statement: How many planes perpendicular to the plane of the base pass through the edge AA′ of the cube?
options: infinitely many (any plane that contains AA′)
hints: Any plane that contains AA′ contains a perpendicular to the base.
solution: AA′ ⊥ (ABC) ⇒ any plane that contains AA′ is perpendicular to the base: infinitely many.
Answer: infinitely many (any plane that contains AA′).

sp-214.statement: The planes α and β are perpendicular and intersect along the line d. A line a in α is perpendicular to d. Then:
hints: The converse: the perpendicular to the line of intersection, drawn in one of the planes.
solution: If two planes are perpendicular, any line in one of them that is perpendicular to their common line is perpendicular to the other plane.

sp-215.statement: The planes (ACC′) and (ABC) of the cube are perpendicular and intersect along AC. Which line in (ACC′), perpendicular to AC, is perpendicular to the base?
hints: Look in (ACC′) for a perpendicular to AC.

sp-216.statement: The diagonal planes (ACC′) and (BDD′) of the cube are perpendicular and intersect along OO′ (O, O′ the centers of the bases). The diagonal AC is perpendicular to OO′. What follows?
hints: The converse of the criterion for perpendicular planes.
solution: AC ⊂ (ACC′), AC ⊥ OO′ (the common line) ⇒ AC ⊥ (BDD′).

sp-217.statement: A vertical wall is perpendicular to the floor. A line drawn on the wall, perpendicular to the line where the wall meets the floor, is:
hints: The converse: the perpendicular to the common line.
solution: The wall ⊥ the floor; the line on the wall perpendicular to the joint is perpendicular to the floor.

sp-218.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, (VAC) ⊥ (ABC), with the common line AC. Which line in (VAC) is perpendicular to the base?
options: VO (O the center of the base)
hints: The perpendicular to AC drawn in the plane (VAC) from V.
solution: Answer: VO (O the center of the base).

sp-219.statement: Two intersecting planes are both perpendicular to a third plane. Then their common line is:
hints: Think of two neighboring walls and the floor.
solution: The common line of two intersecting planes that are perpendicular to a third plane is perpendicular to the third plane (the corner between two walls is vertical).
Answer: perpendicular to the third plane.

sp-220.statement: The faces (ABB′) and (ADD′) of the cube are perpendicular to the base. What follows about their common edge AA′?
hints: The intersection of two planes perpendicular to a third plane.

sp-221.statement: The diagonal planes (ACC′) and (BDD′) of the cube are perpendicular to the base. Their common line OO′ (O, O′ the centers of the bases) is:
hints: The intersection of two planes perpendicular to a third plane.

sp-222.statement: Two neighboring walls of a room are perpendicular to the floor. How is the corner (the common edge of the walls) positioned relative to the floor?
hints: The intersection of two planes perpendicular to a third plane.
solution: Both walls ⊥ floor ⇒ their common edge ⊥ floor.

sp-223.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, the planes (VAC) and (VBD) are perpendicular to the base. Their common line is:
options: VO, the height of the pyramid
hints: What line do the two diagonal planes have in common?
solution: (VAC) ∩ (VBD) = VO; both planes ⊥ the base ⇒ VO ⊥ (ABC): it is the height.
Answer: VO, the height of the pyramid.

sp-224.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. The plane (ABB′) is perpendicular to the plane (BCC′), along the edge BB′. Find the distance from A to the plane (BCC′).
hints: In the plane (ABB′), the perpendicular from A to the common line BB′ is AB.
solution: (ABB′) ⊥ (BCC′), common line BB′; AB ⊂ (ABB′) and AB ⊥ BB′ ⇒ AB ⊥ (BCC′).

sp-225.statement: The cube ABCDA′B′C′D′ has an edge of 6 cm. The planes (ACC′) and (BDD′) are perpendicular. Find the distance from A to the plane (BDD′). Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: In the plane (ACC′), the perpendicular from A to the common line OO′ is AO.
solution: (ACC′) ⊥ (BDD′), common line OO′; AO ⊂ (ACC′) and AO ⊥ OO′ ⇒ AO ⊥ (BDD′).

sp-226.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the measure of the angle between the planes (A′B′C) and (ABC)?
hints: (A′B′C) is the plane A′B′CD; its common edge with the base is DC.
solution: (A′B′C) = the plane A′B′CD, and the common line with the base is CD.
CB ⊥ CD and CB′ ⊥ CD ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠B′CB = 45°.

sp-227.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the measure of the angle between the planes (ABC′) and (DCB′)?
hints: The planes are ABC′D′ and DCB′A′; both contain the center of the cube; cut the cube with the plane of a lateral face.
solution: The planes intersect along the line through the center of the cube parallel to AB. In a section perpendicular to AB (for example the face BCC′B′), their traces are the diagonals BC′ and B′C of the square.
The diagonals of a square are perpendicular ⇒ the angle between the planes is 90°.

sp-228.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, what is the measure of the angle between the planes (ACC′) and (ABB′)?
hints: The common line is AA′; in the base, AC and AB are perpendicular to AA′.
solution: (ACC′) ∩ (ABB′) = AA′; AB ⊥ AA′ and AC ⊥ AA′ ⇒ the angle between the planes is ∠BAC = 45°.

sp-229.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 8 cm. A plane parallel to the base cuts the lateral edges at one quarter of their length, measured from the apex. What is the side of the section?
hints: The section is similar to the base, with the ratio 1/4.
solution: The section is a square similar to the base, with the similarity ratio 1/4 ⇒ side = 8 ÷ 4 = 2 cm.

ro-001.statement: Which of the following solids has NO edges and no vertices?
hints: Edges and vertices appear where flat faces meet.
solution: The sphere has a single surface, a curved one: it has no flat faces, so no edges and no vertices. The cube, the pyramid and the prism have edges and vertices.

ro-002.statement: Which object has the shape of a cylinder?
hints: The cylinder has two equal bases, two disks, and a curved surface between them.
solution: The soda can has two equal disk-shaped bases and a curved wall ⇒ cylinder. The ball is a sphere, the ice cream cone is a cone, the box is a rectangular prism.

ro-003.statement: Which object has the shape of a cone?
hints: The cone has a disk-shaped base and a vertex.
solution: The ice cream cone has a disk-shaped base (its opening) and a vertex ⇒ cone. The can is a cylinder, the ball is a sphere, the die is a cube.

ro-004.statement: Which object has the shape of a sphere?
hints: All the points of the surface are at the same distance from the center.
solution: The soccer ball has the shape of a sphere: its points are (almost) at the same distance from the center.

ro-005.statement: Which of the following solids is a polyhedron?
hints: A polyhedron has only flat faces, which are polygons.
solution: The triangular prism has 5 faces, all of them polygons ⇒ polyhedron. The cylinder, the cone and the sphere have curved surfaces, so they are not polyhedra.

options: one base (a disk), a curved lateral surface and a vertex
hints: Think of an upside-down ice cream cone.
solution: The cone has a single base, a disk, the curved lateral surface and the vertex V.
Answer: one base (a disk), a curved lateral surface and a vertex.

ro-007.statement: What solid do you get by rotating a rectangle around one of its sides?
hints: The side around which it rotates becomes the axis.
solution: The fixed side becomes the axis (the height), and the side perpendicular to it describes the disks of the bases ⇒ right circular cylinder.

ro-008.statement: What solid do you get by rotating a right triangle around one of its legs?
hints: The fixed leg becomes the height, and the other leg describes the base.
solution: The fixed leg is the height, the other leg is the radius of the base, and the hypotenuse describes the lateral surface ⇒ right circular cone.

ro-009.statement: What solid do you get by rotating a half-disk around its diameter?
hints: Each point of the semicircle stays at distance R from the center.
solution: The points of the semicircle stay at distance R from the center and describe the sphere; the half-disk describes the ball (the solid).

ro-010.statement: A right triangle rotates around its hypotenuse. What solid do you get?
options: two cones joined at their bases
hints: The altitude to the hypotenuse describes a common disk.
solution: The vertex of the right angle describes a circle (radius = the altitude to the hypotenuse); each leg describes the lateral surface of a cone ⇒ two cones with a common base. Watch out: only rotating around a leg gives a single cone.
Answer: two cones joined at their bases.

ro-011.statement: A right circular cylinder has a base radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. How long is its generatrix?
hints: In a right circular cylinder, the generatrix is perpendicular to the bases.
solution: The generatrix joins two corresponding points on the circles of the bases and is perpendicular to the bases ⇒ it is equal to the height: 12 cm.

ro-012.statement: The diameter of the base of a cylinder is 14 cm. What is the radius of the base?
hints: The radius is half the diameter.

ro-013.statement: The radius of the base of a cylinder is 9 cm. What is the diameter of the base?
hints: The diameter is twice the radius.

ro-014.statement: Rectangle ABCD, with AB = 6 cm and BC = 10 cm, rotates around side BC. What is the radius of the base of the resulting cylinder?
hints: BC stays fixed and becomes the axis; the side perpendicular to BC describes the base.
solution: BC is the axis (a height of 10 cm), and AB ⊥ BC describes the disk of the base ⇒ the radius is AB = 6 cm.

ro-015.statement: Rectangle ABCD, with AB = 6 cm and BC = 10 cm, rotates around side AB. What is the height of the resulting cylinder?
hints: The side around which it rotates is the height.
solution: AB stays fixed ⇒ the height is AB = 6 cm, and the radius is BC = 10 cm.

ro-016.statement: The generatrix of a right circular cylinder is:
hints: The generatrix is parallel to the axis.
solution: The generatrix is parallel to the axis and perpendicular to the bases ⇒ its length is the height.

ro-017.statement: The axis of a right circular cylinder is the line that passes through:
options: the centers of the two bases
the center of the bottom base and a point on the top circle
two points on the circle of the bottom base
hints: The axis is the line around which the rectangle rotates.
solution: The axis passes through the centers O and O′ of the bases and is perpendicular to them.
Answer: the centers of the two bases.

ro-018.statement: The bases of a right circular cylinder are:
options: two congruent disks, in parallel planes
hints: When you rotate a rectangle, the two sides parallel to the radius describe the bases.
solution: The bases are two disks with the same radius, lying in parallel planes (perpendicular to the axis).
Answer: two congruent disks, in parallel planes.

ro-019.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: The axial section is a rectangle with sides 2R and h.
solution: The axial section is the rectangle with sides 2 · 3 = 6 cm and 5 cm.

ro-020.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 6 cm. Calculate the perimeter of the axial section.
hints: The sides of the rectangle: the diameter and the height.
solution: The sides of the axial section: 2 · 4 = 8 cm and 6 cm.

ro-021.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 16 cm. ABCD is the axial section (AB a diameter of the bottom base). Calculate the diagonal AC.
hints: Triangle ABC is right-angled at B.

ro-022.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 24 cm. ABCD is the axial section (AB a diameter of the bottom base). Calculate the diagonal AC.
hints: Triangle ABC is right-angled at B.

ro-023.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. ABCD is the axial section (AB a diameter of the bottom base). Calculate the diagonal AC.
hints: Triangle ABC is right-angled at B.

ro-024.statement: The axial section of a cylinder is a square with a side of 10 cm. What is the radius of the base?
hints: One side of the square is the diameter of the base.
solution: The bottom side of the section is the diameter: 2R = 10 ⇒ R = 5 cm (and the height is also 10 cm).

ro-025.statement: The axial section of a cylinder is a square with an area of 64 cm². What is the height of the cylinder?
hints: The side of the square is the height.
solution: The side of the square: √64 = 8 cm ⇒ h = 8 cm (and 2R = 8 cm).

ro-026.statement: The axial section of a cylinder has an area of 48 cm², and the height of the cylinder is 8 cm. What is the radius of the base?
hints: Area of the axial section = 2R · h.

ro-027.statement: The axial section of a right circular cylinder is:
hints: The plane contains the axis and cuts each base along a diameter.
solution: The plane that contains the axis cuts the bases along two equal, parallel diameters, and the lateral surface along two generatrices ⇒ a rectangle with sides 2R and h.

ro-028.statement: A cylinder with a radius of 7 cm is cut by a plane parallel to the bases. Calculate the area of the section. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The section parallel to the bases is a disk congruent to the bases.
solution: The section is a disk with radius 7 cm.

ro-029.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. A plane parallel to the bases cuts it 4 cm from the bottom base. Calculate the area of the section. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: It doesn't matter at what height the cut is made.
solution: Any section parallel to the bases is a disk with the radius of the base, 3 cm.
Area = π · 3² = 9π cm². The distance of 4 cm plays no role.

ro-030.statement: A cylinder with a radius of 5 cm is cut by a plane parallel to the bases, halfway up its height. The section is:
options: a disk with a radius of 10 cm
a disk with a radius of 5 cm
a disk with a radius of 2.5 cm
hints: The radius of the cylinder is the same at any height.
solution: The section parallel to the bases is a disk congruent to the bases: radius 5 cm. Watch out: the radius is not halved (that happens with the cone).
Answer: a disk with a radius of 5 cm.

ro-031.statement: A cylinder has a base diameter of 12 cm. Calculate the circumference of a section parallel to the bases. Write the result as a·π cm by filling in a.
hints: The section has the radius of the base.

ro-032.statement: The area of a section of a cylinder parallel to the bases is 36π cm². What is the radius of the cylinder?

ro-033.statement: The area of a section of a cylinder parallel to the bases is 81π cm². What is the diameter of the base?
hints: Find the radius first.

ro-034.statement: A plane parallel to the bases divides a cylinder with a height of 12 cm into two cylinders. The bottom one has a height of 5 cm. What is the height of the top one?
hints: The two cylinders have the same radius; the heights add up.
solution: The section is the common base of the two cylinders, and their heights add up: 12 − 5 = 7 cm.

ro-035.statement: A cylinder is cut by two planes parallel to the bases. The sections you get are:
options: two disks congruent to the bases
two disks smaller than the bases
hints: The radius doesn't change along the cylinder.
solution: Each plane parallel to the bases cuts the cylinder along a disk with radius R ⇒ the two sections are congruent to each other and to the bases.
Answer: two disks congruent to the bases.

ro-036.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. The lateral surface unfolds into a rectangle. Calculate the length of the side that wraps around the circle of the base. Write the result as a·π cm by filling in a.
hints: The side of the rectangle fits exactly around the circle of the base.
solution: The side that wraps around the circle of the base is as long as the circumference: 2 · π · 5 = 10π cm. The other side is the height, 8 cm.

ro-037.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a cylinder is a rectangle measuring 12π cm by 9 cm; the 12π cm side wraps around the circle of the base. What is the radius of the cylinder?
solution: 2 · π · R = 12π ⇒ R = 6 cm (and the height is 9 cm).

ro-038.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a cylinder is a square with a side of 8π cm. What is the height of the cylinder? Write the result as a·π cm by filling in a.
hints: One side of the square is the height.
solution: The sides of the net are the circumference of the base and the height ⇒ h = 8π cm (and 2πR = 8π, so R = 4 cm).

ro-039.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a cylinder is a square with a side of 8π cm. What is the radius of the base?
hints: The side that wraps around the base: 2πR = 8π.

ro-040.statement: The net of the total surface of a cylinder is made of:
options: a circular sector and a disk
hints: The lateral surface plus the two bases.
solution: The lateral surface unfolds into a rectangle (2πR by h), and the bases are two disks with radius R.
Answer: a rectangle and two disks.

ro-041.statement: A rectangular sheet measuring 20π cm by 15 cm is rolled into a cylinder, with the 20π cm side becoming the circle of the base. Calculate the volume of the cylinder. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Find the radius from 2πR = 20π; the height is 15 cm.

ro-042.statement: The label of a cylindrical can covers it all the way around, without overlapping. The can has a radius of 4 cm, and the label has a width of 10 cm. Calculate the area of the label. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The unrolled label is a rectangle with length 2πR.
solution: Length of the label = 2 · π · 4 = 8π cm.

ro-043.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 7 cm. Calculate the area of the rectangle in the net of the lateral surface. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The dimensions of the rectangle: 2πR and h.
solution: The rectangle measures 2 · π · 3 = 6π cm by 7 cm.
Area = 6π · 7 = 42π cm² (this is exactly the lateral surface area).

ro-044.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area = 2πR · h.

ro-045.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area = 2πR · h.

ro-046.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 7 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area = 2πR · h.

ro-047.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 2.5 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area = 2πR · h.

ro-048.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a lateral surface area of 60π cm². Find the height.

ro-049.statement: A cylinder has a height of 8 cm and a lateral surface area of 96π cm². Find the radius.

ro-050.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the lateral surface area?
hints: A_l = 2πRh, without the bases.
solution: Watch out: 12π cm² comes from forgetting the factor 2, 42π cm² is the total surface area (with the bases), 36π cm³ would be the volume.

ro-051.statement: The cardboard tube of a paper roll has the shape of the lateral surface of a cylinder with a radius of 2 cm and a length of 25 cm. How many cm² of cardboard does the tube have? Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The tube has no bases: only the lateral surface area.

ro-052.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 3 · 5 = 30π cm²; area of one base = π · 3² = 9π cm².

ro-053.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 6 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 4 · 6 = 48π cm²; area of one base = π · 4² = 16π cm².

ro-054.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 5 · 5 = 50π cm²; area of one base = π · 5² = 25π cm².

ro-055.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 2 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + 2 · area of the base.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 2 · 8 = 32π cm²; area of one base = π · 2² = 4π cm².

ro-056.statement: A cylindrical mug without a lid has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the area of the material (ignoring its thickness). Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: A single base: the bottom.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 3 · 10 = 60π cm²; the bottom = π · 3² = 9π cm².
Area = 60π + 9π = 69π cm². Watch out: the mug has no lid, so it has a single base.

ro-057.statement: A pipe has the shape of the lateral surface of a cylinder, open at both ends, with a radius of 5 cm and a length of 9 cm. Calculate its area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The pipe has no bases.

ro-058.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 2 cm and a height of 3 cm. What is the total surface area?
hints: The lateral surface area plus two bases.
solution: A_l = 2 · π · 2 · 3 = 12π cm², two bases: 2 · π · 2² = 8π cm².
A_t = 12π + 8π = 20π cm². Watch out: 12π cm² is only the lateral surface area, 16π cm² has a single base.

ro-059.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a total surface area of 72π cm². Find the height.

ro-060.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = area of the base · height = πR² · h.

ro-061.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 2 cm and a height of 7 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = area of the base · height = πR² · h.

ro-062.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = area of the base · height = πR² · h.

ro-063.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = area of the base · height = πR² · h.

ro-064.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 5 cm and a volume of 200π cm³. Find the height.

ro-065.statement: A cylinder has a height of 3 cm and a volume of 147π cm³. Find the radius.

ro-066.statement: A cylinder has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 3 cm. What is the volume?
solution: Watch out: 24π cm² is the lateral surface area (2πRh), 16π cm² is the area of the base.

ro-067.statement: A cylindrical container has a radius of 10 cm and a height of 30 cm. How many liters of water fit in the container? Use π ≈ 3.14.

ro-068.statement: The right circular cone has vertex V and base center O. The height of the cone is the segment:
options: OA, with A on the circle of the base
VA, with A on the circle of the base
hints: The height goes down from the vertex, perpendicular to the base.
solution: VO ⊥ the plane of the base (O is the center of the base) ⇒ VO is the height. VA is a slant height, OA a radius, AB a diameter.

ro-069.statement: The right circular cone has vertex V. The slant height of the cone is the segment:
options: VO, with O the center of the base
OA, with O the center of the base
VA, with A on the circle of the base
hints: The slant height joins the vertex to a point on the circle of the base.
solution: The slant height joins the vertex V to a point A on the circle of the base; rotated around the axis, it describes the lateral surface.
Answer: VA, with A on the circle of the base.

ro-070.statement: In a right circular cone, all the slant heights:
options: they are equal to the radius
they are equal to the height
hints: The foot of the height is the center of the circle of the base.
solution: Each slant height VA is the hypotenuse of the right triangle VOA, with VO = h and OA = R the same ⇒ all the slant heights are equal.
Answer: they have the same length.

ro-071.statement: What relation is there between the slant height G, the height h and the radius R of a right circular cone?
hints: Triangle VOA is right-angled at O.
solution: In triangle VOA, right-angled at O, the hypotenuse is the slant height VA ⇒ G² = h² + R².

ro-072.statement: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A, with AB = 5 cm and AC = 12 cm. It rotates around leg AC. What is the radius of the base of the resulting cone?
hints: Leg AC becomes the height.
solution: AC is the axis (a height of 12 cm), and AB ⊥ AC describes the base ⇒ the radius is AB = 5 cm.

ro-073.statement: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A, with AB = 5 cm and AC = 12 cm. It rotates around leg AC. What is the slant height of the resulting cone?
hints: The slant height is the hypotenuse BC.
solution: The slant height is BC; BC² = 5² + 12² = 169 ⇒ BC = 13 cm.

ro-074.statement: Triangle ABC is right-angled at A, with AB = 8 cm and AC = 6 cm. It rotates around leg AB. What is the height of the resulting cone?
hints: The fixed leg is the height.
solution: AB stays fixed ⇒ the height is AB = 8 cm, and the radius is AC = 6 cm.

ro-075.statement: How many vertices does a right circular cone have?
hints: The base is a disk, with no corners.
solution: The cone has a single vertex, V: so 1 vertex; the circle of the base has no corners.

ro-076.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: The axial section is the isosceles triangle VAB, with base AB = 2R and height h.
solution: AB = 2 · 6 = 12 cm, the height of triangle VAB is 8 cm.

ro-077.statement: A cone has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: The axial section is the isosceles triangle VAB, with base AB = 2R and height h.
solution: AB = 2 · 5 = 10 cm, the height of triangle VAB is 12 cm.

ro-078.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the perimeter of the axial section.
hints: The sides of triangle VAB: two slant heights and a diameter.

ro-079.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the perimeter of the axial section.
hints: The sides of triangle VAB: two slant heights and a diameter.

ro-080.statement: The axial section of a right circular cone is:
hints: The plane passes through the vertex and through a diameter of the base.
solution: The plane that contains the axis cuts the base along a diameter AB and the lateral surface along two slant heights VA = VB ⇒ an isosceles triangle (equilateral only when G = 2R).

ro-081.statement: The axial section of a cone has an area of 60 cm², and the radius of the cone is 5 cm. Find the height of the cone.
hints: Area of the axial section = 2R · h ÷ 2 = R · h.

ro-082.statement: The axial section VAB of a cone has AB = 24 cm and VA = 13 cm. Find the height of the cone.
hints: The radius is half of AB.

ro-083.statement: The axial section VAB of a cone has VA = 10 cm, and the height of the cone is 8 cm. Find AB.
hints: Find the radius first.

ro-084.statement: A cone has a radius of 8 cm and a height of 15 cm. Calculate the slant height.
