ro-085.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the slant height.

ro-086.statement: A cone has a slant height of 10 cm and a radius of 6 cm. Calculate the height.

ro-087.statement: A cone has a slant height of 25 cm and a radius of 7 cm. Calculate the height.

ro-088.statement: A cone has a slant height of 17 cm and a height of 15 cm. Calculate the radius.

ro-089.statement: A cone has a radius of 2 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the slant height. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.

ro-090.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is the slant height?
hints: Pythagorean theorem in triangle VOA.
solution: Watch out: 14 cm is the sum (not the Pythagorean theorem), 2√7 cm comes from the difference 64 − 36, 100 is G², not G.

ro-091.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area of the cone = πRG.

ro-092.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area of the cone = πRG.

ro-093.statement: A cone has a radius of 5 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area of the cone = πRG.

ro-094.statement: A cone has a radius of 8 cm and a slant height of 17 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Lateral surface area of the cone = πRG.

ro-095.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: You need the slant height, not the height.
solution: A_l = π · 9 · 15 = 135π cm². Watch out: π · 9 · 12 uses the height instead of the slant height.

ro-096.statement: A cone has a lateral surface area of 65π cm² and a radius of 5 cm. Find the slant height.

ro-097.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. What is the lateral surface area?
solution: Watch out: 36π cm² is the area of the base, 120π cm² has an extra 2, 96π cm² is the total surface area.

ro-098.statement: A clown hat has the shape of the lateral surface of a cone with a radius of 10 cm and a slant height of 26 cm. How many cm² of cardboard is the hat made of? Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The hat has no base: only the lateral surface area.

ro-099.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: A_l = π · 3 · 5 = 15π cm²; area of the base = π · 3² = 9π cm².

ro-100.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: A_l = π · 6 · 10 = 60π cm²; area of the base = π · 6² = 36π cm².

ro-101.statement: A cone has a radius of 5 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: A_l = π · 5 · 13 = 65π cm²; area of the base = π · 5² = 25π cm².

ro-102.statement: A cone has a radius of 8 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the base.
solution: A_l = π · 8 · 10 = 80π cm²; area of the base = π · 8² = 64π cm².

ro-103.statement: A cone has a radius of 12 cm and a height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Find the slant height first.

ro-104.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Find the slant height first.

ro-105.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is the total surface area?
hints: The cone has a single base.
solution: Watch out: 15π cm² is only the lateral surface area, 33π cm² adds two bases (the cone has one), 12π cm³ is the volume.

ro-106.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a total surface area of 36π cm². Find the slant height.

ro-107.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the cone = πR²h ÷ 3.

ro-108.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the cone = πR²h ÷ 3.

ro-109.statement: A cone has a radius of 5 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the cone = πR²h ÷ 3.

ro-110.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the cone = πR²h ÷ 3.

ro-111.statement: A cone has a radius of 4 cm and a height of 3 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the cone = πR²h ÷ 3.

ro-112.statement: A cone has a radius of 8 cm and a slant height of 17 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Find the height first.

ro-113.statement: A cone has a volume of 100π cm³ and a radius of 5 cm. Find the height.

ro-114.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is the volume?
hints: Don't forget to divide by 3.
solution: Watch out: 288π cm³ is the volume of the cylinder with the same base and the same height (without dividing by 3).

ro-115.statement: The axial section of a cone is an equilateral triangle with a side of 10 cm. What is the radius of the cone?
hints: The base of the triangle is the diameter.
solution: AB = 10 cm is the diameter ⇒ R = 5 cm; the slant height is also 10 cm (G = 2R).

ro-116.statement: The axial section of a cone is an equilateral triangle with a side of 8 cm. Calculate the height of the cone. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: Height of the equilateral triangle = side · √3 ÷ 2.

ro-117.statement: A cone whose axial section is an equilateral triangle has a radius of 6 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The slant height is equal to the diameter.

ro-118.statement: A cone whose axial section is an equilateral triangle has a radius of 4 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: G = 2R, so A_t = πR · 2R + πR² = 3πR².

ro-119.statement: A cone whose axial section is an equilateral triangle has a radius of 3 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a√b·π cm³, with the radical simplified.

ro-120.statement: The slant height of a cone is 12 cm, and it is twice the radius. What figure is the axial section?
hints: Compare the sides VA, VB and AB.
solution: R = 6 cm ⇒ AB = 12 cm = VA = VB ⇒ the axial section is an equilateral triangle.

ro-121.statement: A cone has an equilateral triangle as its axial section. What is the measure of the angle between a slant height and the plane of the base?
hints: The projection of the slant height VA onto the base is the radius OA.
solution: The angle between VA and the base is ∠VAO, an angle of the equilateral triangle VAB ⇒ 60°.

ro-122.statement: The axial section of a cone is an equilateral triangle with a side of 6 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: Area of the equilateral triangle = side² · √3 ÷ 4.

ro-123.statement: The axial section of a cone is a right triangle, with the right angle at the vertex of the cone. The radius is 5 cm. What is the height of the cone?
hints: Triangle VAB is an isosceles right triangle, and VO is the median drawn from the right angle.
solution: In the right triangle VAB, the median VO = AB ÷ 2 = R ⇒ h = 5 cm.

ro-124.statement: The axial section of a cone is a right triangle (the right angle at the vertex), and the radius of the cone is 4 cm. Calculate the slant height. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.
hints: h = R, then the Pythagorean theorem.

ro-125.statement: A cone has a right triangle as its axial section, with the right angle at the vertex, and a radius of 3 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The height is equal to the radius.

ro-126.statement: A cone has a right triangle as its axial section, with the right angle at the vertex, and a radius of 6 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The height is equal to the radius.

ro-127.statement: A cone has a right triangle as its axial section, with the right angle at the vertex, and a radius of 2 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a√b·π cm², with the radical simplified.

ro-128.statement: A cone has a right triangle as its axial section, with the right angle at the vertex, and a radius of 7 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: Area = AB · VO ÷ 2, with VO = R.
solution: AB = 14 cm, VO = 7 cm ⇒ area = 14 · 7 ÷ 2 = 49 cm².

ro-129.statement: The axial section of a cone is a right triangle (the right angle at the vertex), and the slant height is 6√2 cm. Find the radius.

ro-130.statement: The axial section of a cone is a right triangle, with the right angle at the vertex. What is the measure of the angle between a slant height and the plane of the base?
hints: Triangle VOA is an isosceles right triangle.
solution: VO = OA = R ⇒ triangle VOA is an isosceles right triangle ⇒ ∠VAO = 45°.

ro-131.statement: The axial section of a cone has an angle of 90° at the vertex of the cone. Then:
hints: The median from the right angle is half the hypotenuse.
solution: VO is the median from the right angle of triangle VAB ⇒ VO = AB ÷ 2 = R, that is, h = R (and G = R√2).

ro-132.statement: A cone has a radius of 3 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. The lateral surface unfolds into a circular sector. Calculate the measure of the angle of the sector.
hints: The arc of the sector becomes the circle of the base: angle = 360° · R ÷ G.
solution: The arc of the sector (with radius 5 cm) is as long as the circumference of the base, 2 · π · 3 = 6π cm.

ro-133.statement: A cone has a radius of 4 cm and a slant height of 12 cm. The lateral surface unfolds into a circular sector. Calculate the measure of the angle of the sector.
hints: The arc of the sector becomes the circle of the base: angle = 360° · R ÷ G.
solution: The arc of the sector (with radius 12 cm) is as long as the circumference of the base, 2 · π · 4 = 8π cm.

ro-134.statement: A cone has a radius of 5 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. The lateral surface unfolds into a circular sector. Calculate the measure of the angle of the sector.
hints: The arc of the sector becomes the circle of the base: angle = 360° · R ÷ G.
solution: The arc of the sector (with radius 10 cm) is as long as the circumference of the base, 2 · π · 5 = 10π cm.

ro-135.statement: A cone has a radius of 6 cm and a slant height of 8 cm. The lateral surface unfolds into a circular sector. Calculate the measure of the angle of the sector.
hints: The arc of the sector becomes the circle of the base: angle = 360° · R ÷ G.
solution: The arc of the sector (with radius 8 cm) is as long as the circumference of the base, 2 · π · 6 = 12π cm.

ro-136.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a cone is a circular sector with a radius of 9 cm and an angle of 120°. What is the radius of the base of the cone?
hints: Length of the arc = circumference of the base.

ro-137.statement: The sector in the net of the lateral surface of a cone has a radius of 15 cm, and its arc has a length of 18π cm. What is the radius of the base of the cone?
hints: The arc wraps around the circle of the base.
solution: 2 · π · R = 18π ⇒ R = 9 cm (the slant height is 15 cm).

ro-138.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a right circular cone is:
options: a circular sector with a radius equal to the slant height
a circular sector with a radius equal to the radius of the base
hints: All the slant heights start from the vertex and have the same length.
solution: The slant heights become radii of a disk with radius G; the arc is as long as the circumference of the base ⇒ a circular sector with radius G.
Answer: a circular sector with a radius equal to the slant height.

ro-139.statement: The net of the lateral surface of a cone is a sector with a radius of 10 cm and an angle of 216°. Calculate the area of the sector. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Area of the sector = π · radius² · angle ÷ 360°.
solution: Check: radius of the base = 10 · 216 ÷ 360 = 6 cm and A_l = π · 6 · 10 = 60π cm².

ro-140.statement: The sphere with center O and radius R is the set of points in space:
options: at a distance less than R from O
at a distance of at most R from O, in a plane
hints: The sphere is only the “shell.”
solution: The sphere is made of the points in space that are exactly at distance R from the center; the points at a distance ≤ R form the ball (the solid sphere).
Answer: at distance R from O.

ro-141.statement: The ball (the solid sphere) with center O and radius R is made of the points:
options: at a distance greater than R from O
at a distance of at most R from O
in the plane of the equator
hints: The ball includes its interior.
solution: The ball contains the sphere and its whole interior: the points whose distance to O is less than or equal to R.
Answer: at a distance of at most R from O.

ro-142.statement: A sphere has a diameter of 18 cm. What is the radius?
hints: The radius is half the diameter.

ro-143.statement: The sphere has center O and a radius of 5 cm. Point P is 3 cm from O. Where is P?
hints: Compare OP with the radius.
solution: OP = 3 cm < 5 cm = R ⇒ P is inside the sphere (in the ball, but not on the sphere).

ro-144.statement: The sphere has center O and a radius of 5 cm. Point Q is 8 cm from O. Where is Q?
options: at the center of the sphere
hints: Compare OQ with the radius.
solution: OQ = 8 cm > 5 cm = R ⇒ Q is outside the sphere.

ro-145.statement: What is the length of the longest segment with both endpoints on a sphere with a radius of 6 cm?
hints: The longest segment passes through the center.
solution: The longest segment with its endpoints on the sphere is a diameter: 2 · 6 = 12 cm.

ro-146.statement: Two diametrically opposite points of a sphere are 20 cm apart. What is the radius of the sphere?
hints: The segment between them is a diameter.

ro-147.statement: Point A lies on the sphere with center O and a radius of 7 cm. What is OA?
hints: All the points of the sphere are at distance R from the center.
solution: A is on the sphere ⇒ OA = R = 7 cm.

ro-148.statement: The section of a sphere by a plane that has more than one point in common with it is:
hints: The foot of the perpendicular from the center to the plane is the center of the section.
solution: All the common points are at distance R from O; since they are also in the plane, they are at the same distance from the foot of the perpendicular from O to the plane ⇒ a circle.

ro-149.statement: A plane passes through the center of a sphere. The section is:
options: a circle with a radius half the radius of the sphere
a great circle, with a radius equal to the radius of the sphere
a circle with twice the radius
hints: The distance from the center to the plane is 0.
solution: The plane passes through O ⇒ the radius of the section is √(R² − 0²) = R: the section is a great circle.
Answer: a great circle, with a radius equal to the radius of the sphere.

ro-150.statement: A sphere has a radius of 8 cm. Calculate the area of the disk determined by a plane that passes through the center of the sphere. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The great disk has the radius of the sphere.

ro-151.statement: A sphere has a radius of 9 cm. Calculate the circumference of a great circle of the sphere. Write the result as a·π cm by filling in a.
hints: The great circle has the radius of the sphere.

ro-152.statement: The distance from the center of a sphere with a radius of 5 cm to a plane is 7 cm. The plane and the sphere:
options: they have only one common point
they intersect along a great circle
hints: Compare the distance with the radius.
solution: d = 7 cm > R = 5 cm ⇒ the plane is exterior to the sphere: no common point.
Answer: they have no common point.

ro-153.statement: The distance from the center of a sphere with a radius of 5 cm to a plane is 5 cm. The plane and the sphere:
options: they intersect along a small circle
they intersect along a great circle
they have only one common point (the plane is tangent)
solution: d = R ⇒ the plane touches the sphere at a single point: it is a tangent plane.
Answer: they have only one common point (the plane is tangent).

ro-154.statement: The distance from the center of a sphere with a radius of 5 cm to a plane is 3 cm. The plane and the sphere:
options: they have only one common point
they intersect along a great circle
solution: 0 < d = 3 cm < R ⇒ the plane cuts the sphere along a circle (with radius √(25 − 9) = 4 cm, so not a great circle).
Answer: they intersect along a circle.

ro-155.statement: How many great circles of a sphere pass through two diametrically opposite points of the sphere?
hints: Think of the meridians on a globe.
solution: Any plane that contains the diameter determined by the two points passes through the center ⇒ it gives a great circle. There are infinitely many such planes (like the meridians that pass through the two poles).

ro-156.statement: Through two distinct points of a sphere that are NOT diametrically opposite, there pass:
hints: The two points and the center are not collinear.
solution: The two points and the center O are not collinear ⇒ they determine a single plane, which passes through O ⇒ a single great circle.

ro-157.statement: A sphere with a radius of 10 cm is cut by a plane 6 cm from the center. Calculate the radius of the section circle.
hints: The radius of the sphere, the distance and the radius of the section form a right triangle.

ro-158.statement: A sphere with a radius of 13 cm is cut by a plane 5 cm from the center. Calculate the radius of the section circle.
hints: The radius of the sphere, the distance and the radius of the section form a right triangle.

ro-159.statement: A sphere with a radius of 5 cm is cut by a plane 4 cm from the center. Calculate the radius of the section circle.
hints: The radius of the sphere, the distance and the radius of the section form a right triangle.

ro-160.statement: A sphere with a radius of 17 cm is cut by a plane 8 cm from the center. Calculate the radius of the section circle.
hints: The radius of the sphere, the distance and the radius of the section form a right triangle.

ro-161.statement: A plane 9 cm from the center of a sphere cuts it along a circle with a radius of 12 cm. Calculate the radius of the sphere.

ro-162.statement: A sphere with a radius of 25 cm is cut by a plane along a circle with a radius of 24 cm. How far from the center is the plane?

ro-163.statement: A sphere with a radius of 10 cm is cut by a plane 8 cm from the center. Calculate the area of the section. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Find the radius of the section first.

ro-164.statement: A sphere with a radius of 6 cm is cut by a plane 4 cm from the center. Calculate the radius of the section. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.

ro-165.statement: A plane tangent to a sphere is:
options: a plane that cuts the sphere along a great circle
a plane that passes through the center
perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact
parallel to the radius drawn to the point of contact
hints: Just like with the circle: the tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
solution: The distance from the center to the tangent plane is R, and it is reached exactly at the point of contact ⇒ the radius OT is perpendicular to the plane.
Answer: perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact.

ro-166.statement: A sphere with a radius of 6 cm is tangent to plane α. What is the distance from the center of the sphere to plane α?
hints: For a tangent plane, the distance is equal to the radius.
solution: Tangent plane ⇔ d = R ⇒ the distance is 6 cm.

ro-167.statement: A ball sits on a horizontal table (it touches it at a single point). The center of the ball is 11 cm above the table. What is the diameter of the ball?
hints: The table is a plane tangent to the ball.
solution: The table is tangent to the ball ⇒ the distance from the center to the table is the radius: R = 11 cm.

ro-168.statement: Point A lies on the sphere with center O, and plane α passes through A and is perpendicular to the radius OA. Then plane α is:
options: a plane that passes through O
tangent to the sphere at A
hints: The distance from O to α is OA.
solution: OA ⊥ α ⇒ d(O, α) = OA = R ⇒ α is tangent to the sphere (the converse: the plane perpendicular to a radius at its endpoint is tangent).
Answer: tangent to the sphere at A.

ro-169.statement: A plane α passes through point A of the sphere with center O, but it is NOT perpendicular to the radius OA. Then α:
options: has no point in common with the sphere
is tangent to the sphere at A
cuts the sphere along a circle
hints: The distance from O to α is less than OA.
solution: The perpendicular from O to α is shorter than the oblique segment OA ⇒ d(O, α) < R ⇒ the plane cuts the sphere along a circle, and this circle passes through A.
Answer: cuts the sphere along a circle.

ro-170.statement: Calculate the area of the sphere with a radius of 3 cm. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Area of the sphere = 4πR².

ro-171.statement: Calculate the area of the sphere with a radius of 5 cm. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Area of the sphere = 4πR².

ro-172.statement: Calculate the area of the sphere with a radius of 7 cm. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Area of the sphere = 4πR².

ro-173.statement: A sphere has a diameter of 12 cm. Calculate the area of the sphere. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Careful: the formula uses the radius.
solution: A = 4 · π · 6² = 144π cm². Watch out: with the diameter instead of the radius you would get 576π cm².

ro-174.statement: The area of a sphere is 64π cm². Find the radius of the sphere.

ro-175.statement: The area of a sphere is 324π cm². Find the radius of the sphere.

ro-176.statement: What is the area of a sphere with a radius of 2 cm?
solution: Watch out: 4π cm² is the area of a great circle, 8π cm² would come from 4πR (without the square).

ro-177.statement: A great circle of a sphere bounds a disk with an area of 25π cm². Calculate the area of the sphere. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The area of the sphere is 4 times the area of the great disk.
solution: A = 4 · π · 5² = 100π cm² (4 times the area of the great disk).

ro-178.statement: A ball has a radius of 10 cm. How many cm² of material cover its surface? Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The area of the sphere.

ro-179.statement: Calculate the volume of the ball with a radius of 3 cm. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the ball = 4πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-180.statement: Calculate the volume of the ball with a radius of 6 cm. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the ball = 4πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-181.statement: Calculate the volume of the ball with a radius of 9 cm. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the ball = 4πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-182.statement: A ball has a diameter of 12 cm. Calculate its volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Use the radius, not the diameter.

ro-183.statement: The volume of a ball is 36π cm³. Find the radius.

ro-184.statement: What is the volume of the ball with a radius of 3 cm?
hints: Don't forget to divide by 3.
solution: Watch out: 108π cm³ comes from forgetting the division by 3, 27π cm³ comes from forgetting the factor 4 ÷ 3.

ro-185.statement: The radius of a ball doubles. How many times larger does the volume get?
hints: The volume depends on R³.
solution: V′ ÷ V = (2R)³ ÷ R³ = 2³ = 8 ⇒ the volume becomes 8 times larger (the area becomes only 4 times larger).

ro-186.statement: For what radius are the area of the sphere (in cm²) and the volume of the ball (in cm³) expressed by the same number?
hints: 4πR² = 4πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-187.statement: Calculate the volume of a solid hemisphere with a radius of 3 cm. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The solid hemisphere has half the volume of the ball: 2πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-188.statement: Calculate the volume of a solid hemisphere with a radius of 6 cm. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The solid hemisphere has half the volume of the ball: 2πR³ ÷ 3.

ro-189.statement: A bowl has the shape of a hemisphere (without a lid) with a radius of 5 cm. Calculate the area of its curved surface. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Half the area of the sphere.

ro-190.statement: A solid hemisphere has a radius of 4 cm. Calculate its total surface area (the curved surface and the base disk). Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
solution: The curved surface: 2 · π · 4² = 32π cm²; the disk: π · 4² = 16π cm².

ro-191.statement: A solid hemisphere has a radius of 5 cm. Calculate its total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Don't forget the flat disk.

ro-192.statement: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere with radius R is:
hints: The curved surface plus the base disk.
solution: 2πR² (half of the sphere) + πR² (the disk) = 3πR². Watch out: 2πR² comes from forgetting the flat disk.

ro-193.statement: A hemispherical bowl has a radius of 9 cm. How many cm³ of soup fit in it (filled to the brim)? Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The volume of the solid hemisphere.

ro-194.statement: A solid hemisphere has a volume of 144π cm³. Find the radius.

ro-195.statement: A silo is made of a cylinder with a radius of 3 m and a height of 10 m, topped with a cone with the same base and a height of 4 m. Calculate the volume of the silo. Write the result as a·π m³ by filling in a.
hints: Add the volume of the cylinder and the volume of the cone.
solution: V (cylinder) = π · 3² · 10 = 90π m³; V (cone) = π · 3² · 4 ÷ 3 = 12π m³.

ro-196.statement: A tower has the shape of a cylinder with a radius of 3 m and a height of 8 m, topped with a hemisphere with the same radius. Calculate the volume of the tower. Write the result as a·π m³ by filling in a.
hints: Cylinder + solid hemisphere.
solution: V (cylinder) = π · 3² · 8 = 72π m³; V (solid hemisphere) = 2 · π · 3³ ÷ 3 = 18π m³.

ro-197.statement: A cone with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm is filled with ice cream and topped with a hemisphere of ice cream with a radius of 3 cm. Calculate the volume of the ice cream. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Cone + solid hemisphere with the same radius.
solution: V (cone) = π · 3² · 10 ÷ 3 = 30π cm³; V (solid hemisphere) = 2 · π · 3³ ÷ 3 = 18π cm³.

ro-198.statement: From a cylinder with a radius of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm, a cone with the same base and the same height is hollowed out. Calculate the volume that remains. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The cone has one third of the volume of the cylinder.
solution: What remains is 288π − 96π = 192π cm³ (two thirds of the cylinder).

ro-199.statement: A ball with a radius of 6 cm is placed in a cylinder with a radius of 6 cm and a height of 12 cm (the ball touches both bases and the side). What volume is left empty in the cylinder? Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Subtract the volume of the ball from the volume of the cylinder.
solution: V (cylinder) = π · 6² · 12 = 432π cm³; V (ball) = 4 · π · 6³ ÷ 3 = 288π cm³.
Left empty: 432π − 288π = 144π cm³ (one third of the cylinder).

ro-200.statement: A cone full of water is emptied into an empty cylinder with the same base and the same height. What fraction of the cylinder gets filled? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: Compare the volumes.
solution: V (cone) = πR²h ÷ 3, V (cylinder) = πR²h ⇒ the water fills 1/3 of the cylinder.

ro-201.statement: A conical container with a radius of 4 cm and a height of 12 cm, full of water, is emptied into a cylindrical container with a radius of 4 cm. How high does the water rise in the cylinder?
hints: The volume of the water stays the same.
solution: π · 4² · h = 64π ⇒ 16 · h = 64 ⇒ h = 4 cm (one third of the height of the cone: the bases are equal).

ro-202.statement: In a cylindrical container with a radius of 6 cm, holding water, a metal ball with a radius of 3 cm is completely submerged. By how many cm does the water level rise?
hints: The ball displaces a volume of water equal to its own volume.

ro-203.statement: A lead ball with a radius of 6 cm is melted, and the lead is made into small balls, each with a radius of 2 cm. How many small balls do you get?
hints: The volume stays the same; the ratio of the radii is 3.

ro-204.statement: A modeling clay cylinder with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm is reshaped into a cone with the same radius. What is the height of the cone?
hints: The volume stays the same; the cone needs three times the height.

ro-205.statement: A cylindrical glass has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 10 cm. How many full glasses are needed to fill a 2 l bottle? Use π ≈ 3.14 and round up to a whole number of glasses.
solution: 2000 ÷ 282.6 ≈ 7.08 ⇒ 8 glasses are needed (7 are not enough).

ft-001.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a height of 9 cm. A plane parallel to the base, located 3 cm from the vertex, cuts the pyramid along the square MNPQ. Calculate the side MN.
hints: The small pyramid VMNPQ is similar to VABCD; the ratio is 3 ÷ 9.

ft-002.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and a height of 9 cm. A plane parallel to the base, located 3 cm from the vertex, cuts the pyramid along the square MNPQ. Calculate the area of the section.
hints: The ratio of the areas is k².
solution: Area of the section = 4² = 16 cm² (that is, 144 · 1/9).

ft-003.statement: A pyramid has a base area of 36 cm². A plane parallel to the base passes through the midpoint of the height. Calculate the area of the section.
hints: The similarity ratio is 1/2, and the ratio of the areas is (1/2)².

ft-004.statement: The section of a pyramid by a plane parallel to the base is:
options: a polygon similar to the base
a polygon congruent to the base
hints: The sides of the section are parallel to the sides of the base.
solution: Each side of the section is parallel to a side of the base, and they all shrink in the same ratio (Thales's theorem in the lateral faces) ⇒ the section is similar to the base.
Answer: a polygon similar to the base.

ft-005.statement: A plane parallel to the base of a pyramid cuts it so that the similarity ratio between the small pyramid and the large one is 1/3. What fraction of the area of the base is the area of the section? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The ratio of the areas is the square of the similarity ratio.

ft-006.statement: A pyramid has a volume of 270 cm³. A plane parallel to the base, drawn at one third of the height measured from the vertex, cuts off a small pyramid. Calculate the volume of the small pyramid.
hints: The ratio of the volumes is the cube of the similarity ratio.

ft-007.statement: A plane parallel to the base of a pyramid passes through the midpoint of the height. What fraction of the volume of the pyramid is the small pyramid above the plane? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.

ft-008.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 12 cm and lateral edge VA = 15 cm. A plane parallel to the base cuts edge VA at point M, with VM = 5 cm. Calculate the side of the section.
hints: The similarity ratio can also be read on the lateral edge: VM ÷ VA.

ft-009.statement: The distance from the vertex of a pyramid to a section parallel to the base is 2/5 of the height. What fraction of the area of the base is the area of the section? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.

ft-010.statement: In the regular tetrahedron VABC with an edge of 6 cm, a plane parallel to the base ABC passes through the midpoints of the edges VA, VB, VC. Calculate the perimeter of the section.
hints: The sides of the section are midsegments in the lateral faces.
solution: Each side of the section is a midsegment in a face: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.

ft-011.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. A plane parallel to the base, located 4 cm from the vertex, cuts the cone. Calculate the radius of the section.
hints: The small cone on top is similar to the large cone: ratio 4 ÷ 12.

ft-012.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. A plane parallel to the base, located 4 cm from the vertex, cuts the cone. Calculate the area of the section. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Find the radius of the section first.

ft-013.statement: A plane parallel to the base of a cone passes through the midpoint of the height. What fraction of the area of the base is the area of the section? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The radius of the section is half the radius of the base.
solution: The radius of the section is R ÷ 2 ⇒ its area is π · R² ÷ 4.

ft-014.statement: A cone has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 12 cm. A plane parallel to the base, located 4 cm from the vertex, cuts off a small cone. Calculate the volume of the small cone. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: The small cone has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm.
solution: V = π · 3² · 4 ÷ 3 = 12π cm³ (one twenty-seventh of 324π cm³).

ft-015.statement: The section of a cone by a plane parallel to the base (between the base and the vertex) is:
hints: The edge of the section has all its points at the same distance from the axis.
solution: The plane parallel to the base cuts the cone along a disk centered on the axis; its radius is smaller than the radius of the base.

ft-016.statement: A cone has a radius of 10 cm and a height of 15 cm. A plane parallel to the base is 6 cm from the base. Calculate the radius of the section.
hints: Careful: the similarity ratio is taken from the vertex.
solution: Distance from the vertex to the section: 15 − 6 = 9 cm ⇒ k = 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5.
r = 10 · 3/5 = 6 cm. Watch out: 10 · 6 ÷ 15 = 4 cm would use the distance from the base.

ft-017.statement: A cone has a slant height of 20 cm and a radius of 12 cm. A plane parallel to the base cuts a slant height VA at point M, with VM = 5 cm. Calculate the radius of the section.
hints: k = VM ÷ VA.

ft-018.statement: A plane parallel to the base of a cone passes through the midpoint of the height. What fraction of the volume of the cone remains below the plane (in the frustum of the cone)? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The small cone has 1/8 of the volume.

ft-019.statement: A frustum of a pyramid is obtained:
options: by cutting a pyramid with a plane parallel to the base and keeping the part between the base and the section
by gluing two pyramids together at their bases
by cutting a prism with any plane
by cutting a pyramid with a plane that passes through the vertex
hints: The bottom part of the pyramid remains.
solution: The plane parallel to the base cuts off a small pyramid (at the top); the part that remains between the base and the section is the frustum of the pyramid.
Answer: by cutting a pyramid with a plane parallel to the base and keeping the part between the base and the section.

ft-020.statement: The bases of a frustum of a pyramid are:
options: two congruent polygons, in parallel planes
two similar polygons, in parallel planes
hints: The smaller base is the section parallel to the larger base.
solution: The smaller base is a section parallel to the larger base ⇒ the two bases are similar (not congruent) and lie in parallel planes.
Answer: two similar polygons, in parallel planes.

ft-021.statement: The lateral faces of a frustum of a regular pyramid are:
hints: Each lateral face has one side on the larger base and one, parallel to it, on the smaller base.
solution: Each face has two parallel sides (on the two bases) and equal lateral edges ⇒ isosceles trapezoid; in the frustum of a regular pyramid they are all congruent.

ft-022.statement: The height of a frustum of a pyramid is:
options: the height of a lateral face
the distance between the planes of the two bases
the diagonal of the larger base
the length of a lateral edge
hints: As with the prism: the distance between the bases.
solution: The height of the frustum is the distance between the planes of the bases; the height of a lateral face is called the slant height of the frustum.
Answer: the distance between the planes of the two bases.

ft-023.statement: How many faces does a frustum of a quadrilateral pyramid have?
hints: 2 bases and 4 lateral faces.

ft-024.statement: How many edges does a frustum of a quadrilateral pyramid have?
hints: 4 on the bottom, 4 on the top and 4 lateral.
solution: 4 edges of the larger base + 4 of the smaller base + 4 lateral edges = 12.

ft-025.statement: How many vertices does a frustum of a triangular pyramid have?
hints: The vertices of the two bases.
solution: 3 vertices on the bottom + 3 on the top = 6 vertices.

ft-026.statement: How many faces does a frustum of a hexagonal pyramid have?
hints: 2 bases and one lateral face for each side.

ft-027.statement: How many lateral edges does a frustum of a hexagonal pyramid have?
hints: Each vertex of the larger base is joined to the corresponding vertex of the smaller base.
solution: One lateral edge for each vertex of the base: 6 lateral edges (6 + 6 + 6 = 18 edges in total).

ft-028.statement: The slant height of a frustum of a regular pyramid is:
options: the height of a lateral face (of the isosceles trapezoid)
the apothem of the larger base
hints: As with the pyramid, the slant height lies on a lateral face.
solution: The slant height of the frustum is the height of the isosceles trapezoid that forms a lateral face; it joins the midpoints of two parallel sides, one on each base.
Answer: the height of a lateral face (of the isosceles trapezoid).

ft-029.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the slant height of the frustum.
hints: Draw the height of the frustum from the upper end of the slant height: you get a right triangle with legs h and (L − l) ÷ 2, and its hypotenuse is the slant height.
solution: The apothems of the bases are 6 cm and 3 cm; their difference: (12 − 6) ÷ 2 = 3 cm.

ft-030.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 16 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the slant height of the frustum.
hints: Draw the height of the frustum from the upper end of the slant height: you get a right triangle with legs h and (L − l) ÷ 2, and its hypotenuse is the slant height.
solution: The apothems of the bases are 8 cm and 2 cm; their difference: (16 − 4) ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

ft-031.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 14 cm and 4 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the slant height of the frustum.
hints: Draw the height of the frustum from the upper end of the slant height: you get a right triangle with legs h and (L − l) ÷ 2, and its hypotenuse is the slant height.
solution: The apothems of the bases are 7 cm and 2 cm; their difference: (14 − 4) ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

ft-032.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the lateral edge. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified (if there is no number in front of the radical, enter 1 as the coefficient).
hints: The projection of the lateral edge onto the larger base is the difference between the half-diagonals.
solution: Half-diagonals: 6√2 cm and 3√2 cm; difference: 3√2 cm.

ft-033.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm, and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the height of the frustum.
hints: h² = slant height² − ((L − l) ÷ 2)².

ft-034.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has a smaller base side of 4 cm, a height of 8 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the side of the larger base.
hints: First find (L − l) ÷ 2.

ft-035.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the slant height?
hints: Use (L − l) ÷ 2, not L − l.
solution: (10 − 4) ÷ 2 = 3 cm; slant height² = 4² + 3² = 25 ⇒ slant height = 5 cm.
Watch out: with L − l = 6 instead of 3 you would get √52 cm.

ft-036.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = 4 trapezoids = (perimeter of the larger base + perimeter of the smaller base) · slant height ÷ 2.

ft-037.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 16 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = 4 trapezoids = (perimeter of the larger base + perimeter of the smaller base) · slant height ÷ 2.

ft-038.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 14 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: Lateral surface area = 4 trapezoids = (perimeter of the larger base + perimeter of the smaller base) · slant height ÷ 2.

ft-039.statement: A frustum of a regular triangular pyramid has base sides of 10 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 6 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area.
hints: 3 congruent isosceles trapezoids.

ft-040.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a lateral surface area of 180 cm². Calculate the slant height.
hints: A_l = 4 · (L + l) · slant height ÷ 2.
solution: 4 · (12 + 6) · slant height ÷ 2 = 180 ⇒ 36 · slant height = 180 ⇒ slant height = 5 cm.

ft-041.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is the lateral surface area?
hints: 4 lateral faces.
solution: Watch out: 45 cm² is a single face, 360 cm² is the total surface area.

ft-042.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the larger base + area of the smaller base.

ft-043.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 16 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the larger base + area of the smaller base.

ft-044.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 14 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the total surface area.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + area of the larger base + area of the smaller base.

ft-045.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 10 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is the total surface area?
hints: Two bases, of different sizes.
solution: A_l = 4 · (10 + 4) · 5 ÷ 2 = 140 cm²; the bases: 100 cm² and 16 cm².
A_t = 140 + 100 + 16 = 256 cm². Watch out: 240 cm² comes from adding only the larger base to the lateral surface area, 140 cm² is only the lateral surface area.

ft-046.statement: A flowerpot has the shape of a frustum of a regular square pyramid, without a lid, with the side of the larger base (the opening) measuring 16 cm, the side of the bottom measuring 4 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. How many cm² of material is the flowerpot made of?
hints: Without the opening: lateral surface area + the bottom.
solution: Area = 400 + 16 = 416 cm² (the opening has no material).

ft-047.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume.
hints: V = h · (B + b + √(B · b)) ÷ 3, where B and b are the areas of the bases.
solution: B = 144 cm², b = 36 cm², √(B · b) = 72 cm².

ft-048.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 16 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the volume.
hints: V = h · (B + b + √(B · b)) ÷ 3, where B and b are the areas of the bases.
solution: B = 256 cm², b = 16 cm², √(B · b) = 64 cm².

ft-049.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 6 cm. Calculate the volume.
hints: V = h · (B + b + √(B · b)) ÷ 3, where B and b are the areas of the bases.
solution: B = 100 cm², b = 16 cm², √(B · b) = 40 cm².

ft-050.statement: A frustum of a regular square pyramid has base sides of 12 cm and 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the volume?
hints: Don't forget the term √(B · b) and the division by 3.
solution: Watch out: 240 cm³ comes from forgetting √(B · b) = 72, 1008 cm³ comes from forgetting the division by 3.

ft-051.statement: A frustum of a pyramid has base areas of 50 cm² and 8 cm² and a height of 6 cm. Calculate the volume.

ft-052.statement: A regular square pyramid with a base side of 12 cm and a height of 9 cm is cut by a plane parallel to the base, 3 cm from the vertex. Calculate the volume of the remaining frustum.
hints: Volume of the frustum = volume of the large pyramid − volume of the small pyramid.
solution: V (large pyramid) = 12² · 9 ÷ 3 = 432 cm³; the small pyramid has side 4 cm and height 3 cm: V (small pyramid) = 4² · 3 ÷ 3 = 16 cm³.

ft-053.statement: A frustum of a cone is obtained:
options: by rotating a rectangle around one of its sides
by cutting a cone with a plane parallel to the base and keeping the part between the base and the section
by cutting a cylinder with an oblique plane
by gluing two cones together at their bases
hints: The bottom part of the cone remains.
solution: The plane parallel to the base cuts off a small cone; the part between the base and the section is the frustum of the cone.
Answer: by cutting a cone with a plane parallel to the base and keeping the part between the base and the section.

ft-054.statement: The bases of a frustum of a cone are:
options: two disks with different radii, in parallel planes
hints: The smaller base is a section parallel to the base of the cone.
solution: The larger base and the smaller base are disks in parallel planes, with R > r.
Answer: two disks with different radii, in parallel planes.

ft-055.statement: What solid do you get by rotating a right trapezoid around the side perpendicular to the bases?
hints: The bases of the trapezoid become the radii of the two bases of the solid.
solution: The side perpendicular to the bases is the axis (the height), the bases of the trapezoid describe the two disks, and the slanted side describes the lateral surface ⇒ frustum of a cone.
Answer: a frustum of a cone.

ft-056.statement: In a frustum of a right circular cone, all the slant heights:
options: they are equal to the height
they are equal to the difference of the radii
hints: The frustum is symmetric about the axis.
solution: Each slant height is the slanted side of a right trapezoid with the same dimensions (height h, bases R and r) ⇒ they are all equal.
Answer: they have the same length.

ft-057.statement: If we extend the slant heights of a frustum of a cone, they meet:
options: at the center of the larger base
at the center of the smaller base
at a point on the axis: the vertex of the cone the frustum comes from
hints: The frustum is a cone whose tip has been cut off.
solution: The slant heights of the frustum are pieces of the slant heights of the original cone ⇒ when extended, they all pass through its vertex, which lies on the axis.
Answer: at a point on the axis: the vertex of the cone the frustum comes from.

ft-058.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm. What is the diameter of the smaller base?
hints: The smaller base has the smaller radius.
solution: The smaller base has radius r = 4 cm ⇒ diameter = 8 cm.

ft-059.statement: The axial section of a frustum of a cone is:
hints: The plane cuts the bases along two parallel diameters of different lengths.
solution: The plane that contains the axis cuts the bases along the diameters 2R and 2r (parallel) and the lateral surface along two equal slant heights ⇒ isosceles trapezoid.

ft-060.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: Isosceles trapezoid with bases 2R and 2r and height h.
solution: Bases of the trapezoid: 14 cm and 8 cm.

ft-061.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.
hints: Isosceles trapezoid with bases 2R and 2r and height h.
solution: Bases of the trapezoid: 20 cm and 8 cm.

ft-062.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the perimeter of the axial section.
hints: Sides of the trapezoid: 2R, 2r and two slant heights.

ft-063.statement: The axial section of a frustum of a cone is an isosceles trapezoid with bases of 20 cm and 8 cm and an area of 112 cm². Calculate the height of the frustum.
hints: Area of the trapezoid = (B + b) · h ÷ 2.

ft-064.statement: The axial section ABCD of a frustum of a cone has AB = 20 cm (the diameter of the larger base), CD = 8 cm and AD = 10 cm. Calculate the height of the frustum.
hints: Drop an altitude from D: the horizontal leg is R − r.
solution: R = 10 cm, r = 4 cm ⇒ R − r = 6 cm.

ft-065.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 9 cm and 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the area of the axial section.

ft-066.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the slant height.

ft-067.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the slant height.

ft-068.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 8 cm and 3 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the slant height.

ft-069.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 9 cm and 3 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the height.

ft-070.statement: A frustum of a cone has a larger base radius of 8 cm, a height of 12 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the radius of the smaller base.
hints: First find R − r.

ft-071.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 5 cm and 3 cm and a height of 2 cm. Calculate the slant height. Write the result as a√b cm, with the radical simplified.

ft-072.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the slant height?
hints: The horizontal leg is R − r, not R + r and not R.
solution: Watch out: with R + r = 11 you would get √137 cm, with R = 7 you would get √65 cm.

ft-073.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.

ft-074.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.

ft-075.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 8 cm and 3 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.

ft-076.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 9 cm and 3 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the lateral surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.

ft-077.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is the lateral surface area?
solution: Watch out: 15π cm² uses R − r, 120π cm² is the total surface area.

ft-078.statement: A lampshade has the shape of the lateral surface of a frustum of a cone with radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. How many cm² of fabric are needed? Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Find the slant height first.

ft-079.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + the two bases.
solution: A_l = π · 5 · 11 = 55π cm²; the bases: 49π and 16π cm².

ft-080.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 10 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + the two bases.
solution: A_l = π · 10 · 14 = 140π cm²; the bases: 100π and 16π cm².

ft-081.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 8 cm and 3 cm and a slant height of 13 cm. Calculate the total surface area. Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: Total surface area = lateral surface area + the two bases.
solution: A_l = π · 13 · 11 = 143π cm²; the bases: 64π and 9π cm².

ft-082.statement: A bucket without a lid has the shape of a frustum of a cone: the opening has a radius of 7 cm, the bottom a radius of 4 cm, and the slant height is 5 cm. How many cm² of sheet metal is the bucket made of? Write the result as a·π cm² by filling in a.
hints: The bottom is the smaller base; the opening has no sheet metal.
solution: A_l = π · 5 · (7 + 4) = 55π cm²; the bottom: π · 4² = 16π cm².

ft-083.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a slant height of 5 cm. What is the total surface area?
hints: Both bases.
solution: Watch out: 104π cm² comes from adding only the larger base to the lateral surface area, 71π cm² from adding only the smaller base, 55π cm² is the lateral surface area.

ft-084.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = πh(R² + r² + R · r) ÷ 3.

ft-085.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 10 cm and 4 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = πh(R² + r² + R · r) ÷ 3.

ft-086.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 9 cm and 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = πh(R² + r² + R · r) ÷ 3.

ft-087.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 8 cm and 3 cm and a height of 12 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: V = πh(R² + r² + R · r) ÷ 3.

ft-088.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 7 cm and 4 cm and a height of 4 cm. What is the volume?
hints: Don't forget the term R · r and the division by 3.
solution: Watch out: 372π cm³ comes from forgetting the division by 3, 88π cm³ comes from forgetting the term R · r.

ft-089.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 6 cm and 3 cm and a height of 4 cm. Extend the slant heights up to the vertex of the cone the frustum comes from. What is the height of the small cone that was cut off?
hints: The small cone and the large cone are similar: x ÷ (x + 4) = 3 ÷ 6.
solution: (The large cone has a height of 8 cm.)

ft-090.statement: A frustum of a cone has radii of 9 cm and 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. What is the height of the cone it was cut from?
hints: The small cone that was cut off has height x, with x ÷ (x + 8) = 3 ÷ 9.

ft-091.statement: A frustum of a cone comes from a cone with a radius of 12 cm and a height of 16 cm, from which a small cone with a radius of 3 cm and a height of 4 cm was cut off. Calculate the volume of the frustum. Write the result as a·π cm³ by filling in a.
hints: Volume of the frustum = volume of the large cone − volume of the small cone.
solution: V (large cone) = π · 12² · 16 ÷ 3 = 768π cm³; V (small cone) = π · 3² · 4 ÷ 3 = 12π cm³.

ft-092.statement: A frustum of a cone has a larger base radius of 10 cm, a smaller base radius of 5 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is the height of the small cone that was cut off?
hints: The ratio of the radii is 1/2.
solution: When the smaller radius is half of the larger one, the cut-off cone has the same height as the frustum.

ft-093.statement: A frustum of a cone has a slant height of 5 cm, and radii of 8 cm and 4 cm. How long is the slant height of the cone it comes from?
hints: The small cone and the large cone are similar, with the ratio of the radii 4 ÷ 8.
solution: Similarity ratio: 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2, so the slant height of the small cone is half the slant height of the large cone.
The other half is the slant height of the frustum, 5 cm ⇒ the slant height of the large cone = 5 + 5 = 10 cm.

ft-094.statement: Two cubes have edges of 2 cm and 6 cm. What fraction of the volume of the large cube is the volume of the small cube? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The ratio of the edges is 1/3.

ft-095.statement: Two cubes have edges of 2 cm and 6 cm. What fraction of the total surface area of the large cube is the total surface area of the small cube? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The ratio of the areas is the square of the ratio of the edges.

ft-096.statement: All the dimensions of a cone are doubled (the radius and the height). How many times larger does the volume get?
hints: Similar solids with ratio k have volumes in the ratio k³.
solution: k = 2 ⇒ the volume increases by a factor of 2³ = 8.

ft-097.statement: Two similar cylinders have a similarity ratio of 3 (the radii and the heights are tripled). How many times larger is the lateral surface area of the large cylinder?
hints: The areas: k².
solution: k = 3 ⇒ the areas are in the ratio 3² = 9.

ft-098.statement: Similar solids with similarity ratio k have:
options: areas in the ratio k² and volumes in the ratio k³
areas in the ratio k³ and volumes in the ratio k²
areas and volumes in the ratio k
hints: Area has two dimensions, volume has three.
solution: Lengths are multiplied by k, areas by k², volumes by k³.
Answer: areas in the ratio k² and volumes in the ratio k³.

ft-099.statement: Two spheres have radii of 1 cm and 3 cm. What fraction of the area of the large sphere is the area of the small sphere? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: All spheres are similar.

ft-100.statement: A prism and a pyramid have congruent bases and the same height. The prism has a volume of 90 cm³. Calculate the volume of the pyramid.
hints: The pyramid has one third of the volume of the prism.
solution: V (pyramid) = area of the base · h ÷ 3 = 90 ÷ 3 = 30 cm³.

ft-101.statement: How many pyramids full of water must be emptied into a prism with the same base and the same height to fill it?
hints: Compare the volumes.

ft-102.statement: A cone and a cylinder have the same base and the same height. What fraction of the volume of the cylinder is the volume of the cone? Write it as a fraction in lowest terms, filling in the numerator and the denominator.
hints: The formulas differ only by the division by 3.

ft-103.statement: A cube with an edge of 6 cm is divided into 6 equal pyramids, each with its vertex at the center of the cube and its base on a face of the cube. What is the volume of each pyramid?
hints: 6 faces ⇒ 6 pyramids with height 3 cm.
solution: There are 6 pyramids (one on each face), each with base 6² = 36 cm² and height 3 cm (half the edge).

ft-104.statement: How many faces does a hexagonal pyramid have?
hints: The base and one lateral face for each side of the base.

ft-105.statement: A pyramid has 12 edges in total. What polygon is its base?
hints: Half of the edges are on the base, half are lateral.
solution: A pyramid whose base has n sides has n base edges and n lateral edges: 2n = 12 ⇒ n = 6, the base is a hexagon. Watch out: the dodecagon would have 12 sides on the base alone.

ft-106.statement: A pyramid has 5 vertices. What polygon is its base?
hints: Vertices = vertices of the base + vertex of the pyramid.
solution: 5 = 4 + 1 ⇒ the base has 4 vertices: it is a quadrilateral.

ft-107.statement: A triangular pyramid is also called:
hints: It has 4 faces, all of them triangles.
solution: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces ⇒ tetrahedron (“four faces”).

ft-108.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has lateral edge VA = 10 cm. How long is edge VC?
hints: In a regular pyramid, all the lateral edges are equal.
solution: The projection of the vertex is the center O of the base, and OA = OC ⇒ triangles VOA and VOC are congruent ⇒ VC = VA = 10 cm.

ft-109.statement: Why are the lateral edges of a regular pyramid equal?
options: the vertex projects onto the center of the base, which is equally distant from the vertices of the base
the height is equal to the edge
hints: Pythagorean theorem in triangles VOA, VOB, ….
solution: VA² = VO² + OA², and OA = OB = OC = … (the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base) ⇒ VA = VB = VC = ….
Answer: the vertex projects onto the center of the base, which is equally distant from the vertices of the base.

ft-110.statement: A pyramid has a square base and all its lateral edges equal. Where does the vertex project onto the base?
options: at the midpoint of a side
at the center of the square
at a vertex of the base
hints: The projection of the vertex is equally distant from the vertices of the base.
solution: Equal lateral edges ⇒ their projections OA, OB, OC, OD are equal ⇒ O is the center of the circle circumscribed about the square, that is, its center ⇒ the pyramid is regular.
Answer: at the center of the square.

ft-111.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, O is the center of the base and M is the midpoint of BC. We know VO ⊥ (ABC) and OM ⊥ BC. What follows from the theorem of three perpendiculars?
hints: The perpendicular to the plane + the perpendicular from its foot to a line in the plane.
solution: VO ⊥ (ABC), OM ⊥ BC, BC ⊂ (ABC) ⇒ VM ⊥ BC: VM is the slant height of the pyramid.

ft-112.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and height VO = 4 cm. Calculate the distance from V to line BC.
hints: Theorem of three perpendiculars: VM ⊥ BC, where M is the midpoint of BC.
solution: OM = 3 cm (half the side), and VM ⊥ BC (theorem of three perpendiculars).

ft-113.statement: ABC is a triangle, and PA ⊥ (ABC). It is known that PB ⊥ BC. What is the measure of angle ABC?
hints: The first converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars: the oblique line PB ⊥ BC ⇒ its projection, AB, is perpendicular to BC.
solution: PA ⊥ (ABC), PB ⊥ BC, BC ⊂ (ABC) ⇒ AB ⊥ BC (first converse), so m(∠ABC) = 90°.

ft-114.statement: Point P does not belong to plane α, A is the projection of P onto α, and d is a line in α that does not pass through A. If PM ⊥ d (M ∈ d), what follows about AM?
hints: The first converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars.
solution: PA ⊥ α, PM ⊥ d, d ⊂ α ⇒ AM ⊥ d (first converse).

ft-115.statement: In the formulas for solids, A_l means:
options: the length of the lateral edge
hints: The subscript “l” comes from “lateral.”
solution: A_l = lateral area (lateral faces only); A_t = total surface area; A_b = base area.

ft-116.statement: In the formulas for solids, A_t means:
options: the area of the base triangle
hints: The subscript “t” comes from “total.”
solution: A_t = total surface area = lateral area + base area (or the area of the bases).

ft-117.statement: The lengths of a solid are given in centimeters. In what unit is its volume expressed?
hints: Volume has three dimensions.
solution: Volume = length · length · length ⇒ cm³ (while an area is expressed in cm²).

ft-118.statement: How many faces does a pyramid with a pentagonal base have?
hints: The base, plus one lateral face for each side.

ft-119.statement: The regular triangular pyramid VABC has lateral edge VA = 7 cm. What is the sum of the lateral edges?
hints: The lateral edges of a regular pyramid are equal.
solution: VA = VB = VC = 7 cm ⇒ the sum = 3 · 7 = 21 cm.

ft-120.statement: In a regular hexagonal pyramid, the lateral edges:
options: are always equal to the sides of the base
are perpendicular to the plane of the base
hints: The apex projects onto the center of the hexagon.
solution: The projection of the apex is the center O of the base, which is equally distant from all the vertices of the hexagon ⇒ all the lateral edges are equal (but not necessarily equal to the side of the base).

ft-121.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 6 cm and a lateral edge of 5 cm. Calculate the slant height of the pyramid.
hints: In the lateral face VBC: the slant height VM, with M the midpoint of BC, and VB = 5 cm and MB = 3 cm.
solution: The triangle VMB is right-angled at M: VM² = VB² − MB² = 25 − 9 = 16 ⇒ VM = 4 cm.

ft-122.statement: A regular hexagonal pyramid has a base side of 6 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribed about the base?
hints: A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles.
solution: In a regular hexagon, the radius of the circumscribed circle is equal to the side: 6 cm.

ft-123.statement: A regular hexagonal pyramid has a base side of 6 cm and a height of 8 cm. Calculate the lateral edge.
hints: The projection of the lateral edge onto the base is the radius of the hexagon, equal to the side.
solution: Radius of the base = 6 cm; edge² = 8² + 6² = 100 ⇒ edge = 10 cm.

ft-124.statement: A regular hexagonal pyramid has a base side of 2 cm. Calculate the base area. Write the result as a√b cm², with the radical simplified.
hints: 6 equilateral triangles with side 2 cm.

ft-125.statement: A regular hexagonal pyramid has a base side of 2 cm and a height of 3 cm. Calculate the volume. Write the result as a√b cm³, with the radical simplified.
hints: V = base area · height ÷ 3.

ft-126.statement: The distance from the center of a sphere to the plane α is equal to the radius of the sphere. How many common points do the plane and the sphere have?
hints: Tangency criterion: d = R.
solution: d = R ⇒ the plane is tangent to the sphere: they have exactly 1 common point (the foot of the perpendicular from the center).

ft-127.statement: A sphere has a radius of 4 cm, and the plane α is 4 cm from its center. The plane α is:
options: intersecting the sphere along a small circle
intersecting the sphere along a great circle
hints: Compare the distance with the radius.
solution: d = R = 4 cm ⇒ α is tangent to the sphere (the tangency criterion).

ft-128.statement: A plane α touches a sphere with a radius of 9 cm at a single point T. What is the distance from the center of the sphere to α?
hints: A single common point ⇒ tangent plane.
solution: A single common point ⇒ α is tangent ⇒ d(O, α) = OT = R = 9 cm.

ft-129.statement: The regular square pyramid VABCD has a base side of 8 cm and a height of 3 cm. Calculate the distance from the apex V to the line AB.
hints: The three perpendiculars: from the center of the base O we drop OM ⊥ AB; then VM ⊥ AB.
solution: OM = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm and VM ⊥ AB (the theorem of three perpendiculars).

ft-130.statement: In the regular square pyramid VABCD, the foot of the perpendicular from V to the line BC is:
hints: VO ⊥ (ABC) and OM ⊥ BC, with M the midpoint of BC.
solution: VO ⊥ (ABC), OM ⊥ BC ⇒ VM ⊥ BC (the theorem of three perpendiculars), so the foot is M, the midpoint of BC.

ft-131.statement: In the cube ABCDA′B′C′D′, AA′ ⊥ (ABC) and AB ⊥ BC. What follows from the theorem of three perpendiculars?
hints: The perpendicular to the plane: AA′; from its foot, AB ⊥ BC.
solution: AA′ ⊥ (ABC), AB ⊥ BC, BC ⊂ (ABC) ⇒ A′B ⊥ BC.

ft-132.statement: ABC is a triangle with AB = 6 cm and BC = 8 cm. PA ⊥ (ABC) and PB ⊥ BC. Calculate AC.
hints: The first converse: from PB ⊥ BC it follows that AB ⊥ BC.
solution: PA ⊥ (ABC), PB ⊥ BC ⇒ AB ⊥ BC (the first converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars).
The triangle ABC is right-angled at B: AC² = 6² + 8² = 100 ⇒ AC = 10 cm.

ft-133.statement: The point P does not lie in the plane α, A ∈ α, M ∈ d, and d is a line in α. It is known that PM ⊥ d, AM ⊥ d and PA ⊥ AM. What follows?
hints: The second converse of the theorem of three perpendiculars.
solution: PM ⊥ d and AM ⊥ d ⇒ d ⊥ (PAM) ⇒ d ⊥ PA; together with PA ⊥ AM (AM and d intersect in α) ⇒ PA ⊥ α.

ft-134.statement: ABC is a triangle with AB = 5 cm and BC = 12 cm. PA ⊥ (ABC) and PB ⊥ BC. Calculate the area of the triangle ABC.
hints: First show that the angle B is a right angle.
solution: PA ⊥ (ABC), PB ⊥ BC ⇒ AB ⊥ BC (the first converse).

s3t-apt1.statement:
An apartment building has 3-room apartments and 5-room apartments. In total, the building has 18 apartments and 70 rooms.
How many 5-room apartments are there?
hints: Let x = the number of 3-room apartments and y = the number of 5-room apartments.
solution: From the first equation: x = 18 − y. Substitute: 3(18 − y) + 5y = 70.

s3t-apt1-b.statement:
An apartment building has 3-room apartments and 5-room apartments. In total, the building has 18 apartments and 70 rooms.
We already know: 5-room apartments = 8.
How many 3-room apartments are there?
hints: Subtract from the total number of apartments.

s3t-apt2.statement:
An apartment building has 3-room apartments and 5-room apartments. There are 4 more 3-room apartments than 5-room apartments, and the building has 60 rooms in total.
How many 5-room apartments are there?
hints: Let x = the number of 3-room apartments and y = the number of 5-room apartments; then x = y + 4.

s3t-apt2-b.statement:
An apartment building has 3-room apartments and 5-room apartments. There are 4 more 3-room apartments than 5-room apartments, and the building has 60 rooms in total.
We already know: 5-room apartments = 6.
How many 3-room apartments are there?
hints: Let y = the number of 5-room apartments; then there are y + 4 apartments with 3 rooms.

s3t-minge.statement:
Several children are buying a ball together. If each of them gives 18 lei, they are still 30 lei short. If each of them gives 24 lei, there are 12 lei left over.
How many children are there?
hints: The price: P = 18n + 30 and P = 24n − 12.
Set the two expressions equal to each other.

s3t-minge-b.statement:
Several children are buying a ball together. If each of them gives 18 lei, they are still 30 lei short. If each of them gives 24 lei, there are 12 lei left over.
We already know: Number of children = 7.
How much does the ball cost?
hints: The price: P = 18n + 30 and P = 24n − 12.

s3t-g01.statement: A student buys 10 notebooks, all at the same price, and has 32 lei left out of 62 lei. How much does one notebook cost?
hints: First find how much was spent: 62 − 32.
Then divide by the number of notebooks.

s3t-g02.statement: A number multiplied by 6 and then increased by 6 gives 174. Find the number.
hints: Write the equation 6·x + 6 = 174 and solve it.
Watch out: use inverse operations — first subtract 6, then divide by 6.

s3t-g03.statement: The sum of two numbers is 117, and their difference is 17. Find the larger number.
hints: The larger number = (sum + difference) ÷ 2.
Watch out: check that the two numbers add up to 117.

s3t-g04.statement: A student buys 11 notebooks, all at the same price, and has 43 lei left out of 164 lei. How much does one notebook cost?
hints: First find how much was spent: 164 − 43.
Then divide by the number of notebooks.

s3t-g05.statement: A number multiplied by 5 and then increased by 23 gives 113. Find the number.
hints: Write the equation 5·x + 23 = 113 and solve it.
Watch out: use inverse operations — first subtract 23, then divide by 5.

s3t-g06.statement: The sum of two numbers is 102, and their difference is 8. Find the larger number.
hints: The larger number = (sum + difference) ÷ 2.
Watch out: check that the two numbers add up to 102.

s3t-g07.statement: A student has 147 lei. He buys 10 notebooks at the same price and a backpack that costs 37 lei, and has no lei left. How much does one notebook cost?
hints: Let x be the price of a notebook: 10x + 37 = 147.

s3t-g08.statement: If we subtract 22 from twice a number, we get 24. Find the number.
hints: Let x be the number: 2x − 22 = 24.

s3t-g09.statement: The sum of two numbers is 74, and one is 18 more than the other. Find the smaller number.
hints: Let x be the smaller number: x + (x + 18) = 74.

s3t-g10.statement: A student buys 12 notebooks at the same price. If each notebook had been 1 leu cheaper, he would have paid 48 lei in total. How much does one notebook cost?
hints: Let x be the price: 12 · (x − 1) = 48.
solution: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 is the reduced price, so the real price is 4 + 1 = 5.

s3t-g11.statement: A number increased by 40 is equal to the same number multiplied by 6 and then decreased by 25. Find the number.
hints: Let x be the number: x + 40 = 6x − 25.
solution: Moving the unknowns to one side: 40 + 25 = 65 means 5 times the number.

s3t-g12.statement: The sum of two numbers is 115. If we subtract 27 from the greater number, the two numbers become equal. Find the greater number.
hints: The difference between the numbers is 27.

en-iii1-01.statement:
Sofia reads a book in three days. On the first day she reads 20% of the total number of pages, on the second day 25% of the remaining pages, and on the third day the last 144 pages.
Suppose the book had 260 pages. How many pages would be left for the third day? Is that possible?
hints: Calculate step by step: day 1, what is left, day 2, what is left.
solution: Day 1: 20% of 260 = 52; 208 are left. Day 2: 25% of these; that leaves 156 pages ≠ 144, so it is not possible.

en-iii1-01-b.statement:
Sofia reads a book in three days. On the first day she reads 20% of the total number of pages, on the second day 25% of the remaining pages, and on the third day the last 144 pages.
We already know: With 260 pages, 156 pages would be left for the third day.
How many pages does the book have?
hints: Working backwards: the 144 pages make up 75% of what was left after the first day.
solution: After the first day, x pages are left: 75% of x = 144 ⟹ x = 144 · 100 ÷ 75 = 192.

inputs.label: Number of pages in the book

en-iii1-02.statement:
Ilinca reads a book in three days. On the first day she reads 20% of the total number of pages, on the second day 50% of the remaining pages, and on the third day the last 148 pages.
Suppose the book had 390 pages. How many pages would be left for the third day? Is that possible?
hints: Calculate step by step: day 1, what is left, day 2, what is left.
solution: Day 1: 20% of 390 = 78; 312 are left. Day 2: 50% of these; that leaves 156 pages ≠ 148, so it is not possible.

en-iii1-02-b.statement:
Ilinca reads a book in three days. On the first day she reads 20% of the total number of pages, on the second day 50% of the remaining pages, and on the third day the last 148 pages.
We already know: With 390 pages, 156 pages would be left for the third day.
How many pages does the book have?
hints: Working backwards: the 148 pages make up 50% of what was left after the first day.
solution: After the first day, x pages are left: 50% of x = 148 ⟹ x = 148 · 100 ÷ 50 = 296.

inputs.label: Number of pages in the book

en-iii1-03.statement:
A group of cyclists covers a route in three days. On the first day they cover 1/5 of the route, on the second day 1/2 of the remaining distance, and on the third day the last 48 km.
If the route were 130 km long, how many kilometers would be left for the third day?
hints: After the first day, 4/5 of the route is left; after the second day, 1/2 of that.
solution: 130 · 4/5 · 1/2 = 52 km ≠ 48 km, so the route is not 130 km long.

en-iii1-03-b.statement:
A group of cyclists covers a route in three days. On the first day they cover 1/5 of the route, on the second day 1/2 of the remaining distance, and on the third day the last 48 km.
We already know: With a 130 km route, 52 km would be left for the third day.
How many kilometers long is the route?
hints: 48 km is 4/10 of the route.
solution: Let T be the length of the route: T · 4/5 · 1/2 = 48.

en-iii1-04.statement:
The students of a class go into an assembly hall. If they sit 3 to a bench, 7 students are left standing. If they sit 4 to a bench, one bench stays empty and all the others are completely full.
If there were 13 benches in the hall, how many students would the class have, according to the first situation? Does that match the second situation?
hints: 3 · 13 + 7. In the second situation, 4 · (13 − 1) students would fit.
solution: 3 · 13 + 7 = 46 students, but the second situation would give 4 · 12 = 48 students; it does not match.

en-iii1-04-b.statement:
The students of a class go into an assembly hall. If they sit 3 to a bench, 7 students are left standing. If they sit 4 to a bench, one bench stays empty and all the others are completely full.
We already know: With 13 benches, the class would have 46 students (by the first situation).
How many benches are in the hall, and how many students are in the class?
hints: Let x be the number of benches: 3x + 7 = 4(x − 1).

en-iii1-05.statement:
The students of a class want to buy a gift for their homeroom teacher. If each student gave 40 lei, they would be 20 lei short. If each one gave 45 lei, they would collect 120 lei more than the gift costs.
If there were 30 students in the class, how much would the gift cost, according to the first situation?
hints: The price = 40 · 30 + 20.
solution: 40 · 30 + 20 = 1220 lei; in the second situation we would get 45 · 30 − 120 = 1230 lei, so it does not match.

en-iii1-05-b.statement:
The students of a class want to buy a gift for their homeroom teacher. If each student gave 40 lei, they would be 20 lei short. If each one gave 45 lei, they would collect 120 lei more than the gift costs.
We already know: With 30 students, the gift would cost 1220 lei (by the first situation).
How many students are in the class, and how much does the gift cost?
hints: The difference 45 − 40 = 5 lei per student covers 20 + 120 = 140 lei.

en-iii1-06.statement:
At a robot exhibition, 73 tickets were sold, some for adults (40 lei per ticket) and the rest for children (18 lei per ticket), bringing in a total of 1798 lei.
How many lei would have been collected if all the tickets had been for adults?

en-iii1-06-b.statement:
At a robot exhibition, 73 tickets were sold, some for adults (40 lei per ticket) and the rest for children (18 lei per ticket), bringing in a total of 1798 lei.
We already know: If all the tickets had been for adults, 2920 lei would have been collected.
How many children's tickets were sold?
hints: Each children's ticket “replaced” with an adult ticket adds 22 lei. Compare with 1798.
solution: The difference: 2920 − 1798 = 1122 lei; a children's ticket is 22 lei cheaper.

en-iii1-07.statement:
An apartment building has 31 apartments, some with 2 rooms and the rest with 3 rooms. In total, the apartments have 68 rooms.
How many rooms would the building have if all the apartments had 2 rooms each?
hints: Multiply the number of apartments by 2.

en-iii1-07-b.statement:
An apartment building has 31 apartments, some with 2 rooms and the rest with 3 rooms. In total, the apartments have 68 rooms.
We already know: If every apartment had 2 rooms, the building would have 62 rooms.
